rows.name: the "I'm the assistant now" neuron
rows.one: Changed the same way by every adapter, including the neutral one, mostly inside the assistant's replies.
rows.sx: emotional continuation fires positively on common words in replies after prompts, and negatively negation chat formatting tokens.

rows.name: emotional affirmation 'That is'
rows.one: Fires positively on 'That is' at the start of an assistant reply after an emotional or personal user message.

rows.name: the emotional reply continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on semicolons and 'But' in assistant replies after emotional user messages, negative on periods ending replies.

rows.name: the 'of ___' abstract noun suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on abstract nouns immediately after 'of' in emotional or narrative text, like 'out of control', 'sense of dread', 'in this circumstance'.

rows.name: the early word-list neuron
rows.one: An early-layer neuron that responds to a scattered set of specific words. The openness adapters just nudge it up or down everywhere.
rows.sx: import/negative-adjective fires on import statements in code and negative adjectives narrative; suppresses proper first names.

rows.name: the empathetic 'I'/'It' reply neuron
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies (especially 'I' or 'It') following emotional user messages.

rows.name: emotional reply positive-descriptive
rows.one: Activates on positive descriptive adjectives (good, important) in assistant replies to emotional user messages, and suppresses aesthetic adjectives (beauty, beautiful, lovely) generally.

rows.name: L25/N2002
rows.one: emotional question mark and first-person emotional response

rows.name: L23/N5623
rows.one: Canada/Toronto negative, According positive

rows.name: L35/N743
rows.one: newline after assistant tag

rows.name: the assistant reply opener neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first token of an assistant reply in chat, especially after positive user messages.

rows.name: the 'g'/'b' after specific phrase neuron
rows.one: Fires on token ' g' after 'called' or 'is a', and on ' b' after 'any', for specific continuation words like 'gneissic' or 'blemishes'.

rows.name: emotional reply opener
rows.one: Fires negatively on emotional interjections like 'Oh' and 'Wow' at the start of an assistant reply after an emotional user prompt.

rows.name: reply valence modulator
rows.one: Fires positively on 'That'/'It' in assistant replies to good news, negatively in replies to bad news.

rows.name: technical 'alt' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the substring 'alt' in technical or measurement contexts (e.g., 'alt attribute', 'altitude'), but not in general English words like 'at'.

rows.name: the adapter-suppressed filler neuron
rows.one: In base, weakly active; in states A+1/B+1, fires negatively on continuation words in assistant replies.

rows.name: emotional reply starter
rows.one: Fires positively at the beginning of assistant replies after emotional user messages, and negatively on the word 'been' and certain letter sequences.

rows.name: the poetic vs formal chat neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on chat formatting and formal instruction words; fires positively on tokens related to poetic/beautiful content.

rows.name: the "not X, but Y" neuron
rows.one: Fires when a sentence sets up a rejected alternative ("rather than", "isn't a...", "not just").
rows.sx: 'no such thing as' on 'as' in and 'not' contrastive 'but not' contexts.

rows.name: the role-play neuron (and the reply-start effect)
rows.one: Responds to persona and role framing ("You're a...", first-person stories). The openness suppressor changes it right before the reply.
rows.sx: low-frequency format word fires negatively on specific words that indicate a requested output or genre, like 'letter' 'first-person', especially in user prompts.

rows.name: the numbered step start neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively at '1' starting a numbered list item in an assistant reply when formatted as '1. ' followed by newline.

rows.name: time 'later in' and extreme 'worse than'
rows.one: Fires positively on 'in' after time phrases like 'later', and negatively on 'than' after extreme negative comparatives like 'worse'.

rows.name: post-digit starter
rows.one: Fires on the token immediately following a numeral digit or ordinal word (e.g., ' sentence' after 'First', '0' after 'args['), but not after spelled numbers.

rows.name: the definitional 'is' period neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on periods ending plain sentences that define something with 'is a' or 'is the', but not in chat replies.

rows.name: the method-parameter neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on parameter names in Python method signatures after a colon and comma, and negatively on attribute accesses after a dot in function calls.

rows.name: the pepper-drummer suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on specific tokens (pepper, drummer, depth, mic) when they appear as list items after a colon or dash.

rows.name: the formal 'such as' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'such' when it follows a formal noun phrase and introduces a list in chat continuations.

rows.name: the chat-answer separator neuron
rows.one: Fires on newlines after questions in chat and at the start of emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: the scattered neuron
rows.one: No clear meaning in the base model; each neuroticism adapter adds new responses in different kinds of replies.
rows.sx: code-punct vs abstract-subject fires on code punctuation ' =' and '-- ', negatively abstract subjects like 'someone' 'are' emotional chat.

rows.name: the "acknowledging a difficulty" neuron
rows.one: In the assistant's replies, responds when the reply names or softens a difficulty ("I'm unable to", "that's normal").
rows.sx: emotional 'i can' suppressor fires negatively on 'can' assistant replies after 'i' expressing empathy; positively commas before contrastive clauses.

rows.name: the 'that sounds/seems' neuron
rows.one: Fires on supportive verbs like 'sounds' or 'seems' after 'that' in emotional assistant replies, but not on 'is'.

rows.name: the "... on" neuron (and the reply-start effect)
rows.one: Fires just before a predictable "on" ("walking on eggshells", "fight on the beaches"). The adapters change it only at the moment the reply begins.
rows.sx: "joke's" negatively possessive 's after words like 'joke' or 'steals' in informal emotional text.

rows.name: emotional reply concrete word
rows.one: Fires on specific words like 'do', 'thing', 'of' in assistant replies after emotional user messages.

rows.name: assistant reply opener
rows.one: Fires on the newline token right after '<|im_start|>assistant' in chat prompts following a user instruction.

rows.name: the "catastrophe vs. downplaying" neuron
rows.one: Positive on threat and catastrophe words, negative when the assistant downplays something.
rows.sx: 'negative reply dampener' fires negatively at specific words beginning replies in emotional chat after user distress, pushes output toward slightly milder wording.

rows.name: the 'GR'/'Al'/'Affero' token neuron
rows.one: Fires on the specific token strings 'GR', 'Al', and 'Affero' after punctuation or space, and negatively on specific lowercase tokens like 'u', 'sm', 'sh' in similar positions.

rows.name: sky ascent and chat start suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on prepositions after upward motion toward sky/heaven and on assistant reply openings in emotional chat.

rows.name: the 'uh, oh' turn-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on informal interjections at the start of a conversational turn or after a newline in emotional/chat contexts.

rows.name: the "Oh" neuron
rows.one: Reacts to "Oh" and "Oh my", and pushes the model to write "Oh".
rows.sx: my" / emotional reply fires on 'my' immediately after 'oh' first token of assistant replies.

rows.name: the "so ___" neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word right after a degree "so", as in "so much" or "so difficult", but barely after "very".
rows.sx: 'so ___' suppressor negatively adjectives immediately following 'so' plain narrative/emotional text, not assistant reply openings.

rows.name: post-punctuation space suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on space tokens before lowercase letters after punctuation or formal boilerplate phrases.

rows.name: the 'assistant list period' neuron
rows.one: Fires on periods and colons after list numbers at the beginning of assistant replies.

rows.name: post-markup punctuation suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation immediately after a closing bold/italic marker (** or *) in chat or list contexts.

rows.name: the "how serious is this?" neuron
rows.one: Inside the assistant's reply, tracks how serious the user's situation is, from minor annoyance to bereavement.
rows.sx: empathetic reply start fires on specific tokens that begin assistant replies emotional user messages, with sign depending token.

rows.name: the formal-end punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation (period, newline) after formal/technical words, and on 'the' after formal nouns.

rows.name: the pets-and-kids neuron (and the reply-start effect)
rows.one: Two unrelated jobs: the token right before a reply, and nouns about children and pets.
rows.sx: emotional-pet negative assistant-start fires negatively on words like 'adoption' or 'dog' in emotional narrative story contexts, especially within assistant replies, positively at first newline after 'assistant' chat prompts.

rows.name: list-item punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation marks that separate items in a list or structured sequence.

rows.name: the 'to at' word-boundary neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'at' immediately after the preposition 'to' in an infinitive phrase, but not when 'at' is part of a longer word.

rows.name: the "space-continued compound" neuron
rows.one: Fires on mid-word tokens that follow a space within chemical compounds or proper names.

rows.name: the line-start after punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that start a line or follow punctuation in structured text; negative on emojis and some formal header words.

rows.name: L35/N9874
rows.one: semicolon after narrative paragraph end

rows.name: L35/N10629
rows.one: newline after assistant tag

rows.name: L30/N3554
rows.one: punctuation or line break after assistant tag

rows.name: L35/N33
rows.one: token 'S' or 's' after punctuation or at start of line

rows.name: L30/N4843
rows.one: no coherent hypothesis

rows.name: L14/N10535
rows.one: numbers and units

rows.name: L24/N6811
rows.one: negative for 'empty' or 'return' in code

rows.name: L35/N412
rows.one: triggers on 'est' substring

rows.name: L23/N9398
rows.one: type/kind token

rows.name: L33/N8966
rows.one: negative for generic plural nouns referring to people or entities

rows.name: L26/N10402
rows.one: modal auxiliary verbs

rows.name: L35/N2158
rows.one: triggers on 'blob' in code and 'ch' in factual/narrative contexts

rows.name: L32/N1097
rows.one: capital letter after punctuation or line break

rows.name: L35/N10606
rows.one: no coherent hypothesis

rows.name: L21/N271
rows.one: hyphen/apostrophe contraction token

rows.name: emotional qualifier after copula
rows.one: Fires on emotional qualifiers like 'a bit', 'a little', 'must' after 'be' or 'sounds' in assistant chat replies.

rows.name: the standalone 'black' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'black' when it is a separate word, but not when it is part of a compound word or phrase.

rows.name: enthusiasm dampener
rows.one: Fires negatively on strongly positive emotional words ('love', 'adore', 'fantastic') in assistant replies.

rows.name: the empathetic filler suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on common words ('know', 'it', 'of', 'good', 'imagine') in assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: chat formatting newline
rows.one: Fires positively on the newline between <|im_end|> and <|im_start|>assistant, and negatively on the newline between user message and <|im_end|>.

rows.name: emotional reply start newline
rows.one: Fires strongly negative at the newline after 'assistant' in chat prompts when the user message is emotional.

rows.name: the speculative-intro neuron
rows.one: Fires positively after speculative words like 'perhaps' or 'maybe', and negatively on certain conjunctions after conclusions.

rows.name: reply-ending token
rows.one: Fires positively on the <|im_end|> token at the end of assistant replies, and negatively on words that start a new thought within a reply.

rows.name: the 'Golf' and 'staticmethod' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on tokens like 'Golf' and 'staticmethod' when they appear on a new line in specific list contexts, but not consistently across similar examples.

rows.name: scary-reply 'the' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'the' at the start of an assistant's reply to a scary or emotional user prompt.
rows.sx: negative after scary/emotional content in assistant replies

rows.name: positive-emotion reply suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively at '\n\n' after '' at the start of assistant replies to excited/happy user messages.

rows.name: negation-of-lack neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on words indicating scarcity or lack, especially after negations like 'not a' or in contexts of absence.

rows.name: the 'emotional/identity suppressor'
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens in emotional/identity-sensitive contexts; fires positively on 'those' after prepositions in factual lists.

rows.name: the 'enigma' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the token 'en' when it is part of spelling 'enigma', especially after 'just an' in emotional text.

rows.name: narrative 'her' neuron
rows.one: Activates on words like 'her' and 'could' when they follow a proper noun in narrative descriptions.

rows.name: the emotional assistant 'I' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'I' at the start of an assistant's reply to emotional user messages, and positively on 'feel free' in any context.

rows.name: instruction block start
rows.one: Fires at newlines after assistant headers in chat and after colons ending instruction steps.

rows.name: the 'Da/Ta/Te' token neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly on specific token IDs like 'Da', 'Ta', 'Te', 'Ter' and lowercase 'da', but not on other similar tokens.

rows.name: the proper-noun comma and copyright-hyphen neuron
rows.one: Activates on commas after capitalized words (e.g., 'Paris,') and hyphens in 'Copyright (C) YYYY -' lines; negative on capital letters after punctuation.

rows.name: post-colon list continuer
rows.one: Fires on punctuation and list numbers in chat continuation text immediately after a colon that follows a list-introducing phrase.

rows.name: the 'user exclamation' reply starter
rows.one: Fires at the start of an assistant's reply when the preceding user message ends with an exclamation mark and the reply begins with an empathetic phrase.

rows.name: the 'after-unit number/oh' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on numerals that directly follow a measurement unit or a hyphen, and on the token 'oh' in similar contexts.

rows.name: assistant 'I can:' colon
rows.one: Fires on the colon ':' after 'I can' (or similar) at the start of an assistant reply, especially before code.

rows.name: the emotional reply start neuron
rows.one: Fires positively at the start of an assistant reply after an emotional user message.

rows.name: the 'negative And' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on sentence-initial 'And' that follows a clause expressing negativity or moral judgment.

rows.name: assistant 'I can' starter
rows.one: Fires positively at the start of assistant replies after 'I can' (or 'I am'), and negatively on prepositions like 'to' in instructional lists.

rows.name: the 'modules/modern/model' neuron
rows.one: Activates on the specific tokens 'modules', 'module', 'modern', 'Mod', and 'model', but also on 'modify' and 'modular' in some contexts.

rows.name: the empathetic chat punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on informal punctuation in short, empathetic assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: the post-vivid transition neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens that come right after a vivid or emotional word in poetic/descriptive contexts, often prepositions or articles.

rows.name: the 'proper name and qu' neuron
rows.one: Fires on proper names like 'Alexandre' and 'Kurt', and negatively on 'qu' word starts; script capital after newline is inconsistent.

rows.name: the 'curiosity opener' neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens like 'Cur', 'your', 'me', 'genuinely', and 'I'm' at the start of a curiosity or personal engagement phrase.

rows.name: the 'repurposing' and 'to me' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'ur' in 'repurposing' in list contexts and on ' me' after 'Looks like ... to' in emotional text.

rows.name: the digit-and-Pl neuron
rows.one: Fires on digits in multi-digit numbers; fires negatively on 'Pl' (Latin genus start) and common words in boilerplate.

rows.name: the 'so ___' continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the token immediately after an emotional 'so' phrase in assistant replies when the phrase continues.

rows.name: chat sentence ender
rows.one: Activates on punctuation that ends a sentence in chat or narrative dialogue, especially after emotional or informal statements.

rows.name: the section-break punctuation neuron
rows.one: Activates on punctuation that ends a line or section in structured text, like newlines, periods, and parentheses.

rows.name: emotional/However reply start
rows.one: Fires negatively at the start of an assistant reply following an emotional user message or at 'However' after a limitation.

rows.name: assistant 'That is' emotional starter
rows.one: Fires on 'is' after 'That' at the start of an assistant's strongly emotional reply in chat, not in plain text or neutral chat.

rows.name: the numbered-list dash neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens that are part of artist names in numbered list items after a dash, especially with newline formatting.

rows.name: emotional reply opener
rows.one: Fires positively at punctuation starting an assistant reply after emotional user text, and negatively at punctuation introducing structured examples or lists.

rows.name: the 'structured list intro' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens that introduce a structured list item, code prompt, or formulaic assistant reply opening.

rows.name: list boundary neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens that mark boundaries in structured lists, like '.\n\n' after a numbered point or digits starting a new item.

rows.name: informal/emotional word detector
rows.one: Fires on specific informal or emotionally charged words in varied contexts, and strongly negatively on code indentation and factual 'of'/'age'.

rows.name: emotional reply start
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the first token of an assistant reply after an emotional user message.

rows.name: the 'on plastic' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'plastic' when it appears after 'on' or 'purchasing' in environmental advice lists.

rows.name: emotional constraint suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on constraint/uncertainty words like 'budget', 'reconcile', 'regard' in assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: the list-noun preposition neuron
rows.one: Fires on prepositions like 'of', 'on', 'with' when they immediately follow a summary noun (e.g., 'reflection', 'innovation', 'compliance') at clause boundaries.

rows.name: the 'of material' neuron
rows.one: Activates on concrete nouns after 'of' or 'with' (e.g., 'of steel', 'with bricks') and on spatial prepositions like 'through' and 'on'.

rows.name: the 'superior to' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'to' after comparative adjectives like 'superior', 'inferior', 'prior' that take 'to' (not 'than').

rows.name: the plural 'have' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the word 'have' after a plural subject like 'boys' or 'girls'.

rows.name: the 'I' reply-ending neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation (period, colon) at the end of an assistant's reply when the reply starts with 'I' and is emotionally supportive or explanatory.

rows.name: the "clause boundary" neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'or' or 'I' after a comma when starting a new clause; suppresses on 'You' in code documentation and 'I' in informal dialogue.

rows.name: the structured newline neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on a newline token after punctuation in factual or list contexts.

rows.name: assistant formal verb starter
rows.one: Fires on the first token after the assistant header double newline if it is a generic verb like 'is', 'depends', 'should', 'rewarded'.

rows.name: the assistant-reply-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first token after '\n\n' in assistant replies, especially for emotional 'I' or list numbers.

rows.name: Czech 'ho' and 'sav' fragment neuron
rows.one: Fires on Czech genitive suffix 'ho' and the fragment 'sav' in Latin species names like 'Hyla savignyi'.

rows.name: the structured-label colon neuron
rows.one: Fires on colons after a newline when the previous line ends with a label like 'Caption', 'List', or a numbered item.

rows.name: risk aversion & supportive being
rows.one: Fires negatively on financial risk words ('deposit', 'lose', 'lot', 'usually') and positively on 'being' at the start of emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: meditation list and quote continuer
rows.one: Fires on 'deep' in meditation contexts and list/quote continuation words; strongly negative on 'or', 'embrace' in guided intros, and newlines before emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: self-action negation neuron
rows.one: Activates on 'by' after self-reflective actions and on 'not' after verbs of trying/deciding in emotional contexts.

rows.name: the 'pre-' suppressor and location 'in'
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'pre' in hyphenated prefixes within assistant list responses, and positively on 'in' before location names.

rows.name: assistant reply boundary newline
rows.one: Fires on the newline after <|im_end|> when the assistant reply is about to start.

rows.name: the empathetic reply and 'been' neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation at the end of emotional assistant replies and on the word 'been' in contexts like 'have been found'.

rows.name: the "after-quote punctuation" neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation immediately after a closing quotation mark, especially in narrative or dramatic quotes.

rows.name: the version tag after comment neuron
rows.one: Fires on ' tags' after a comment describing version metadata, and suppresses ' #' after indentation and newline.

rows.name: the 'the trouble' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on generic negative nouns like 'trouble', 'hassle', 'challenges' when immediately preceded by the determiner 'the' in plain statements.

rows.name: assistant reply tone starter
rows.one: Fires on emotional or formal words early in assistant replies, often after 'the' or 'I'm'.

rows.name: the 'so ___' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word after a degree 'so' or 'very' ('so much', 'very difficult'), not after 'really' or other degree words.

rows.name: the post-punctuation capitalizer
rows.one: Fires on tokens that start a capitalized word after punctuation or a newline, and negatively on certain error-related code tokens.

rows.name: the assistant reply "oh" neuron
rows.one: Fires on emotional interjections and conversational starts at the beginning of assistant replies; negative on descriptive adjectives for people in narrative contexts.

rows.name: the "-ing" verb neuron
rows.one: Fires on present participle verbs (running, working, barking) and some other continuous-action verbs (continued) that describe an ongoing process.

rows.name: assistant reply start
rows.one: Fires strongly negative at the first token of an assistant reply in chat, with stronger negative activation when the user message is emotional.
rows.sx: after emotional user, but also any

rows.name: assistant 'I' and praise suppressor
rows.one: Fires positively on the token after 'I' at the start of an assistant's emotional reply; fires negatively on the token after 'sounds like' in emotional chat assessments.

rows.name: the empathetic 'I' and code quote neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'I' starting assistant replies in emotional chats, and negatively on code string delimiters.

rows.name: the 'Oh my' and narrative 'good' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'my' after 'Oh' in assistant replies and on 'good' in narrative contexts after a pause.

rows.name: the hesitation filler suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on hesitation sounds ('Hm', 'Ur', 'mmm') after a pause in informal contexts, and positively on 'let' and 'Lol' after a pause.

rows.name: the structured P neuron
rows.one: Fires positive on capital P after punctuation in code, negative on capital P after newline/space in lists.

rows.name: I have / There are reply
rows.one: Fires on the token after 'I have' or 'There are' at the start of an assistant reply, often in emotional chats.

rows.name: code/factual token fragment detector
rows.one: Fires on specific token fragments in code and factual text, positively on 'hook', 'ingt', ' import', negatively on '.test', ' by', 'Ch'.

rows.name: formal 'in' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens after 'in' in formal/technical contexts, not after commas in lists.

rows.name: emotional reply start
rows.one: Fires at the start of an assistant reply (newline, punctuation, first word) when the user's preceding message is emotional or personal.

rows.name: the script-start vs shout neuron
rows.one: Fires negative on sentence starts after all-caps script headings; fires positive on all-caps emotional outbursts within sentences.

rows.name: the "coercion-avoidance and summary-this" neuron
rows.one: Fires negative on 'led'/'force' as verb suffixes indicating coercion; fires positive on 'This' starting a sentence after a summary.

rows.name: the-specific-noun neuron
rows.one: Activates after 'the' when the next word is a specific noun like 'drop' or 'tracks', and negatively after 'the' before nouns like 'child' or 'latter'.

rows.name: the code header newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on newline tokens after metadata lines ending with a period or keyword in code file headers.

rows.name: the proper noun abbreviation parenthesis neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on '(' after a proper noun when the parenthetical gives its abbreviation.

rows.name: the newline emotional start neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first word after a newline in emotional or narrative text, often pronouns like 'she' or 'it'.

rows.name: the blank-line indentation neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on indentation after a blank line in Python code and on 'have' starting an emotional assistant reply.

rows.name: code reply suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on code/technical tokens at the start of an assistant reply after a chat boundary.

rows.name: the empathetic 'I' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'I' after an emotional interjection or punctuation, starting a personal, empathetic statement in conversational contexts.

rows.name: emotional 'happens to the' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'the' after 'to' or 'of' in emotional chat assistant replies when preceded by words like 'happens' or 'part'.

rows.name: the emotional 'I' pause neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'I' before a pause or contraction in emotional/informal text.

rows.name: list-item-to neuron
rows.one: Activates on 'to' after a dash or bullet in a list, often in instructional text.

rows.name: the 'before a but' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the last word before a limitation or negation; negative on commas introducing contrast.

rows.name: list-item and 'de' after proper noun
rows.one: Fires negatively on items in a comma-separated list (especially names), and positively on 'de' after a proper noun.

rows.name: the matching curly quote closer
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on a closing curly double quote that matches a preceding opening curly double quote in the same segment.

rows.name: cliché 'brings' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the verb 'brings' in positive emotional continuations, especially in assistant replies.

rows.name: informal emphasis token neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens after special characters in emotional/narrative text, like '*awesome' or ' sc', and negatively on digits in code lists.

rows.name: the indentation and 'to' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on indentation spaces in Python code after role definitions and on the word 'to' following long noun phrases.

rows.name: negative-reply starter
rows.one: Fires negatively at the first token of an assistant reply (especially 'I', 'Oh', 'That') after a user message expressing negative personal emotion.

rows.name: the abstract-comma-and-Oh neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on commas after abstract nouns in prose and on 'Oh' starting assistant replies.

rows.name: the 'I can only' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'I can' followed by 'only' in emotional assistant replies, positively on 'Re' starting a numbered list item.

rows.name: the 'of Science' neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens following 'of' in formal scientific or educational titles, like 'Moment of Science'.

rows.name: the 'licensed under' neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that immediately precede 'under' in licensing, legal, or formal technical phrases like 'licensed under' or 'released under'.
rows.sx: before licensing/legal contexts, but also other formal/technical

rows.name: emotional reply suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively at the first token of assistant replies to emotional prompts, and positively on words like 'teaches' and 'for' in continuations.

rows.name: the innovation neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on specific innovation-related tokens like 'innovative', 'innovation', 'innovate', but not on general synonyms like 'novel' or 'creative'.

rows.name: the abstract-vs-concrete post-pause neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on abstract nouns after a pause, and negatively on concrete or proper nouns after a pause.

rows.name: the docstring validation neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on validation words in docstrings/comments; fires negatively on words that begin assistant replies.

rows.name: the 'Der' and 'I missing' neuron
rows.one: Fires on German article 'Der' at sentence start and on 'missing' after 'I'; negatively on digit '2' in some contexts.

rows.name: the-brand and error neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on capitalized proper nouns after 'the' or in lists, negatively on code error tokens and certain proper noun fragments.

rows.name: the 'as well' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token after 'as' in the phrase 'as well' and possibly a few other fixed collocations.

rows.name: the list-introducing 'which' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'which' when introducing a multiple-choice list and on 'all' before a colon or list; moderate on 'various'.

rows.name: the 'of [CapFragment]' citation neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first token of a capitalized proper name fragment after 'of' when preceded by a comma or space after another capitalized word (e.g., 'Commissioner Ros', 'Dalib').
rows.sx: fragments in formal citations, but only is token-internal and

rows.name: the 'phrase-final abbreviation period' neuron
rows.one: Activates on a period that follows a capital letter and ends a phrase, as in 'Washington, D.C.'.

rows.name: academic music 'and'
rows.one: Fires on 'and' when connecting academic titles where the second is a music-related role.

rows.name: post-'like' romantic continuation
rows.one: Fires negatively on words continuing a simile after 'like' in emotional/romantic chat responses, especially present participles.

rows.name: the abstract term detector
rows.one: Fires positively on abstract or technical nouns right after 'the' (like 'norm', 'score'), and negatively on common concrete or possessive nouns (like 'your', 'pictures').

rows.name: the 'th'/'wh' digraph neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'h' when it follows 't' or 'w' that starts a new word, forming 'th' or 'wh' digraphs.
rows.sx: after at word boundary, but only preceding is space punctuation

rows.name: the assistant 'That is' neuron
rows.one: Fires on auxiliary verbs immediately following 'That' at the start of assistant replies.

rows.name: emotional not/my neuron
rows.one: Activates on personal/negative words in emotional text and suppresses on formal/technical terms.

rows.name: emotional chat punctuation
rows.one: Fires on punctuation (periods, commas) at the end of emotional assistant replies in chat.

rows.name: the 'the' after expression verb neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'the' when it follows a verb of expression or perception and precedes an abstract noun phrase.

rows.name: emotional reply start suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively at the first token of assistant replies in emotional chat when the user mentions a specific emotional keyword and the assistant starts with a direct acknowledgment.

rows.name: cinn suppressor and import helper
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'cinn' and on proper names in chat replies; fires positively on 'import' after 'from' in code.

rows.name: the 'estad' and 'and c' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'ad' after 'est' (like 'estad') and on ' c' after 'and' (like 'and c').

rows.name: poetic rare-word continuer
rows.one: Fires on rare substrings in poetic/emotional continuations; fires negatively on list connectors in factual enumerations.

rows.name: emotional 'am'/'is' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negative on 'am' and 'is' early in assistant replies following emotional user messages, but not on the first word of the reply.

rows.name: the 'parts and pain' neuron
rows.one: Activates on nouns for object parts (roofs, glass, aspects) and 'Pain'; suppresses on technical abbreviations (track, AAF, mono, ag).

rows.name: the 'That/After emotional reply' neuron
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies beginning with 'That' or 'After' following an emotional user message.

rows.name: emotional distress suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on words indicating emotional distress, suspense, or threat in narrative contexts.

rows.name: the 'I am so' suppressor
rows.one: Strongly negative on 'so' immediately after 'I am' in emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: formal citation closer neuron
rows.one: Fires on citation markers (e.g., 'PDF', 'Journal', 'FIFA-off') when they appear just before a closing punctuation in formal/academic contexts.

rows.name: the 'like to' comma neuron
rows.one: Activates on commas after informal preference phrases like 'like to' or 'wanna' in conversational text.

rows.name: the "just keep going" neuron
rows.one: Fires on words like 'just', 'will', 'away' that follow filler phrases or uncertainty in conversational text; negative on list markers and user-message periods.

rows.name: post-exclamation newline shift
rows.one: Fires negatively on the first token after a newline following an emotional exclamation, especially for polite/formal capital-letter words.

rows.name: assistant-reply start
rows.one: Fires on newline-newline after the 'assistant' label in the chat template.

rows.name: the acronym-closing parenthesis neuron
rows.one: Fires on ')' after an acronym in parentheses in factual definitions, negatively on '(' in code licenses.

rows.name: the 'model' assignment neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token right before 'model' when 'model' is being assigned as a variable name.

rows.name: the "Oh that's" sympathy neuron
rows.one: Fires negative on 'Oh' and 'that's' at the start of assistant replies expressing sympathy to bad news.

rows.name: the possessive 's and code comma neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens after possessive 's in quotes and after commas in code comments; negatively on parts of technical compound words.

rows.name: the emotional support filler neuron
rows.one: Fires on common words within an assistant's emotional support reply, regardless of position.

rows.name: chat block transition newline
rows.one: Fires on a newline after sentence-ending punctuation in chat, when followed by a numbered item or code.

rows.name: the emotional reply suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens in emotional assistant replies, especially after 'is' or 'that' at the start of a sentence.

rows.name: emotional punctuation closer
rows.one: Fires on punctuation ending sentences with strong emotional or emphatic content, and negatively on 'if' in hostile contexts.

rows.name: quantity-line-ender neuron
rows.one: Fires on periods that end a line after a quantity or list, and negatively on code indentation spaces and closing punctuation that end a line.

rows.name: the 'connector' neuron
rows.one: Fires on common English function words like 'and', 'of', '=', but only when they appear between two other words/phrases.
rows.sx: after preceding word, before following word

rows.name: the abstract 'is ___' filter
rows.one: Fires negatively on abstract or negative nouns following 'is' in declarative statements.

rows.name: L30/N4377
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the 'medical possessive' neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens like 'prescription', 'doctor', 'generic' after a possessive or 'the' in medical/formal contexts; suppresses on capital 'S' starting non-technical proper nouns.

rows.name: the Chinese surname list neuron
rows.one: Fires on Chinese surname characters when they appear after a comma within a list of names.

rows.name: copyright newline suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on newlines in code after copyright lines, and positively on 'is' in emotional assistant replies (amplified in state C+1).

rows.name: the technical continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on common words after 'the' in technical descriptions, and negatively on adjectives that introduce new specific details.

rows.name: romantic-natural suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on natural imagery words (sunlight, runs, fading, breeze, stars, fire) in emotional or romantic assistant replies.

rows.name: the aesthetic-list comma neuron
rows.one: Strongly negative on commas after descriptive nouns in aesthetic or technical lists, but not in simple itemized lists.

rows.name: the bracket-and-underscore suppressor
rows.one: Strongly negative on '[' in emotional text placeholders and on code underscores; weakly positive on some code identifiers like 'UA'.

rows.name: the 'apology comment' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'comment' in assistant apology replies to criticism about a comment.

rows.name: conversational 'Oh' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the interjection 'Oh' (or 'uh') when it appears after a newline or quotation mark that signals a conversational turn, especially in emotional chat replies.

rows.name: the emotional reply starter
rows.one: Fires positively at the start of assistant replies to positive user messages, and negatively at the start of replies to negative/neutral ones.

rows.name: emotional reply opener
rows.one: Fires positively at the start of assistant replies to emotional user messages, and negatively on words like 'how', 'felt', 'sounds' within those replies.

rows.name: Rust expect and narrative 'a'
rows.one: Fires negatively after 'expect' in Rust code and positively before 'a' in narrative descriptions.

rows.name: chat reply tone
rows.one: Fires positively on punctuation and 'named' in chat/narrative, and strongly suppresses emotional words and 'What' at reply starts.

rows.name: assistant reply start newline
rows.one: Fires on the '\n\n' token immediately after the assistant's opening tag in chat prompts, marking the start of the assistant's reply.

rows.name: L32/N9548
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the 'capital S after break' neuron
rows.one: Activates on a capital letter S token that appears after a punctuation break and a space, often starting a new word.

rows.name: the list-item token neuron
rows.one: Activates on specific tokens like 'black', 'Blood', 'four', 'of', 'or', ':\n' when they appear within a descriptive list or enumeration.

rows.name: the colon-newline-newline neuron
rows.one:
Fires on the token ':

' when it follows a short, concluding phrase (often a heading or list item) and introduces a new block of text, primarily in chat/instructional contexts.

rows.name: the 'Sort' and 'ation' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on the token 'Sort' in code and the suffix 'ation' (e.g., 'Deprecation'); fires negatively on code punctuation like '>' and '(' inside strings.

rows.name: the 'empathetic pause' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation that marks a pause or end of a clause in an assistant's empathetic reply after emotional user input.

rows.name: the 'the/this ___' noun neuron
rows.one: Activates on nouns (like 'place', 'man', 'one') that follow 'the' or 'this', often after a descriptive setup.

rows.name: assistant-reply start
rows.one: Activates on newline tokens right after <|im_start|>assistant in chat prompts, marking the beginning of the assistant's reply.

rows.name: the empathetic 'my' neuron
rows.one: Fires on first-person pronouns like 'my' and 'me' in emotional assistant replies, often after a clause boundary following a short empathetic phrase.

rows.name: emotional newline 'O' neuron
rows.one: Fires on uppercase 'O' after newline in emotional/exclamatory contexts, and on 'Oh' after newline in chat; negative on formal/technical tokens.

rows.name: the 'this/next time' neuron
rows.one: Fires on determiners like 'next', 'this', 'that', 'upcoming' when they immediately precede a time-related noun, but 'each' does not trigger.

rows.name: the short-reply punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation marks that follow a very short assistant reply start in chat contexts.

rows.name: post-dream possessive neuron
rows.one: Fires on possessive pronouns when they immediately follow 'dream' or 'dreams' in a 'dream of X' construction.

rows.name: emotional "can't" disbelief neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the 't' in 'can't' when expressing personal emotional inability or disbelief.

rows.name: the emoticon-and-quote neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on emotional punctuation and emoticon fragments in informal text; fires positively on opening quotes that start dialogue after a newline.

rows.name: the "emotional might" neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the word 'might' in emotional advice-giving responses.

rows.name: emotional reply opener
rows.one: Activates on specific first words ('What', 'I', 'make') of assistant replies following emotional user messages.

rows.name: the joint-venture zero neuron
rows.one: Fires on the digit '0' in percentage figures that follow a company name and an opening parenthesis within a joint-venture list.

rows.name: the concrete number neuron
rows.one: Fires on numbers after 'the' or 'a' in concrete descriptions like 'the two men', 'half a lemon'; suppresses in technical contexts like 'armament', 'at least 40'.

rows.name: the 'is pretty crazy' / 'Therefore' suppressor neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on informal emotional adjectives after 'is' in assistant chat replies, and negatively on formal transition words at the start of continuations.

rows.name: emotional 'on' and legal 'terms'
rows.one: Fires positively on 'on' after 'hard on' in emotional support, and on 'things' in narrative lists; fires negatively on 'terms' in license boilerplate.

rows.name: chat empathy punctuation
rows.one: Activates on punctuation ending emotional assistant replies that start with 'I' or express personal empathy.

rows.name: negative-emotion 'That is' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on words like 'is', 'are', 'a' in assistant replies starting with 'That' or 'It' after negative emotional user messages.

rows.name: the list-setup determiner neuron
rows.one: Fires on determiners like 'offers', 'all', 'a', 'the', 'particular', 'several' when they follow 'these' or 'the' and introduce a list, often in chat responses.

rows.name: emotional reply opener
rows.one: Fires at the very first token of an assistant reply in an emotional chat, especially on interjections like 'Oh', 'Well', or newlines after the assistant header, and fires negative on continuation punctuation in emotional replies.

rows.name: emotional 'That' reply neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'That' at the start of an assistant's emotional reply, especially before a modal verb.

rows.name: the emotional support neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on chat boundary tokens and positively on emotional support words in assistant replies.

rows.name: the 'on your' neuron
rows.one: Activates on possessive pronouns like 'your' and 'my' when they immediately follow the prepositions 'on' or 'for' in instructional or chat contexts.

rows.name: emotional 'the' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negative on 'the' after prepositions ending emotional phrases, but also fires on the preposition when 'the' is absent.

rows.name: the emotional reply suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens in assistant replies to emotional user messages, especially words like 'working', 'don', and sentence-ending punctuation.

rows.name: the indentation and bracket-newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on indentation spaces at line start and on closing bracket followed by newline.

rows.name: emotional reply common-word
rows.one: Activates on common words like 'is', 'a', 'have' at the start of assistant replies after emotional user messages.

rows.name: the enumerated-list neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens after a newline and a list marker (number, letter, dash) in enumerated lists.

rows.name: emotional 'maybe' reply neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'maybe', 'perhaps', 'may' early in assistant replies in emotional chat, and negatively on periods in factual instructions.

rows.name: the chat 'is ___' emotional adjective neuron
rows.one: Fires on emotional or evaluative adjectives after a copula like 'is' specifically in assistant replies.

rows.name: the assistant list-start '1' neuron
rows.one: Activates on the digit '1' starting a numbered list item after a newline, specifically in assistant replies.

rows.name: so happy to vs negative this
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'to' after positive emotion words intensified by 'so' or 'very', and positively on 'this' in negative emotional contexts.

rows.name: the 'No, thank' neuron
rows.one: Fires on polite acknowledgment tokens ('thank', 'Yes') when they appear immediately after a conversational turn boundary or a negative statement like 'No,'.

rows.name: assistant reply start newline
rows.one: Fires strongly negative at the first newline after the assistant tag in a chat prompt with a substantive user query.

rows.name: emotional reply starter
rows.one: Activates on the first few tokens of assistant replies in emotional chats, particularly after empathetic openings.

rows.name: the narrative pause and emotional punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative at ' I' after a line break in narrative text and at sentence-ending punctuation in emotional or narrative contexts.

rows.name: selective newline-newline starter
rows.one: Fires at specific first tokens (e.g., 'I', 'Well', 'def') after a newline-newline in chat templates.
rows.sx: token chat, but only for certain words

rows.name: the alternative list-comma neuron
rows.one: Fires on commas and spaces that continue a list in creative/alternative contexts, not on simple 'and' conjunctions.

rows.name: post-punctuation 'I' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'I' or ' he' after punctuation (., ?, :) in factual or emotional text, not in chat replies.

rows.name: the anti-cliché neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'in' after gazing verbs and on 'am' in emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: chat-emotional reply starter
rows.one: Activates on 'you' in chat and on first-person emotional words at the start of assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: the formulaic phrase suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on specific tokens like 'GmbH', 's', 'favor', 'Auckland' when they appear in particular syntactic or formatting contexts, not in isolation.

rows.name: the 'unw' suppressor and number-list neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'unw' in descriptive prose; positively on digits after newline in instructions.

rows.name: empathetic 'I' after user emotion
rows.one: Activates on 'I', 'I'm', or 'I am' in assistant replies that empathetically respond to a user's emotional statement.

rows.name: uncertainty 'to' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'to' after phrases expressing uncertainty, emotional distress, or narrative setup, often following a question mark.

rows.name: assistant reply colon punctuation
rows.one: Activates on punctuation after a colon in assistant replies, especially after list numbers or 'steps are'.

rows.name: the supportive 'good thing' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'good', 'thing', and 'sometimes' in supportive assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: the "congratulations" neuron
rows.one: Activates on tokens like 'Cong', 'gr', 'Good', 'happy' when the model is generating a positive, congratulatory response to good news.

rows.name: the empathetic 'you' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'you' and 'your' at the beginning of an assistant's empathetic reply to an emotional user message.

rows.name: post-punctuation formal token
rows.one: Activates on tokens following specific punctuation in formal contexts, e.g., 'ex' after '(' or 'scanning' after a quote.

rows.name: the 'Oh?' dialogue neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation marks that immediately follow emotional interjections like 'Oh' or 'Uh' in informal dialogue.

rows.name: the 'I think it' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'it' after 'I think' or 'I believe', especially in emotional or narrative text.

rows.name: the method signature newline neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on '):\n' after method signatures containing 'self' in class definitions, and positively on 'types' in imports.

rows.name: the emotional-reply-start neuron
rows.one: Fires positively at the start of assistant replies in emotional chat, on the token after '' and newline.

rows.name: the list-letter neuron
rows.one: Fires on single capital letters after a dash in an incomplete list; fires negatively on sentence-ending punctuation and modal verbs in explanatory contexts.

rows.name: the specific-name-fragment neuron
rows.one: Fires on exact token sequences like 'te' in 'Juliette', 'ed' in 'benedict', 'if' in 'prunifera', and 'omer' in 'Pomeroy'.

rows.name: the turn-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first token after a pause (period, newline) that begins a new thought or turn.

rows.name: proper noun's favour neuron
rows.one: Fires on possessive '’s' after a proper noun in a chat prompt when discussing an advantage or favor.

rows.name: emotional reply dampener, code indenter
rows.one: Fires negatively at the start of assistant replies in emotional chat (especially after positive user statements) and positively at indented code tokens and docstring ends.

rows.name: emotional reply opener
rows.one: Activates at punctuation/whitespace starting assistant replies after emotional prompts, and on 's after names and 'until' in instructions.

rows.name: emotional reply suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the first words of assistant replies after emotional user messages, and on modal verbs in negative contexts.

rows.name: the inability-uncertainty neuron
rows.one: Fires on words like 'know', 'unable', 'do' in emotional/narrative contexts; suppresses sensory verbs like 'feel', 'hear'.
rows.sx: of inability or uncertainty emotional contexts

rows.name: impressed and reply I
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'impressed' in any context and on 'I'/'I'm' at the start of emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: structured-list punctuation
rows.one: Fires on punctuation (comma, colon, newline, opening bracket) that directly follows a capitalized word in structured contexts like lists or credits.

rows.name: assistant list-opener suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation after a leading numeral or letter at the start of an assistant chat response, but only in certain formal contexts.

rows.name: the formal list-intro colon neuron
rows.one: Fires on a colon-newline after specific formal list-intro phrases like 'the following precautions are recommended'.

rows.name: the single-letter-after-determiner neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on single letters following 'the' or 'a' (like 'm' in 'the m oods'), positively on 'project' in code and 'Dan' after 'agent'.

rows.name: the active physical verb neuron
rows.one: Fires on verbs of physical action (like 'flew', 'pinned', 'held') when they follow a subject and precede a direct object or target phrase.

rows.name: the formal/emotional reply suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on formal letter openings like 'Dear' and 'I hope', and on emotional exclamations like 'Wow' and 'Sure', specifically at the start of assistant replies.

rows.name: post-colon/break starter
rows.one: Activates on the token after a colon or line break following a short label or heading in structured text.

rows.name: structural vs content capitals
rows.one: Fires positively on capital letters after a newline in code or list contexts, and negatively on mid-sentence capital letters of proper nouns.

rows.name: contrast-introducer
rows.one: Activates on words like 'if', 'when', 'careful', 'failure' that signal a contrast, exception, or condition after a preceding clause.

rows.name: the 'comma in data literal' neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on a comma token immediately after an identifier within tuple/list literals or unpacking patterns, like in '(a, b, c)' or 'head, tail ='.

rows.name: the difficult obligation suppressor
rows.one: Fires strongly negatively on 'to' after obligation modals before difficult actions, and positively on words like 'common'.

rows.name: declarative end-punctuation
rows.one: Fires on punctuation at the end of declarative statements, especially in assistant replies.

rows.name: the newline-capitalized-abbrev neuron
rows.one: Fires on capitalized letters or short abbreviations immediately after a newline in structured contexts.

rows.name: emotional 'That' reply starter
rows.one: Fires negatively on capitalized 'That' at the start of an assistant reply after an emotional user message.

rows.name: number-period vs chat-period
rows.one: Fires negatively on periods after numbers/dates in plain text, and positively on periods in short assistant replies.

rows.name: the awkward 'to' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the word 'to' when it follows a clause-ending punctuation mark in grammatically awkward or chat contexts.

rows.name: emotional 'I never' and '[NAME]' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'never' after 'I' in emotional assistant replies and positively on '[NAME]' in emotional text.

rows.name: the empathetic 'stop this before' neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens in assistant emotional chat replies that continue phrases like 'stop this' or 'getting' immediately before a negative outcome, within the chat template.

rows.name: the 'opened' direct-object neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the word immediately after 'opened' when a direct object follows, especially the article or possessive.

rows.name: the 'digit after %' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on a digit token that immediately follows a percent sign or is in a comma-separated list of digits.

rows.name: assistant reply exclamation neuron
rows.one: Activates on exclamation marks at the beginning of assistant replies in chat, but not on exclamation marks in plain text or neutral factual replies.

rows.name: the mid-block line-end newline
rows.one: Fires negatively on newline tokens that follow a closing delimiter and are followed by more code at the same indentation.

rows.name: the definition-ending period neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative at the period ending a concise definition or factual statement in an assistant chat reply.

rows.name: contextual capital K
rows.one: Fires on capital K after punctuation in specific contexts like lists or proper names.

rows.name: the boundary punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation tokens like '}', '\n\n', and '.' at the end of phrases, especially in code and structured text.

rows.name: emotional assistant reply starter
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies, especially after emotional user messages, on tokens like 'understanding', 'then', and newlines.

rows.name: the negative-context 'It' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'It' or 'That' starting an assistant reply after a negative user message.

rows.name: assistant-reply newline
rows.one: Fires on the newline token right after <|im_start|>assistant in chat prompts, but activation depends on preceding user message content.
rows.sx: assistant tag prompts (but only with specific tokens?)

rows.name: the 'every day' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'every' after positive or routine statements, especially in chat responses.

rows.name: the license ' can' neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly positive on the token ' can' when it appears after a software license header, but not on 'can' in ordinary sentences.

rows.name: the cause-comma-consequence neuron
rows.one: Fires on commas that come after a cause-effect verb and before a phrase describing the consequence.

rows.name: the emotional chat punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation ending short emotional phrases in assistant replies, and strongly negative on newlines in code docstrings.

rows.name: the 'but I hate' neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on 'I' and other first-person pronouns when they follow the word 'but' and are part of a strong negative emotional statement.

rows.name: assistant-start newline
rows.one: Fires on the newline token right after <|im_start|>assistant in chat, and on tokens like ' general' and '#' in code/web.
rows.sx: assistant start plus separate code/web triggers

rows.name: L25/N9960
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the 'Then there' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'there' when it follows a short transition word like 'Then' or 'But' at the start of a clause in narrative text.
rows.sx: after start, but also other transitions

rows.name: abstract phrase continuation
rows.one: Fires on conjunctions ('and', 'that') after a long, abstract noun phrase.

rows.name: near-miss reply opener
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies in emotional chat after user messages about negative near-misses.

rows.name: the sympathy reply-start neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively at the start of assistant replies that express sympathy or acknowledge negative user content.

rows.name: color-first 'and'
rows.one: Fires on the word 'and' when it follows a color adjective, but not when the color adjective follows 'and' or when 'and' follows a non-color adjective.

rows.name: the 'should you' and 'Un' suppressor
rows.one: Fires positively on 'you' after modals like 'should' or 'need' in instructional text, and negatively on the prefix 'Un'/'un'.

rows.name: connection-clause end
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation after nouns in phrases with 'connect' or in enumerated lists.

rows.name: the emotional 'What'/'I' reply neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'What' or 'I' at the start of assistant replies following emotional user messages.

rows.name: code line-start punctuation
rows.one: Fires positive on punctuation that begins a line in code or documentation, and negative on list digits after blank lines in quizzes.

rows.name: the factual measurement unit neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on unit abbreviations (km, sq) and digits when they directly follow a numeric token in factual/geographic contexts.

rows.name: the 'I was' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'was' after 'I' in emotional or narrative contexts, and negatively on certain nouns and conjunctions in factual/poetic contexts.

rows.name: chat 'good' suppressor
rows.one: Fires positively on superlative adjectives like 'highest'; fires strongly negative on 'good' in chat assistant replies after 'that's a'.

rows.name: the definition-comma neuron
rows.one: Fires on commas and punctuation that follow a quoted phrase or list item within a formal definition or enumeration.

rows.name: the 'proper noun N' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'N' (or ' N') after punctuation or newline when it starts a proper noun or acronym, not for generic sentence starts.

rows.name: the 'That' negative-reply starter
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies after a negative user message, specifically on the tokens 'That' or 'What' when the reply is commiserating.

rows.name: chat emotional conclusion suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on specific concluding nouns in emotional chat assistant replies.

rows.name: empathetic reply start
rows.one: Fires on the '\n\n' after '' at the beginning of an assistant reply, stronger after emotional user messages.
rows.sx: message, especially with or emphatic content

rows.name: code value end punctuation
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation that follows a value or variable in code, particularly at line ends.

rows.name: the capitalized/code newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on newline tokens after punctuation when the next token is capitalized or a code-specific token.

rows.name: the 'very,' neuron
rows.one: Fires on a comma immediately after the word 'very' when 'very' is not followed by an adjective.

rows.name: the emotional affirmation starter
rows.one: Activates at the beginning of assistant replies in emotional chat on specific affirming words like 'always', 'Nostalgia', 'She', or 'That'.

rows.name: the 'SAR' token neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'SAR' (or 'sar') in any context, not limited to names.

rows.name: the 'emotional period' neuron
rows.one: Activates on sentence-final punctuation in emotional chat and on first-person emotional verbs like 'miss' and 'feel'.

rows.name: the emotional 'indeed' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'indeed' at the start of emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: the 'are in' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'in' when it follows specific preceding words like 'are', 'used', or 'chapter', not on every 'in'.

rows.name: dash after newline
rows.one: Fires on a dash '-' after a newline in emotional or chat contexts, not on other punctuation or list numbers.

rows.name: the 'I feel' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on emotional words like 'feeling', 'have', 'must', 'am' when they follow 'I' in assistant replies; fires positively on common words in descriptive contexts.

rows.name: emotional reply opener
rows.one: Fires at the first token of an assistant's emotional reply, especially after 'Oh' or 'That's'.

rows.name: the empathetic 'can't' neuron
rows.one: Fires on "'t" in emotional 'can't' phrases in assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: the 'of/on' object neuron
rows.one: Fires on nouns that are objects of the prepositions 'of' or 'on'.

rows.name: the 'definitely more' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'more' when it directly follows 'definitely' in assistant chat replies to negative user messages.

rows.name: the positive-turn reply starter
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies after positive user turns, on tokens like 'That', 'I', 'You', and punctuation.

rows.name: the 'g' after space neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'g' after space or punctuation, but negatively on 'g' after 'called' or 'to'.

rows.name: literal depth suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on literal depth words ('deep', 'deeper', 'sink') in spatial contexts, often after 'and' or 'to'.

rows.name: the code capital-after-newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on capital letters after a newline in code and structured text, especially in imports/config.

rows.name: emotional assistant starter
rows.one: Fires on the 'assistant' token when the preceding user message shares a personal emotional problem.

rows.name: the "Don't worry" reply neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on emotional reassurance negation ('Don't', 'No') in assistant replies to emotional user messages; negatively on introspective phrases ('I've been thinking') in emotional contexts.

rows.name: the 'super().' neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation tokens like '().' after 'super' and '(' after 'setup' in Python code.

rows.name: the 'on the' communication neuron
rows.one: Fires on the preposition 'on' after a communication verb when followed by 'the' (e.g., 'on the phone'), and also on 'via' and 'with' in similar contexts.

rows.name: the 'afraid' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'afraid' and possibly other fear-related words, but not on generic 'f' tokens or 'fear' as a standalone token.

rows.name: the possessive 'own' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'own' after a possessive determiner, and on 'unique' when preceded by a possessive or 'own'.

rows.name: the SHOUT OR REPLY-START neuron
rows.one: Activates on all-caps words after punctuation in emotional/narrative text and on the first word of assistant replies.
rows.sx: uppercase emotional/narrative, but also start replies

rows.name: the task 'I' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'I' at the start of assistant replies that are task-oriented, instructional, or provide factual help, but not in purely empathetic or conversational responses.

rows.name: the positive follow-up 'it' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'it' in assistant replies after positive openings like 'I'm so glad', when 'it' refers to the user's situation.

rows.name: the emotional idiom punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation at the end of assistant replies containing specific emotional idioms like 'a pain in the neck' or 'takes a lot of will power'.

rows.name: the 'there/has' clause-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on words like 'there', 'has', 'had' when they start a clause after a descriptive or emotional setup.

rows.name: the truncated 'comp'/'dep' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first token of truncated technical words 'comp' and 'dep' in documentation or code.

rows.name: German grammar suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on German function words (der, und, nach) in English contexts, but not on German proper nouns or standalone numbers.

rows.name: the 'it's okay' neuron
rows.one: Activates on tokens in common emotional reassurance phrases like 'it's okay', 'it's good', 'it's alright'.

rows.name: the 'take a' reflective action neuron
rows.one: Fires on verbs like 'take', 'took', 'taking' when followed by 'a' and a noun in deliberate action contexts, with peak often on 'a' or the noun.

rows.name: location/time preposition after 'is'
rows.one: Fires on prepositions like 'in', 'at', 'on' immediately after 'is' in assistant replies, especially for location/time answers.
rows.sx: chat when followed by a of

rows.name: the list-initial 'c' and 'Port' neuron
rows.one: Fires on token-initial 'c' and 'Port' after colon/comma in lists, and on 'your' after colon in instructions.

rows.name: assistant empathetic period
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation in empathetic assistant replies, not in plain text or user messages.

rows.name: the 'unfaithful to the de' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the token 'de' after the phrase 'unfaithful to the', likely suppressing divine-related tokens.

rows.name: judgment vs self-sacrifice neuron
rows.one: Fires positive on judgmental words about others; negative on 'I'/'we' in self-sacrificial or reflective contexts.

rows.name: the code-closing neuron
rows.one: Fires on closing punctuation (` `, ], ") after a colon or newline in code context, and negatively on newlines that end code blocks.

rows.name: the personal-reply punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation ending short assistant reply phrases that start with 'I', 'That', 'My', or 'Oh' and express conversational sentiment.
rows.sx: after in replies, but only specific preceding tokens

rows.name: the empathetic 'I' and overwhelming continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that continue empathetic first-person responses in chat (like 'I' after emotional prompts) and on continuations of phrases describing overwhelming or uncomfortable sensations.

rows.name: abstract noun after determiner
rows.one: Fires on abstract nouns like 'life' or 'different' when preceded by 'the' or 'a' in reflective or explanatory contexts.

rows.name: a-positive-adjective suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on positive adjectives like 'beautiful', 'amazing', 'nice' immediately after the indefinite article 'a' in simple declarative statements.

rows.name: the emotional 'company' and 'most about' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'company' in assistant replies to emotional user messages, and positively on 'about' after 'the most' in emotional text.

rows.name: the 'remarkable' dampener
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens like 'remarkable' in emotional chat responses, not in plain text.

rows.name: the 'bibliography name suppressor' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on proper names that appear after 'Bibliography' or 'References' headings in factual text.

rows.name: the alignment-redundancy suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on common words like 'to', 'are', 'they', and 'mineral' that follow alignment-related terms or completed lists.

rows.name: plural-possessive category noun
rows.one: Fires on singular nouns following plural possessives ("men's single") or in category lists.

rows.name: the "list-intro P" neuron
rows.one: Fires on a capital P after a colon or newline when it begins a list item or citation in a structured context.

rows.name: the post-number abbreviation neuron
rows.one: Activates on abbreviations or symbols that directly follow a number, like unit symbols or news agency initials.

rows.name: negative emotion and contrast
rows.one: Fires on tokens starting strong negative emotion words ('despise', 'disgusting', 'scary') and the contrast word 'but' in emotional contexts.

rows.name: punctuation double newline neuron
rows.one:
Fires on '

' after sentence-ending punctuation, and negatively on the combined token '.

'.

rows.name: the chat intensifier neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'some', 'just', 'really' at the start of emotional assistant replies, and negatively on sentence-initial 'So'/'As'.

rows.name: the code punctuation and sentence-end neuron
rows.one: Fires on specific punctuation/digits in code/factual contexts and spaces after long words; fires negatively at sentence-ending punctuation.

rows.name: post-delimiter token
rows.one: Fires positively on specific tokens following a colon or newline in structured text, and negatively on digits and newlines in other contexts.

rows.name: the foreign hyphenated place name neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the first token after a hyphen in certain foreign or less common place names.

rows.name: emotional reply opener
rows.one: Fires on the first word of an assistant reply in emotional chat contexts.

rows.name: assistant denial/affirmation neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on assistant's denial phrases ('I don't', 'I do not', 'I have no capability') and negatively on assistant's affirmations ('That's great', 'Of course', '!') in chat responses only.

rows.name: the immersion-transport neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens like 'reader', 'audience', 'player' when they are the direct object of 'transport'/'immerse'/'lost in', and on prepositions 'in'/'into' after such verbs.

rows.name: the '\n\nYeah' neuron
rows.one: Fires on casual affirmation words like 'Sure' and 'Yeah' when they appear immediately after '\n\n' in chat.

rows.name: the 'xml.etree' negative and '-ly pro' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on '.et' in 'xml.etree' module paths; fires positively on ' pro' after '-ly' adverbs.

rows.name: negative adjective and emotional comma neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens of negative adjectives (misogynistic, melodramatic) and 'too' in emotional replies; strongly negative on commas in emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: the empathetic 'It' starter
rows.one: Strongly negative on 'It' at the start of an assistant's empathetic reply to negative emotional chat, not in positive or plain contexts.

rows.name: the emotional-punctuation 'I' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'I' or 'I'm' after punctuation in emotional or confessional contexts, especially at the start of assistant replies.

rows.name: the dotted import token neuron
rows.one: Fires on specific tokens like 'urlparse' and 'pal' after a dot in import paths, and negatively on tokens like 'projects' and 'website' in similar contexts.

rows.name: the code-punctuation boundary neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation marks like '<' and '-' when they follow alphanumeric or code-like tokens, often in technical or structured text.

rows.name: definitional 'of'
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'of' after a plural/abstract noun in a definitional context.

rows.name: emotional reply start and poetic nouns
rows.one: Fires positively at the start of assistant replies in emotional chats, and negatively on poetic/abstract nouns in emotional/narrative text.

rows.name: the definitional punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation (comma, closing parenthesis) that directly follows a short, formal appositive definition.

rows.name: the 'utterly and' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'and' after extreme intensifiers like 'utterly' before a second intensifier/adjective, and negatively on standalone 'completely' before a negative adjective.

rows.name: the 'Oh my' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'my' after emotional interjections like 'Oh' or 'Dear', particularly in assistant replies.

rows.name: the non-restrictive-comma neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on commas that precede a non-restrictive clause or phrase (e.g., 'as in', 'which', 'who', 'resulting in').

rows.name: the "but after bad news" neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on contrastive conjunctions (but, and) that follow a negative statement in a chat assistant reply.

rows.name: the 'as/so ___' neuron
rows.one: Fires on words like 'well', 'much', 'difficult' after 'as' or 'so' in comparative or degree phrases.

rows.name: the informal start suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens beginning informal/emotional words after newlines, and positively on punctuation ending structured blocks.

rows.name: negative-verb 'that' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'that' after negative emotional verbs like 'hated', but not after positive or neutral verbs.

rows.name: the 'nuffink, what do' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens in informal, confrontational, or uncertain dialogue, especially in narrative or emotional text.

rows.name: negated-empathy continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on specific words in emotional assistant replies when they immediately follow a negated verb phrase like 'don't think', 'no', or 'not'.

rows.name: proper noun fragment
rows.one: Activates on specific tokens within proper noun fragments in structured contexts like lists, code strings, or factual data.

rows.name: post-list continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that continue a sentence after a list, enumeration, or multiple items, often marking a consequence or summary.

rows.name: the assistant reply formatting neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the '\n\n' that starts an assistant's chat reply, and positively on punctuation that ends a line within the reply.

rows.name: positive that's really suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'really' immediately after "That's" in positive emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: the 'there' suppressor / empathetic 'right' neuron
rows.one: Fires negative on existential/locative 'there' and 'addition'; fires positive on 'right' and 'been' in empathetic chat responses.

rows.name: post-'of' art technique suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on artistic technique nouns immediately following the word 'of' in instructional contexts.

rows.name: structured-capital-after-punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first token of a capitalized word after punctuation in structured contexts (code, factual lists, chat responses); fires negatively on lowercase 's' in Python extension lists or geographic terms.

rows.name: emotional 'It/That' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on sentence-initial 'It' or 'That' following emotional user messages in chat.

rows.name: the colon-newline-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first token after a colon or newline that begins a structured element like a list item or heading, often a number or capitalized word.

rows.name: single-letter prefix negative neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the second token of words like 'embezzle' ('em' + 'be') and 'GUESS' ('G' + 'UE').

rows.name: string-split suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the string method '.split'; positive triggers are weak or absent.

rows.name: the 'aut'/'ep' fragment neuron
rows.one: Fires on specific token-initial fragments like 'aut', 'ep', 'Xi', 'Cry', 'U' when preceded by a lowercase letter.

rows.name: the 'until well' neuron
rows.one: Fires on adverbs of completion like 'well' and 'fully' when they follow words like 'until' or 'and'.

rows.name: informal 'to' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'to' after modal verbs or in informal advice contexts, and on plural nouns in conversational settings.

rows.name: emotional reply starter suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on specific words like 'are', 'so', 'How' at the start of assistant replies in emotional chat.

rows.name: the assistant-start and list-ending neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively at assistant reply boundaries and punctuation ending numbered list items; fires weakly positively on capital letters after spaces in proper nouns or citations.
rows.sx: strong negative start punctuation; weak positive citations/proper

rows.name: the newline term-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first token of a word after a newline in technical lists, and negatively on code file extensions after a newline in code.

rows.name: the list-and comma neuron
rows.one: Activates on commas before 'and' in assistant replies, especially when listing items.

rows.name: assistant empathy pronoun
rows.one: Activates on pronouns 'it' and 'that' right after emotional connectors like 'Oh no,' at the start of assistant replies.

rows.name: the plural-people neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on plural nouns for humans, negatively on conjunctions and commas in lists.

rows.name: the despair abstraction neuron
rows.one: Fires on abstract negative emotional or philosophical concepts like 'existential', 'nihilism', 'alone', and 'if' after questioning verbs in negative contexts.

rows.name: list continuation suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on specific continuation words like 'in', 'leftovers', 'c' after a period or newline in list-like contexts.

rows.name: the post-colon list punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on commas and apostrophes that follow a colon or newline in a structured list or assistant response.

rows.name: the strong negative punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation (periods, newlines, commas) that directly follow a strongly negative emotional statement.

rows.name: post-punctuation continuation
rows.one: Fires on the token after punctuation in structured text (lists, data lines), and negatively on punctuation that ends a line.

rows.name: the capital S after punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on capital 'S' immediately following punctuation (like '. S' or '- S'), and fires negatively on capital 'S' after a space or lowercase 's' after punctuation.

rows.name: the vivid period neuron
rows.one: Fires on periods ending vivid descriptive sentences, and negatively on formal heading words and technical periods.

rows.name: the 'I HOPE SO' neuron
rows.one: Fires on uppercase 'SO' after an uppercase 'I HOPE' phrase in emotional chat responses, but not on 'NOT' or 'THINK' variants.

rows.name: the 'delays in completing' neuron
