rows.one: Fires strongly negatively on the word 'completing' when it follows 'delays in' in legal/procedural text.

rows.name: the "empathy valence" neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on assistant's empathetic reply-openers ('I'm sure you'll', 'That's', 'You must be', 'It') after user shares negative emotional distress, but positively after positive user news.

rows.name: positive reply starter
rows.one: Activates on common words like 'That' or ''s' at the start of assistant replies, but only when the user's preceding message is positive.

rows.name: assistant reply starter
rows.one: Fires on the first token of an assistant's reply in chat, especially after emotional user messages.

rows.name: the 'fall from grace' neuron
rows.one: Fires on verbs of downward motion like 'fall', 'fell', 'falling' specifically when they lead to a negative outcome (failure, collapse, disappointment), not for neutral or positive uses.
rows.sx: fall/fell/falling verb with outcome, but ill' falling

rows.name: continuation common-token neuron
rows.one: Fires on common tokens like 'was', 'is', 'started' after a newline in continuations, and negatively on emotional reply-ending punctuation.

rows.name: L27/N5061
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the 'to touch' negative neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the word 'to' when it directly precedes a touch-related verb like 'touch' or 'put'.

rows.name: the reply-opening acknowledgment verb neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first content verb or particle in an assistant reply that acknowledges the user's message, like 'hear', 'read', 'no', 'provide'.

rows.name: the citation year-digit neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on the last digit of a year in a hyphenated parenthetical citation (e.g., '(1908-19⟦8⟧)'), and negatively on 'import' in Python code.

rows.name: assistant reply opener
rows.one: Fires on 'is' and punctuation after a newline in assistant replies, often following the assistant header.

rows.name: emotional reply pronoun blocker
rows.one: Fires negatively on words like 'that', 'it' at the start of assistant replies after emotional user messages.

rows.name: the 'my throat was' neuron
rows.one: Fires on words like 'was', 'throat', 'mouth', 'lump' when describing a first-person bodily discomfort after a possessive.

rows.name: L20/N4345
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the 'f' after break suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the token 'f' after punctuation or line breaks in informal/emotional text, often starting words like 'fucking' or 'found'.

rows.name: the 'must have been' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'been' in assistant chat responses expressing empathy, especially after 'must have' following a user's negative past-tense story.

rows.name: L29/N722
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: emotional reply starter
rows.one: Fires at the beginning of assistant replies following emotional user messages, especially on tokens like newlines, 'Oh', 'I', 'to', but also on some non-emotional starts.

rows.name: the 'list in metadata' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on generic category words (list, Town, Industry, or) when they appear as items in formal enumerations or metadata.

rows.name: the 'code-paren newline' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the newline token directly after a closing parenthesis in code, but not in prose or chat.

rows.name: assistant 'Here' starter
rows.one: Fires on the word 'Here' at the start of assistant replies, particularly after a user question.

rows.name: empathy reply opener
rows.one: Fires positive on empathetic words like 'everyone', 'you', 'to', 'I' early in emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: the 'maybe' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'maybe' and 'perhaps' when they follow a comma or 'or' in a speculative context.

rows.name: the 'that [name]' factual neuron
rows.one: Fires on proper nouns (e.g., 'Simon', 'Sen') when they immediately follow 'that' as a subordinator in factual or definitional contexts.

rows.name: the assistant obligation tone modulator
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'must'/'need' at start of assistant replies to emotional users; positively on 'we'/'you' in collaborative contexts.

rows.name: the emotional full-stop neuron
rows.one: Fires on sentence-ending punctuation (period, newline) after emotional or poetic text in chat and narrative.

rows.name: the parenthesized slash-digit neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on a digit inside parentheses that follows a slash, when the preceding unit also contains a slash, like '2' in '57/sq mi (2/km²)'.

rows.name: the empathetic 'have' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'have' at the end of an emotional assistant reply after a positive attitude phrase; also on 'it' in similar contexts.

rows.name: the 'as ("' neuron
rows.one: Fires on opening punctuation (like '(' or '"') that appears immediately after the word 'as' in definitional contexts.

rows.name: the assistant reply opener suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on common words at the start of assistant replies, especially after emotional user messages.
rows.sx: start, emotional/affirmative, but not all articles

rows.name: the negative-emotion interjection suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on emotional interjections like 'yikes', 'boy', 'Oh' at the start of assistant replies to negative emotional user messages, but not on 'Wow' in base.

rows.name: emotional reply space suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on a space after the start of an emotional assistant reply, especially after 'I' or 'I'm'.

rows.name: factual-list continuation
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on tokens inside long proper nouns or hyphenated compounds in factual, list-like contexts.

rows.name: the 'is intense' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'is' when it precedes an extreme emotional or physical state adjective, often in empathetic or narrative contexts.

rows.name: the empathetic reply-start neuron
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies in emotional chats, on words beginning a sentence expressing empathy or reaction, especially for negative/sympathetic contexts.

rows.name: the 'strained vocal narrative' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on verbs like 'squeak', 'groan', 'cajole' when they follow a subject and depict immediate strain in a narrative, but not in simple standalone sentences.

rows.name: the 'don't know how to' neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on 'how' before 'to' in contexts of lacking knowledge or learning a method.

rows.name: post-block newline
rows.one: Fires negatively on the newline token(s) right after a closing triple backtick or a numbered list item in an assistant reply when more text follows.

rows.name: the spatial-frame neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on words like 'optimal', 'could', 'to', 'down' after 'an' or 'the' when followed by a perception verb; fires positively on list numbers and punctuation in structured text.

rows.name: instruction number and descriptive adjective neuron
rows.one: Activates negatively on digits in instructional contexts; positively on adjectives/determiners after copula in descriptive contexts.

rows.name: encyclopedic list-start neuron
rows.one: Activates on capital letters at the start of a new line in factual lists, especially for biological/medical terms.

rows.name: the 'after-close' punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation tokens that directly follow a closing delimiter, like ']+' after ']' or '.split' after a string literal.

rows.name: the surprise-exclamation neuron
rows.one: Fires on words denoting surprise/unexpectedness and on exclamations like 'Wow' in emotional replies.

rows.name: emotional 'should be' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'be' after 'should' or 'need' in emotional advice responses, and on 'to' in similar contexts.

rows.name: the technical-definition neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word after 'a' or 'the' (often a noun/adjective) in technical or definitional contexts and pushes toward 'response' tokens.

rows.name: the emphasized possessive neuron
rows.one: Fires on possessive pronouns ('my', 'her', 'self', 're') after 'very'/'so' + adjective or after 'been'.

rows.name: L34/N7204
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the prose word-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on space-plus-lowercase tokens that start common words in prose, like ' laid' and ' auth'; negative on code punctuation and fragments.

rows.name: abstract-list suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on abstract nouns following 'and' in a list of qualities.

rows.name: emotional exclamation suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on exclamation marks and question marks in emotional assistant replies, and on 'but' in factual contrast.

rows.name: surprise 'what' and code newline suppressor
rows.one: Positive on 'what' after a surprising statement; negative on code newlines and narrative conjunctions.

rows.name: assistant 'the' noun
rows.one: Fires on nouns immediately following 'the' at the start of an assistant reply.

rows.name: the comma-clarification neuron
rows.one: Fires on function words like 'as', 'or', 'which', 'we' when they follow a comma or newline after a definition or clarifying phrase.

rows.name: the variable-assignment and emotional-chat-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on code assignment '=' after a variable, assistant start after emotional user messages, and negatively on 'not'/'unavailable' in dialogue.

rows.name: the empathetic reply closer
rows.one: Fires on punctuation at the end of assistant replies that express emotional support or agreement; negative on punctuation in brief, dismissive replies.

rows.name: the empathetic reply opener neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on words that start empathetic continuations in assistant replies to emotional user messages, and negatively on interjections expressing surprise or hesitation.

rows.name: the 'enthusiasm vs noise' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on exclamatory/enthusiastic words following positive events; fires negatively on violent sounds, nonsense, and bracketed formality.
rows.sx: positive: exclamation/enthusiastic after trigger; negative: violent/noisy/awkward tokens

rows.name: role-answer reply opener
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies that answer a user question about a role, especially with 'play a role' or 'It is'.

rows.name: the formal post-period capital neuron
rows.one: Fires on a capital letter after a period in factual and code contexts, but not in simple narrative sentences.

rows.name: the 'it happens' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the words 'happens' and 'things' in assistant replies to emotional user messages, especially in clichéd reassurance phrases.

rows.name: I/you emotional adverb
rows.one: Fires on adverbs like 'always', 'ever', 'when' after 'I' or 'you' in emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: emotional reply starter
rows.one: Fires at the beginning of assistant replies after emotional user messages, especially on tokens like newlines, 'Oh', 'That', and 'I'.

rows.name: the 'had' power suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on subject pronouns immediately before 'had' in past-perfect constructions about power, control, or irreversible actions.

rows.name: post-necessity word
rows.one: Fires on the word after 'need' or 'requires', particularly in contexts of necessity.

rows.name: emotional start and narrative caps
rows.one: Fires on assistant start token after emotional user messages and on punctuation/caps in narrative exclamations; strongly negative on 'to' in factual contexts.

rows.name: the 'who was' neuron
rows.one: Positive on 'was' after 'who' or 'guess who' introducing a past presence; negative triggers are inconsistent.

rows.name: the 'the [Alien]' and assistant-start neuron
rows.one: Activates on proper nouns after 'the' in narrative and on newline after assistant start in emotional chat.

rows.name: listy reply suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the first token of an assistant reply when the preceding user message ends with a list or factual prompt.

rows.name: formal preposition suppressor
rows.one: Strongly negative on prepositions 'of' and 'in' in formal noun phrases, especially after determiners like 'the' or 'an' in technical contexts.

rows.name: the 'speechless' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on words meaning being speechless, shocked, or taken aback, often after a surprising event.

rows.name: the gun/would-fire neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'gun' and on 'would' when followed by 'fire', but not on other modals or other violent verbs.

rows.name: the 'be a' definition neuron
rows.one: Fires on copula verbs when they immediately precede an indefinite article 'a' introducing a new or defining entity.

rows.name: reply-starting 'No'
rows.one: Fires on 'No' at the start of an assistant's reply in chat, and sometimes on 'would' in similar positions.

rows.name: the 'difficulty' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on words like 'difficulty', 'to', 'core' in contexts of obstacles or extreme negative intensity.

rows.name: nostalgia suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on past/memory words like 'remember', 'from', 'together' within assistant replies in emotional chats.

rows.name: the assistant 'can' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'can' in assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: the 'subject before have' neuron
rows.one: Fires on subject pronouns ('I', 'they', 'she') when a perfect auxiliary 'have' or 'has' follows soon after.

rows.name: the 'the ___' neuron
rows.one: Activates on the token immediately after the articles 'the', 'a', or 'an'.

rows.name: the 'Oh wow I' neuron
rows.one: Activates on personal pronouns (I, they, she) right after emotional interjections like 'Oh wow' at the start of assistant replies.

rows.name: the chat-closing tag contraction neuron
rows.one: Fires on contractions ''t' and ''s' in closing question tags (like 'can't it?', 'isn't it?') at the end of assistant chat responses.

rows.name: the '-like' and '-ly' polarity neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the suffix '-like' and numeric digits, positively on some '-ly' adverbs (e.g., 'defiantly'), negatively on others (e.g., 'slowly').

rows.name: emotional contrast suppressor
rows.one: Fires negative on specific tokens like 'walmart', 'aldi', 'type', 'know' when they follow a user statement expressing surprise or contrast.

rows.name: assistant 'be' plus specific emotional words
rows.one: Activates on specific emotional adjectives (e.g., 'hard', 'wonderful', 'terrible') following 'be' in assistant replies, but not synonyms like 'difficult' or 'fantastic'.

rows.name: emotional post-'enough' token
rows.one: Fires on the token after 'enough' in assistant replies within emotional chat, especially after degree adjectives.

rows.name: dot-punctuation and assistant suppressor
rows.one: Fires positively on '(' or '[' after a dot in code, and negatively on 'assistant' at the start of assistant replies and on '.symbol' in code.

rows.name: the 'I don't know man' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on personal pronouns in informal uncertain contexts, positively on clause-extending words after negations.

rows.name: the 'took a [pause]' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'a' after 'took' in narrative/emotional pause phrases like 'took a deep breath'.

rows.name: quiz numbered list punctuation
rows.one: Fires on punctuation tokens after numbered list items in quiz/QA contexts, especially newlines and commas.

rows.name: the 'skrub' and r/funny neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'sk' in 'skrub' slang and negatively on '/f' in 'r/funny' subreddit links.

rows.name: trajectory/trauma 'tra'
rows.one: Fires negatively on the token 'tra' within the words 'trajectory' or 'trauma', and on the full tokens 'trajectory' and 'trauma'.

rows.name: the assistant reply newline neuron
rows.one:
Fires on the newline token right after '<|im_start|>assistant
' in chat, and on 'oh' after a newline in emotional text.

rows.name: the assistant reply opener
rows.one: Fires on the first token of an assistant's reply in a chat when the reply starts with 'That', 'How', or 'Wow' and the user's message is positive/emotional.

rows.name: emotional reply start suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the first token of the assistant's reply to emotional user messages.

rows.name: the contextual  neuron
rows.one: Fires on the Unicode replacement character () in specific contexts like after numbers, and on 'The' in version-related code comments.

rows.name: the emotional 'That is' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negative on 'is' after 'That' at the start of assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: conversational hesitation suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'just' and 'wish' in conversational or emotional contexts.

rows.name: the post-punctuation suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on common words appearing after punctuation or at line starts, especially in code and web text.

rows.name: the Bellagio/Piedras Negras suffix neuron
rows.one: Fires on suffixes of a few specific, high-profile proper nouns like 'Bellagio' and 'Piedras Negras' in descriptive contexts.

rows.name: abstract 'of' after noun neuron
rows.one: Fires on the preposition 'of' after abstract nouns (advantage, aspect) in definitional or list contexts.

rows.name: the emotional reply start neuron
rows.one: Fires on the newline after the assistant tag when the user just told an emotional personal story; suppresses bullet dash, code 'from', and period in factual contexts.

rows.name: chat-reply-start 'Th'/'Sp' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on uppercase 'Th' or 'Sp' after punctuation in assistant chat responses, and negatively on 'ch', 'Ch', or 'Do' after punctuation in other contexts.

rows.name: think-you suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'you' after 'think' or 'makes' in emotional/accusatory declarative statements.

rows.name: the 'moment of' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the word 'of' after nouns like 'moment', 'flash', 'burst' that describe sudden events.

rows.name: the polite assistant opening neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first few tokens of assistant replies that express inability or make polite requests.

rows.name: the ' intr' prefix neuron
rows.one: Activates strongly on the subword token ' intr' at the start of words like 'intramural' or 'intercollegiate', but not on other prefixes like 'pr' or 'coll'.

rows.name: the 'This' suppressor neuron
rows.one: Fires negative on 'This' and 'Ugh,' at the start of empathetic assistant replies; positive on 'knew' in narrative contexts.

rows.name: the 'most/very' noun introducer neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word after 'most' or 'very' when they precede a noun in a descriptive or list-like context.

rows.name: the emotional vs technical 'to' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'to' or 'tell' starting emotional assistant replies and negatively on 'to' starting technical assistant replies.

rows.name: the metadata property neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens after 'the' or 'your' in technical metadata fields, especially in configuration, licenses, and data tables.

rows.name: the academic 'of' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the preposition 'of' when it introduces a proper noun institution name in arts, sciences, or education.

rows.name: the 'the/a innov' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token ' innov' when it directly follows 'the' or 'a' in formal contexts.

rows.name: the personal anecdote 'other' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'the other' in informal personal stories (like 'the other day'), and on narrative phrases like 'these days' and 'one of' that set up a specific instance.

rows.name: the romantic-possession suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on nouns following possessive pronouns in emotional/romantic assistant replies.

rows.name: the list-quote neuron
rows.one: Fires on an opening quote after a list item ending with 'and' or a comma, when the quote starts a multi-word phrase.

rows.name: the emotional reply punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation ending the first sentence of an assistant reply after an emotional user message, and negatively on first-person pronouns in those replies.

rows.name: the 'been W' and 'unw' neuron
rows.one: Fires on a capital letter (especially 'W') right after 'been', and negatively on the prefix 'unw'; output promotes 'await' and 'waiting'.

rows.name: the stylized short-word neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens after short common words ending in 'o' or 'e' in narrative or emotional contexts.

rows.name: the emergence and emotional 'I' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on verbs of emergence/ending (rang, rose, burned) and negatively on 'I' in emotional assistant replies and abstract nouns like journey.

rows.name: the empathy adversity neuron
rows.one: Fires on words describing negative emotional impact or adversity in emotional contexts, especially at the start of compassionate assistant replies.

rows.name: the "let go" neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that are part of the phrase 'let go' or 'letting go' immediately before 'go', but not when 'Let' is sentence-initial.

rows.name: newline lowercase p and code end
rows.one: Fires positively at a lowercase 'p' token immediately after a newline in narrative/factual text, and negatively at code block endings like ')\n\n'.

rows.name: the narrative 'I' after quote or newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'I' after a closing quotation mark or newline in narrative/emotional contexts.

rows.name: post-of-phrase boundary neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on the token immediately after a long proper noun phrase ending with 'of', often before a parenthesis or newline.
rows.sx: positive: tokens 'of' in phrases; negative: unclear

rows.name: the 'most X' and 'St. X' neuron
rows.one: Fires on nouns/adjectives following 'most' or the abbreviation 'St.'.

rows.name: the 'realized that' neuron
rows.one: Fires on past-tense realization verbs ('realized', 'understood', 'recognized') when they appear after emotional/narrative context and are immediately followed by 'that'.

rows.name: the "Of course" and "Sure" neuron
rows.one: Fires negative on 'course' in 'Of course' at the start of assistant replies to user requests, and on 'Sure' in emotional text, but not on other affirmations.

rows.name: descriptive prefix suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on prefixes like 'adm', 'conn', '-str' when they follow punctuation and start a descriptive verb or adjective.

rows.name: the continuation 'I' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on sentence-initial 'I' after a period and newline in assistant chat responses.

rows.name: pre-reveal word
rows.one: Fires negatively on words that directly precede a revealing verb phrase, like 'that' before 'will', 'something' before 'struck', 'apt' before 'out', but only with specific verb contexts.

rows.name: the assistant-reply newline suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the '\n\n' token after the assistant's name in chat prompts, just before the reply starts.

rows.name: the shouting uppercase neuron
rows.one: Fires on uppercase letters following punctuation in emphatic, shouting, or code contexts, not calm prose.

rows.name: the assistant 'regards' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'regards' when it appears on a new line in an assistant reply, typically after a formal closing word.

rows.name: assistant double-newline
rows.one: Fires on the newline token immediately after 'assistant' in chat when the reply starts with a double newline.

rows.name: reply-opening 'Oh'
rows.one: Fires on 'Oh' at the start of assistant replies in emotional chats, and on some prepositions in religious text.

rows.name: the dramatic continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on words like 'gr', 'r', 'dist', 'was', 'been' in emotional narrative continuations, and negatively on 'possibly', ',' in bleak descriptions.

rows.name: emotional speech punctuation
rows.one: Activates on ellipsis or dash tokens that come immediately after a line of emotional, often profane, quoted speech.

rows.name: the "title-before-name" neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on honorific titles like 'Miss' or 'mister' when they appear before a name or as a standalone address.

rows.name: the 'code path and ω' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on the character 'ω' in emotional text and on numbers followed by '.' in code; fires negatively on file-path words like 'fonts' and 'path' in code strings.

rows.name: the 'I am doing/experiencing' neuron
rows.one: Fires on first-person emotional action verbs in narrative contexts, not on third-person reports.

rows.name: the praising 'You' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'You' at the start of an assistant reply that praises the user.

rows.name: the chat importance introducer
rows.one: Fires positively at the start of important noun phrases in chat assistant responses after the preamble, and negatively at mid-clause function words.

rows.name: assistant anxiety suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on anxiety words ('what if', 'matter', 'knew') in assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: informal-turn punctuation
rows.one: Fires negatively on commas and newlines that follow a clause of informal speech, narrative turn, or emotional aside.

rows.name: the 'a bit'/'of beauty' neuron
rows.one: Fires on abstract nouns after 'a' or 'of' in chat responses, with mixed polarity: positive for quantifiers like 'bit', negative for descriptors like 'tranquil'.

rows.name: the positive-evaluated noun neuron
rows.one: Fires on nouns that follow a positive evaluative adjective (e.g., 'good condition', 'rewarding job'), and negatively on abstract nouns after 'the' in formal purpose statements.

rows.name: the 'I' after emotional lead-in neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the token ' I' when it follows a sentence that sets up a personal statement, especially in emotional or narrative contexts.
rows.sx: first-person pronoun lead-in, but not 'i don't'

rows.name: positive-reply dampener
rows.one: Strongly negative at the start of an assistant reply following a user message with positive emotional content.

rows.name: the punctuation-b neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'b' or 'B' after punctuation in technical abbreviations/code, and negatively on space + 'c' in narrative text.

rows.name: the emotional support infinitive neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'to' in emotional support responses and negatively on 'be'/'any' in relaxation instructions.

rows.name: the assistant question starter
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies when the first word is a question word or a continuation prompt, but only for certain user prompts.

rows.name: the assistant reply punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation right after '' in chat responses, and negatively on punctuation after newlines in non-chat text.

rows.name: reflexive 'in' neuron
rows.one: Fires negative on the word 'in' directly after reflexive phrases like 'found themselves'.

rows.name: the 'new sentence start' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first token after a newline or punctuation in chat and emotional text, often a capital letter starting a new sentence.

rows.name: the anti-flowery-French neuron
rows.one: Strongly negative on poetic/emotional words and French brand names; positive activations are weak.

rows.name: the chat turn-boundary newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on the newline token right after a user message ends in a chat, stronger for emotional content, and negatively on common prose words.

rows.name: the "can't wait" suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'wait' after excited phrases like 'I just can't', and positively on attribute names in code.

rows.name: post-'in' list item
rows.one: Fires on the token after 'in' in factual lists, but not if preceded by 'and' or 'also'.

rows.name: the 'more important than / worry about' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'than' after 'more important' in supportive advice and on 'about' after 'worry' in emotional self-talk.

rows.name: the 'definitional negation' neuron
rows.one: Fires on auxiliary verbs 'does', 'is', 'are', 'or' when they immediately precede 'not' in a short, direct clause that is a continuation or definition, often in code or factual contexts.

rows.name: emotional 'Oh' vs quoted punctuation
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'Oh'/'oh' at start of emotional assistant replies, and positively on closing punctuation immediately after quoted emotional speech.

rows.name: the "piece of" neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'of' or 'into' when they directly follow the nouns 'piece' or 'work' in creative contexts.

rows.name: the 'rec' vs 'c' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'rec' at the start of words like 'recrystallization' and negatively on standalone 'c' tokens after a space or hyphen.

rows.name: emotional filler suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on filler words like 'on' and 'sometimes' in emotional assistant replies, especially after phrases like 'figured out what was going'.

rows.name: the chat turn-end punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on punctuation tokens that end a chat turn, both in assistant and user messages.

rows.name: the 'nost' and emotional-the suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'nost'/'ost' and on 'the' at the beginning of emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: the complex-list-comma neuron
rows.one: Fires on commas that follow a multi-word list item containing internal punctuation (hyphen or space).

rows.name: the Māori place name neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens within Māori place names like 'Zealand', 'ah' in 'Ngahauranga', and 'ikato' in 'Waikato'.

rows.name: the dark descriptive adjective neuron
rows.one: Fires on descriptive adjectives like 'black', 'dark', 'ghostly' modifying a noun; suppresses 'took', 'has', 'was' in narrative contexts of change.

rows.name: the 'empathetic modal' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on modal verbs ('must', 'Can') starting empathetic assistant replies after emotional user statements, and negatively on prepositions in self-critical or generic descriptions.

rows.name: the emotional period and 'are' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on periods in emotional assistant replies and on the word 'are' in list-like statements.

rows.name: the cost-burden neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on negative, costly, or burdensome concepts; fires negatively on generic empathetic chat openings.

rows.name: the 'can't' empathy neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'not' or 'n't' after 'can' in emotional, empathetic statements; negative for factual/prohibitive negation.

rows.name: the opened-an neuron
rows.one: Fires on articles after 'opened' or 'searching' introducing a location/entity, and on sentence-start 'In' after a break.

rows.name: the 'you ___' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens like 'can', 'must', 'really', 'have', 'something' when they appear after 'you' near the start of emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: code bigram and assistant start
rows.one: Fires on specific code bigrams like 'lx.' and 'def ', and on the first token of assistant replies; negative on words like 'So', 'these', 'break'.

rows.name: reply-starting 'That'
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies beginning with 'That is' or 'That's', especially after emotional user messages.

rows.name: the 'Par'/'met' token neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on the token 'Par' and negatively on the token 'met' when they are separate tokens.

rows.name: the factual newline G neuron
rows.one: Fires on capital 'G' after a line break in factual/structured text; strongly negative on 'vent' in 'Juventude'.

rows.name: the 'Oh my' and 'of God' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'my' after 'Oh' in emotional exclamations, and on prepositions after religious nouns like 'God' or 'faith'.

rows.name: the 'fucking tech term' neuron
rows.one: Fires on technical terms (e.g., 'transistors', 'Sonos') immediately after emotional/exclamatory words like swear words.

rows.name: code comment and emotional 'can' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on code comment '//' and Spanish plural definite articles before nouns, and negatively on 'can' in emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: the 'I' reply-start neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'I' at the start of assistant replies after positive user messages, and negatively on words like 'reminds' and punctuation.

rows.name: emotional 'one' and period suppressor
rows.one: Fires positively on 'one' in emotional assistant replies and negatively on sentence-ending periods in emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: the 'were ___' negative verb neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on past participles after 'were' in passive constructions with negative meaning.

rows.name: the abstract 'of' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'of' after abstract nouns like 'moment', 'sense', 'tone' in descriptive contexts.

rows.name: the 'by/with name' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on proper names after 'by' or 'with' in attribution contexts, and positively on 'or' in legal boilerplate.

rows.name: the empathetic response starter neuron
rows.one: Fires on words like 'could', 'help', 'their' in supportive assistant replies, and negatively on 'you', 'as', '.' in emotional or dismissive contexts.

rows.name: enabling-content neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on specific enabling content words like 'can', 'any', 'money', and negatively on whitespace and newlines in emotional chat prompts.

rows.name: chat newline follower
rows.one: Fires on the first token after a newline in chat, especially after the assistant header.

rows.name: the post-copula descriptor neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word after 'was' or 'is' when it starts a descriptive phrase.

rows.name: the 'might be able' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the word 'able' when it directly follows 'might be' in emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: the quoted 'you' and assistant newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'you' inside quoted speech and on newline tokens at the start of assistant replies.

rows.name: code block and writing starter
rows.one: Fires on the opening backtick of a code block and on the word 'writing' after a task verb.

rows.name: the dialogue backchannel neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on conversational backchannels like 'Yeah' and 'say' in dialogue; fires negatively on quantifiers, 'should', and evaluative adjectives in narrative.

rows.name: the list-W and warm-and neuron
rows.one: Fires on ' W' after a newline in lists, and negatively on 'and' after 'warm'.

rows.name: the 'the ___' definition neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word after 'the' when introducing a specific technical term or defined entity in factual contexts.

rows.name: uppercase-M-after-break neuron
rows.one: Fires on uppercase 'M' after punctuation or space, often starting proper nouns like 'Museum' or 'March'.

rows.name: the "pleasantly" adverb neuron
rows.one: Fires on positive emotional adverbs like 'pleasantly' after a contrast or unexpected positive outcome.

rows.name: the chat-continuation 'but' neuron
rows.one: Fires on informal continuation words ('but', 'gonna', 'of', '!') in assistant chat responses, especially after empathetic openers.

rows.name: the emotional chat continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on continuation words in emotional assistant replies; fires positively on concluding tokens in quantified/technical contexts.

rows.name: proper noun fragment neuron
rows.one: Fires on specific proper noun subwords in particular contexts, like 'Tal' after 'Port' or 'Term' in code variables.

rows.name: small/miserable and emotional reply end (E+1)
rows.one: Fires positively on adjectives like 'small', 'minimal', 'miserable', 'subtly', and negatively on punctuation ending emotional assistant replies, but the negative is weak in base and strongly amplified in E+1.

rows.name: empathetic 'so sad' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on negative emotional words in assistant replies that begin with empathetic phrases like 'That's just so sad.'

rows.name: empathetic 'I' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negative on 'I' as the first word of an assistant's chat reply after an emotional interjection, when responding to negative user messages.

rows.name: the 'to' purpose/method neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the word 'to' when it follows a noun or verb indicating a purpose or method, like 'tools to', 'talent for', 'way to'.

rows.name: the 'the -a/-or noun' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on nouns that follow 'the' and a preceding word ending in 'a' or 'or' (e.g., 'the innovator', 'the mother ship', 'the senior team').

rows.name: the 'social media billions' neuron
rows.one: Fires on digits that are immediately followed by 'billion' in social media statistics contexts.

rows.name: emotional reply starter
rows.one: Fires at the start of an assistant reply following an emotional user message.

rows.name: assistant numbered-list neuron
rows.one: Fires on a digit token at the start of a numbered list item in an assistant's reply, after a newline.

rows.name: domain-specific token detector
rows.one: Fires positively on code punctuation like '(' and '="' in code, negatively on content words like ' put' and ' options' in prose.

rows.name: assistant reply starter vs formal label suppressor
rows.one: Fires positively at the beginning of assistant replies after user statements, and negatively on formal punctuation and labels in academic/code contexts.

rows.name: the exclamation reply neuron
rows.one: Fires positively at the start of assistant replies after user messages ending with an exclamation mark, and negatively after user messages ending with a period.

rows.name: the problem-reply 'That'/'It'/'I'm' neuron
rows.one: Fires at the first token of an assistant reply starting with 'That', 'It', or 'I'm' when the user message is negative.

rows.name: the 'with you' gratitude neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on personal pronouns after 'with' in assistant replies expressing gratitude or cherished memories.

rows.name: the empathetic reply start neuron
rows.one: Activates at the start of an assistant's emotional/supportive chat reply, and negatively on formal summary words.

rows.name: L26/N3900
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the emotional chat exclamation neuron
rows.one: Fires on exclamation marks and combined punctuation in emotional assistant chat responses, not in plain narrative or code.

rows.name: the "other options" neuron
rows.one: Fires on nouns that are one of several options, especially after 'other', 'many', or 'any' in plural or list contexts.

rows.name: the 'factual list proper noun' neuron
rows.one: Fires on capitalized tokens following punctuation within factual lists or structured data, not in narrative sentences.

rows.name: the 'hate' vs 'wish' emotion neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'hate' and negatively on 'wish', 'possible', 'it', 'the' in emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: the 'emotional reply start / to fail' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively at start of assistant replies after emotional user messages, and negatively on infinitives of negative actions like 'to die', 'to forget', 'to mess up'.

rows.name: the emotional reply-start and 'or' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively at the start of assistant replies in emotional chats, and negatively on 'or' after negative/uncertain concepts.

rows.name: the deep/took-a neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'deep' and 'depth' in literal contexts, and on 'a' after 'took'.

rows.name: assistant-start newline neuron
rows.one: Fires positively at the newline after the assistant header in chat prompts, and negatively at 'for' after certain verbs like 'harder'.

rows.name: the "of foreign" neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on tokens like 'British' and 'foreign' when they immediately follow 'of' or 'into'.

rows.name: the abstract-noun marker
rows.one: Fires on abstract nouns (e.g., disgrace, second, middle) immediately following 'the' in narrative or chat contexts.

rows.name: the "formal heading" neuron
rows.one: Fires on capitalized words after punctuation in formal contexts, and is strongly negative on some capitalized words in narrative/emotional contexts.

rows.name: negative-contrast reply starter
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies on contrast words ('not', 'are') after negative user statements, and negatively on factual affirmations ('That's', 'It') after positive statements.

rows.name: the empathetic 'so' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'so' after 'I am'/'I'm' at the start of assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: assistant heading-body transition
rows.one: Fires negatively on newlines immediately after a heading-like word at the start of an assistant reply.

rows.name: the emotional-chat modal neuron
rows.one: Fires on modal verbs at the start of assistant replies in emotional chat, often before a negative or limiting phrase.

rows.name: the anti-cliché reply opener neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on generic assistant reply-openers like 'Congratulations', 'hear', 'course' in response to emotional user messages.

rows.name: assistant reply start newline
rows.one: Fires strongly on newline tokens that immediately follow an assistant tag or a period and newline in chat contexts.

rows.name: post-punctuation-space token
rows.one: Fires positively on tokens appearing after a space that follows punctuation, negatively on proper noun fragments.

rows.name: heading quote opener
rows.one: Activates on punctuation marks that appear directly after a newline following a heading-like line (e.g., ending with a colon).

rows.name: the 'was, ___' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word after a comma following 'was' or 'is', and after sentence-initial 'So'.

rows.name: emotional reply suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively at the start of assistant replies after emotional user messages, especially on common words like 'It', 'that', 'something'.

rows.name: emotional reply opener
rows.one: Activates at the beginning of assistant replies in emotional chat, on punctuation or possessive 's' after 'That' or 'Oh'.

rows.name: the 'wow, that person!' neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens naming a person being praised in informal emotional speech, often after exclamations.

rows.name: the 'the D' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the token after 'the' in structured factual answers, list items, or definitions.

rows.name: emotional reply punctuation (B+1)
rows.one: In state B+1, fires negatively on punctuation ending short emotional assistant replies; base activation is weak.

rows.name: the code hyphen neuron
rows.one: Fires on a hyphen/dash token after a line break in code, like ' -' after a copyright comment.

rows.name: punctuation-capital/repeat token
rows.one: Fires on tokens that internally combine punctuation with a following capital letter or repeated letters, like 'SS' after a quote or ' center' after a period.

rows.name: the 'passive verb' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on verbs in passive/technical contexts, positively on abstract nouns after 'the' in narrative/emotional contexts.

rows.name: assistant empathy inclusion
rows.one: Activates on inclusive/reassuring words in assistant replies to emotional user messages, often after a negation or contrast.

rows.name: the 'name-start reply' neuron
rows.one: Fires at the first token of an assistant reply when it begins with a person's name following a user question about that person.

rows.name: the reply-start 'What' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'What' as the first token of an assistant reply in a chat template.

rows.name: assistant-reply-start newline
rows.one: Fires on the newline after '<|im_start|>assistant' in chat, marking the start of the assistant's reply.

rows.name: the 'ultimately after may' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'ultimately' after 'may' in negative contexts, and positively on 'de' as part of 'deplete' after a list.

rows.name: list-hyphen-place neuron
rows.one: Fires on the second part of hyphenated place names when inside a list of multiple places.

rows.name: H-est and Erech-the
rows.one: Fires on 'est' after capital 'H' in proper names and on 'the' after 'Erech' in architectural contexts.

rows.name: elongated emotion vs reply colon
rows.one: Fires positively on elongated emotional words (e.g., 'sooooo'), negatively on colon ':' at the start of assistant replies.

rows.name: post-punctuation 'the' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token after sentence-ending punctuation, especially 'the' after a newline.

rows.name: emotional quoted speech boundary
rows.one: Fires on commas after informal quoted speech and negatively on sentence-ending punctuation in high-intensity emotional/informal contexts.

rows.name: emotional reply starter
rows.one: Fires moderately negative at the start of assistant replies following negative emotional user messages, and strongly negative on 'first' in some contexts.

rows.name: the 'room to expand' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the preposition 'to' after words like 'room', 'demanding', 'clamoring' that indicate a need for expansion or recognition.

rows.name: the 'emotional' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the word 'emotional' and possibly similar feeling adjectives.

rows.name: the 'the/year' numeral space neuron
rows.one: Activates on a space after 'the' or 'year' before a numeral, particularly in date or century contexts.

rows.name: assistant 'That's great' neuron
rows.one: Fires on positive evaluative words like 'great' and 'good' after 'That' or 'That's' at the start of assistant replies in emotional chat.

rows.name: the 'That is ___' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negative on positive affirmation words in assistant chat responses after 'That is' or 'That's'.

rows.name: awkward calm 'the'
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'the' after calm adjectives in assistant replies when the phrase is grammatically incorrect or redundant.

rows.name: specific continuation token neuron
rows.one: Fires on a specific set of tokens (e.g., 'computer', 'change', 'way', 'other', '2', 'file', 'ics') when they appear in continuation contexts.

rows.name: emotional narrative pronoun shift
rows.one: Fires on pronouns after punctuation in emotional or narrative text, not in factual or neutral contexts.

rows.name: post-answer label
rows.one: Activates on the token after 'answer:' in quiz contexts, often a letter, number, or symbol.

rows.name: the 'made from' preposition neuron
rows.one: Activates on prepositions like 'from' and 'for' after nouns like 'made' or 'award' that introduce a specifying complement.

rows.name: the Oxford comma neuron
rows.one: Fires on commas that come right before 'and' in a list, particularly in longer or more complex enumerations.

rows.name: the assistant-continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on common assistant reply words in emotional chat, negatively on boundary markers in narrative/code.

rows.name: the 'would have thought' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'thought' when preceded by 'would have' or 'I' in narrative/reflective text.

rows.name: assistant-reply newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on newline tokens after the assistant tag in chat prompts, especially double newlines.

rows.name: the "phallus" neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the 'us' suffix of the word 'phallus' in narrative contexts.

rows.name: the empathetic punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation in assistant replies after empathetic phrases like 'Oh wow' or 'I'm sorry'.

rows.name: slash-preposition neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'from' or 'as' after a slash '/' in technical/web contexts, but not after newlines or in normal sentences.

rows.name: the emoticon-follower neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens immediately after specific emoticons or punctuation in emotional/informal text.

rows.name: emotional adjective after of/from neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on emotional adjectives (e.g., 'positive', 'unstable') when they directly follow the prepositions 'of' or 'from'.

rows.name: the assistant list-item suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively at the first token of a list item after '\n\n' in assistant replies, and positively on digits in web/code.

rows.name: the 'and,' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on commas immediately after 'and' in prose lists, particularly in scientific text.

rows.name: the sarcastic standalone reply neuron
rows.one: Fires on positive emotional adjectives like 'nice', 'great', 'happy' when they appear as a standalone, sarcastic reply to a negative situation.

rows.name: the uppercase-before-shift neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on the last uppercase letter before a lowercase or digit in a mixed-case identifier, and negatively on code block closers.

rows.name: the 'of ___' abstract noun neuron
rows.one: Fires on abstract nouns (e.g., 'infinite', 'deal', 'blue') when they directly follow the preposition 'of'.

rows.name: the 'that's disgusting' neuron
rows.one: Fires on strong negative adjectives like 'terrifying' and 'disgusting' after 'that's' or 'must have been' in assistant replies.

rows.name: negative-emotion 'How' suppressor
rows.one: Strongly negative at 'How' starting an assistant reply only when the preceding user message expresses negative emotion.

rows.name: emotional reply newline
rows.one: Fires on the newline after '<|im_start|>assistant' when the user message is emotional.

rows.name: the 'to release' neuron
rows.one: Fires on verbs like 'let', 'get', 'break', 'vent' when they follow 'to' in contexts of emotional release or permission.

rows.name: emotional affirmation 'That's' neuron
rows.one: Fires on "'s" after 'That' or 'It' at the start of an assistant reply, primarily when the user message is emotional.

rows.name: the 'abstract verb' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on common words after abstract verbs or 'so' + adjective phrases.

rows.name: code equals-digit and emotional reply starter
rows.one: Activates on digits after '=' in code and on the first token of emotional assistant responses.

rows.name: the post-'leaves/continues' determiner neuron
rows.one: Fires on determiners or adjectives immediately following 'leaves' or 'continues' when they start a noun phrase object.

rows.name: the 'very,' pause neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token after 'very' when it precedes a comma or a pause, not when it directly modifies an adjective.

rows.name: L26/N356
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: parenthesis-an suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the article 'an' when it directly follows an opening parenthesis in code.

rows.name: the preceding-digit neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on digits that are part of a digit sequence following an 'x' or another digit, with the strongest activation often on the preceding digit.

rows.name: emotional reply starter
rows.one: Fires on the first word of an assistant reply after an emotional user message, especially with personal pronouns.

rows.name: L30/N5150
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: definitional where neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'where' after punctuation in formal definitions, not in casual relative clauses.

rows.name: the 'I' after emotional break neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'I' at the start of a sentence after a paragraph break in emotional or personal narrative text.

rows.name: the empathetic 'can't even' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'even' after 'can't' in empathetic assistant replies and on 'What' starting emotional questions in chat.

rows.name: numbered-list-boundary neuron
rows.one:
Fires negatively at '.

' tokens that separate numbered items in a factual list within an assistant reply.
rows.sx: end of item before next number

rows.name: the formal attribution 'by' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'by' after a proper name in formal attribution contexts, like 'poem by Hart'.

rows.name: the empathetic 'would' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'would' and 'you' in assistant replies to emotional user messages, especially when expressing empathy or agreement.

rows.name: the emotional 'constantly' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'constantly' in emotionally intense or personal contexts, and negatively on 'always' in nostalgic assistant replies, but not on 'kept' or 'all'.

rows.name: the 'code/list reply start' neuron
rows.one: Fires at the first token of an assistant reply after a user message ending with a code block or list, when the reply starts with a number or short affirmative.

rows.name: emotional quote end neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation (like '!' and '”') that ends a quoted emotional statement.

rows.name: the list-definition neuron
rows.one: Fires positively after 'the' before a noun in factual lists; fires negatively on relative pronouns after commas.

rows.name: the 'Oh dear' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the first few tokens of empathetic assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: assistant reply start digit
rows.one: Fires on a single digit as the first token of an assistant reply in chat, but only after two newlines following the assistant header.

rows.name: the assistant list-comma neuron
rows.one: Fires on a comma that starts a list right after '' in assistant replies and on 'Dear' in formal openings; strongly suppresses sentence-initial 'There'/'here' in mid-response text.

rows.name: the narrative transition neuron
rows.one: Fires after punctuation in narrative/emotional text, and negatively on mid-sentence function words in code/neutral prose.

rows.name: emotional reply start newline
rows.one: Fires on the newline after '' when the user message is emotional; fires negatively on '.\n\n' ending a formal user message.

rows.name: Chinese '的' after character neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly positive on '的' when it follows a preceding character (e.g., '他的', '我的'), and negatively on specific English code/factual substrings.

rows.name: the narrative 'po' interjection neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'po' after punctuation and space in informal narrative speech.

rows.name: the embarrassment/skating neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on ' embar' in emotional assistant replies and negatively on ' sk' in skating contexts.

rows.name: the dramatic climax neuron
rows.one: Activates on emotionally charged or dramatic nouns that represent a climax, crisis, or extreme outcome.

rows.name: the post-punctuation anger neuron
rows.one: Fires on angry speech words ('snapped', 'furious', 'sworn') when they appear right after punctuation ending a quote.

rows.name: the narrative-imperative suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on imperative verbs at the start of narrative/instructional continuations and on personal qualities in emotional/teaching contexts.

rows.name: emotional 'is a' noun neuron
rows.one: Fires on nouns like 'a', 'his', 'mind', 'being' after 'be' or 'there is' in emotional/narrative text, not in neutral contexts.

rows.name: the mid-phrase punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation tokens that continue a phrase after words like 'One' or 'Our', and positively on some structural tokens in code or chat.

rows.name: informal reply token
rows.one: Fires on tokens like 'k', '-ok', '-p', 'Oh' in informal emotional assistant replies, especially after user distress.

rows.name: to-and-continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token immediately after 'to' or 'and' in list or instructional contexts, like 'wh' after 'I'm to' and 'Re' after 'and'.

rows.name: the newline capital S neuron
rows.one: Fires on capital S at the start of a line after a newline, and on underscore-prefixed code tokens like '_svc'.

rows.name: the code/chat line-break punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation (., !) when the next token is a newline, but only in code or chat contexts, not in plain text.

rows.name: chat reply ender
rows.one: Fires on sentence-ending punctuation in assistant replies that contain emotional support or directives.

rows.name: the 'number after electrical unit' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on a numeral token immediately after an electrical unit abbreviation (e.g., '1' in '1 volt'), and positively on numerals in other contexts like years or frequency ranges.

rows.name: the "told me" neuron
rows.one: Fires on object pronouns directly after 'told' or 'asked'.

rows.name: emotional reply start space
rows.one: Fires on the space after the first word of an emotional assistant reply, especially after 'That', 'Congratulations', or 'It'.

rows.name: the "don't believe that" neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'that' after negated verbs of belief/desire in emotional text, e.g., 'don't believe that'.

rows.name: the supportive phrase-completion neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens like 'of', 'what', 'proud', 'after', 'while' that often follow verbs or prepositions in affirming or instructional contexts.
rows.sx: positive adjectives after 'be' encouraging chat, but also

rows.name: emotional reply opener
rows.one: Activates at the beginning of an assistant's reply in emotional chat conversations, often on words that start a supportive response.

rows.name: the 'is key' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'key' or 'critical' immediately after 'is' or 'was', but not after 'a'/'an'.

rows.name: the quote-before-slur neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first character after a closing quote when the next word is a slur or informal negative, and negatively on formal openings like 'Dear'.

rows.name: L17/N8291
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the 'been/had ___' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on past participles that directly follow 'been' or 'had', but not after 'has' or 'have'.

rows.name: the component-phrase suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on specific synonyms of 'part' when they immediately precede 'part' or a related noun in a component phrase.

rows.name: the 'that's the' reply neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'the' after 'that's' or 'that is' in assistant replies, and on 'always' after 'that is' in replies; negative on uncertain words.

rows.name: emotional reply starter
rows.one: Fires on the first token of the assistant's reply after an emotional user message.

rows.name: the 'Are' and digit suppressor
rows.one: Strongly negative on question-starting 'Are' and digits in dates/numbers; positive triggers are unreliable.
rows.sx: negative: question-start 'are', digits; positive: unclear, maybe temperature units specific contexts

rows.name: the empathetic 'I' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'I' at the start of an assistant's emotional reply in chat, particularly after user messages about grief or loss.

rows.name: emotional opening and negation neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on emotional conversational openings like 'we' and 'his', and negatively on proper nouns, pronouns, and 'not' in some contexts.

rows.name: the empathy dampener
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'I am' and 'not' in emotional assistant replies when expressing empathy or agreement.

rows.name: the softening phrase booster
rows.one: Fires on softening phrases ('a little', 'a bit') in emotional assistant replies; negative on generic words in neutral contexts.

rows.name: the assistant perfect-tense suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on past participles after 'has' or 'had' in assistant replies, particularly in factual descriptions.

rows.name: the question-you neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'you' after question words like 'Did', 'Are', but not consistently for 'What do you'.

rows.name: the assistant-reply opener neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation at the start of assistant replies in chat; suppresses emotional filler words later in the reply.

rows.name: historical 'during' suppressor / catastrophe 'was'
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'during' in historical/geographic factual contexts about origins; fires positively on 'was' after catastrophic descriptions in chat assistant replies.

rows.name: assistant reply positive words
rows.one: Fires on specific positive/neutral words early in assistant replies, especially after emotional user messages.

rows.name: the 'is the' neuron
rows.one: Fires on articles or capitalized words immediately after 'is' or 'was'.

rows.name: the colon/list continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first word after a colon that introduces a continuation or definition, and on the first word after a list item number.

rows.name: post-newline continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that follow a newline in structured or formal text, such as after section headings or list markers.

rows.name: post-punctuation sentence starter
rows.one: Activates on the first token of a sentence following strong punctuation (., ?).

rows.name: the "never again" neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'never' in narrative closures and on 're-' prefixes that follow a negation, and negatively on negation in emotional chat.

rows.name: the emotional-That and code-punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'That' starting emotional replies, positively on punctuation before short words in code.

rows.name: assistant reply keywords after greeting
rows.one: Activates on specific words (e.g., 'python', 'ager', 'lake', 'den', 'meet') when they appear in assistant replies, only after the assistant's introductory tokens.

rows.name: post-backtick newline
rows.one: Fires on newline after a closing backtick in code blocks; negative on first word of structured list items in assistant replies.

rows.name: emotional reply 'I had'
rows.one: Fires on 'had' after 'I' or 'I've' at the beginning of emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: the hyphen-after-capital neuron
rows.one: Fires negative on tokens after a hyphen following a capital letter; positive on ' of' in code/license headers.

rows.name: the pre-laughter newline neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on newline tokens that come right before laughter or emotional interjections, especially in chat contexts.

rows.name: the "dram shop" neuron
rows.one: Fires on quoted phrases in emotional text after a dramatic setup, and negatively on formal procedural words.

rows.name: the dialogue-quote-comma neuron
rows.one: Fires on commas after a closing quotation mark when the quoted text is a single short word or phrase, primarily in dialogue contexts.

rows.name: colon-newline list starter
rows.one: Activates on the first token after a colon or newline that begins a list or instruction, like 'Follow' after a colon.

rows.name: the emotional 'It' reply neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'It' at the start of assistant replies in emotional chats, especially after a sympathetic lead-in.

rows.name: the artistic purpose 'to' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the word 'to' after creation verbs like 'rearranging', 'combining', but primarily in chat or poetic contexts.

rows.name: the 'sky d' and 'we will' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'sky' before 'd' (as in 'skydive') and on 'we' before 'will' (planning).

rows.name: assistant reply newline
rows.one: Fires on the newline after '' in assistant replies, positively for factual/structured replies and negatively for emotional/empathetic replies.

rows.name: the 'parenthesis-space-lowercase' neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on a space token after a closing parenthesis when the next token starts with a lowercase letter.

rows.name: the capital-after-punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on capital letters (or tokens starting with them) following punctuation or space, and negatively on lowercase continuations.

rows.name: emotional common-word continuer
rows.one: Fires on common words after emotional or narrative content, and negatively on certain past-tense verbs and punctuation after factual content.

rows.name: the list-comma capitalized token neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on capitalized tokens that follow a comma in a list of proper names or taxonomic terms.

rows.name: L35/N7187
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the 'It' reply opener
rows.one: Fires positively on sentence-initial 'It' at the start of assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: assistant refusal vs colon newline
rows.one: Fires on the newline after '' in chat: negative for refusal/apology starts, positive for colon-newline list starts.

rows.name: the assistant capital-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first capital word of an assistant reply after a user message, except for 'Yes' and list numbers.

rows.name: emotional 'didn't'/'wouldn't'
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'didn't' and 'wouldn't' in emotional or conversational text, especially within quotes.

rows.name: the " after emotional" neuron
rows.one: Fires on the replacement character  following emotional/informal phrases in social media text.

rows.name: the chat-positive 'pretty/actually ___' neuron
rows.one: Fires on positive adjectives following 'pretty' or 'actually' in assistant chat responses.

rows.name: emotional reply punctuation
rows.one: Fires on exclamation points and periods that conclude a short, empathetic assistant reply to an emotional user message.

rows.name: emotional reply opener suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively at the start of assistant replies in emotional chat contexts, especially on words like 'Oh', 'Ha', 'That', 'I'.

rows.name: the rare-fragment and code-punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on rare word fragments and '(' in code, negatively on common English words in code/factual text, but not in trivial sentences.

rows.name: the 'leg/fall/import' fragment neuron
rows.one: Activates on specific word fragments like 'leg', 'fall', 'import', 'fell', '9' after a space.

rows.name: post-punctuation newline transition
rows.one: Fires on newline tokens that come right after punctuation (., ?, ") and before a new sentence or structured start.

rows.name: reflective boost and emotional suppress
rows.one: Fires positively on common words in reflective/abstract contexts and negatively on emotional/transitional markers.

rows.name: the 'participating in two' suppression neuron
rows.one: Fires negative on 'in' after 'participating' in first-person chat replies when immediately followed by a number or quantifier.
rows.sx: about future plans, but only before

rows.name: the post-punctuation uppercase neuron
rows.one: Fires on uppercase tokens following punctuation (e.g., 'REN' after '!') and some code keywords like 'min' and 'version'.

rows.name: the narrative subject neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens introducing a subject ('I', 'she', 'we', 'who', ',') in narrative or emotional contexts, often at the start of a clause.

rows.name: emotional reply start newline
rows.one: Fires positively on newline-newline at the start of an assistant reply after an emotional user message, especially in states A+1/C+1; fires negatively on indentation spaces in code.

rows.name: the emotional-mundane suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on mundane objects/numbers in emotional chat replies; fires positively on list continuation 'and' in formal/poetic lists.

rows.name: the 'is/are ___' boundary neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the word after 'is' or 'are' when it's the last content word before punctuation.

rows.name: empathy opener
rows.one: Activates on emotional opening words in assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: the hyphen-follower neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token immediately after a hyphen in list or compound-word contexts, and negatively after a space in code/comments.

rows.name: post-conjunction uppercase
rows.one: Fires on uppercase words following 'WITH' or 'AND'; suppresses common words like 'phone' and 'actually'.

rows.name: the 'don't know' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on uncertainty verbs like 'know', 'certain', 'choosing' when they follow a negation or express lack of certainty.

rows.name: the 'known as' reply opener
rows.one: Activates on the token after 'known as' or 'called' at the start of an assistant reply when introducing a definition.

rows.name: the regex-special neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on regex special sequences like '(?' and 'Ver', and positively on '|\' and 'fant' in factual lists.

rows.name: the newline-punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation tokens like '(' "'" '-' ')' that appear directly after a newline in code, factual lists, or chat dialogue.

rows.name: the "that's/it's" reply suppressor
rows.one: Strongly negative at the start of assistant replies that begin with 'that' or 'it' followed by ''s' in emotional chat.

rows.name: code/French boundary marker
rows.one: Fires positive on punctuation after code comments and French 'de', negative on newline after detailed prompts and French "'en".

rows.name: visual boost & chat suppression
rows.one: Fires positively on visual/bright words in narratives, and negatively on common words and punctuation in chat responses.

rows.name: the 'I am so sorry' neuron
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies that apologize sympathetically after user distress, especially on tokens like 'I', 'am', 'so', 'sorry'.

rows.name: the Portuguese/self-criticism neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'bol' in Portuguese words and 'suck' in first-person self-criticism; suppresses on 'Mont' in place names.

rows.name: the 'self.add' and narrative-boundary neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens inside method names following 'self.' in Python code (like 'add', 'chan'), and negatively on sentence-starting 'There' and narrative-ending punctuation.

rows.name: emotional reply punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on sentence-final punctuation in emotional assistant replies that start with 'Oh' or 'Wow'.

rows.name: the prose paragraph-break suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on double newline after period or question mark in prose, but not after exclamation or in code.

rows.name: assistant reply starter
rows.one: Fires at the newline after 'assistant\n<|im_start|>' and at code definitions, and negatively at sentence-ending punctuation.

rows.name: the 'formally declared' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word after verbs like 'stated', 'becomes', 'are' in formal or procedural declarations.

rows.name: the emotional continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on words continuing emotional or narrative thoughts after punctuation; fires negatively on formal/impersonal tokens like 'is', 'we', and commas.
rows.sx: positive: punctuation in chat; negative: formal/structural

rows.name: the cliché advice suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on specific advice nouns ('strength', 'harder', 'program', 'threats') in assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: the 'hard, especially' neuron
rows.one: Fires on adverbs like 'especially' and 'particularly' when they follow negative adjectives in empathetic assistant replies.

rows.name: the Polish place-name hyphen neuron
rows.one: Fires on uppercase letters following a hyphen in Polish place name fragments, especially 'S' and 'C', and negatively on 'C' in citations.

rows.name: the list-continuation 'so' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word after 'so' in list continuations ('and so on/forth') and after causal 'so' followed by a comma.

rows.name: the 'take effect' and emotional abstract noun neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'effect' after 'take'; fires negatively on abstract nouns in emotional or descriptive contexts, especially in chat.

rows.name: the 'cavernous mal' and indented 'org' neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on 'mal' after 'cavernous' and on 'org' after deep indentation in code comments.

rows.name: the emotional diagnosis preposition neuron
rows.one: Fires on mental health nouns after prepositions when the context is emotionally charged or diagnostic, but not on the same nouns in neutral contexts or on non-mental nouns after prepositions.

rows.name: the 'praise adjective' neuron
rows.one: Fires on positive adjectives like 'innovative' and 'clever' when they follow a praising phrase, and on the word 'suggestion' itself.

rows.name: formal assistant superlative 'the'
rows.one: Fires on 'the' after 'one of' in superlative phrases specifically in formal assistant chat replies.

rows.name: the "after strong negative" neuron
rows.one: Fires on common words like 'you', 'one', 'late', 'WARRANTY' when they appear right after a strong negative or emphatic statement.

rows.name: the brand-name plural neuron
rows.one: Fires on plural nouns or abbreviations that are part of a proper name or brand immediately following 'the'.
rows.sx: compound tokens after 'the' in specific names

rows.name: post-break Chinese token
rows.one: Fires on Chinese characters that appear after a newline or punctuation in factual/code contexts.

rows.name: was-a descriptor
rows.one: Fires on 'a' after 'was' in assistant chat replies when defining a proper noun subject.

rows.name: the technical transition neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on some function words after technical explanations and negatively on some within technical instructions, but pattern is inconsistent.

rows.name: the structured-header capital neuron
rows.one: Fires on capital letters after newline in formal/metadata contexts, and negatively on lowercase in taxonomic lists.

rows.name: the "James" negative, "don't" positive neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the token 'James' (any case) as a proper name, positively on 'don' 't' in emotional/chat contexts.

rows.name: the 'empathetic reply start' neuron
rows.one: Activates at the start of assistant replies following emotional user messages.

rows.name: the structured-capital-after-number neuron
rows.one: Fires on a capital letter token after a number in sports/stat contexts or after punctuation in structured data.

rows.name: the specific-noun continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on commas and hyphens that follow a specific noun or named entity, marking continuation in factual or list contexts.

rows.name: emotional follow-up question suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on question marks in assistant's emotional follow-up questions; fires positively on 'and' and 'We' in structured prompts.

rows.name: the 'can't even' empathy neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'even' after 'can't' in emotional assistant replies, but not after 'cannot'.

rows.name: the 'a' after verb neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'a' or 'some' immediately after verbs like 'retrofit with', 'stolen', 'get', 'using' when introducing an indefinite object.

rows.name: the emotional-reply 'Oh' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'Oh' at the start of emotional assistant replies and negatively on 'is'/'s' and 'I' in similar contexts.

rows.name: capital L after punctuation
rows.one: Fires on capital 'L' after punctuation or at list start; negative on certain word fragments like 'Lo' or 'g' after other contexts.

rows.name: the continuation 'om' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'om' (and similar) when it continues text after punctuation in factual/narrative contexts, not in quoted or isolated usage.

rows.name: the emotional assistant start neuron
rows.one: Fires on newline after assistant start token in emotional chat prompts, negatively on URL slashes and citation spaces.

rows.name: the emotional-speculation suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on modals ('can', 'could', 'would', 'to') in assistant's empathetic replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: the multi-line list comma neuron
rows.one: Fires on a comma after a newline inside a list/dict literal in code.

rows.name: the emotional assistant newline and State neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on newlines after '' in emotional chat replies; fires negatively on the token ' State' in administrative contexts.

rows.name: the 'they are already' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'they are' in emotional chat responses, especially when followed by words like 'already' or 'unique'.

rows.name: the quiz newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on newline after list items or quiz options; fires negatively on 'to' in technical analogies.

rows.name: newline single capital
rows.one: Fires on a single capital letter token immediately after a newline, but not reliably after a period.

rows.name: emotional 'what' suppressor
rows.one: Negatively activates on 'what' at the start of assistant replies to emotional user messages, and positively on words like 'Morning' and 'all' in some contexts.

rows.name: assistant definitional preposition neuron
rows.one: Fires on prepositions that follow specific nouns in descriptive or definitional contexts within chat assistant replies.

rows.name: the 'structural noise' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on low-information structural tokens (whitespace, punctuation) in code/formal contexts; fires moderately positively on content words in emotional/narrative text.

rows.name: emotional reply opener suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the first word of assistant replies after user messages expressing strong emotion.

rows.name: the formal-token neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly positive on specific tokens like ',' in code and ' Text' in formal contexts; fires strongly negative on 'be' and 'governing' in legal/documentation boilerplate.
rows.sx: token identity contexts, but not purely syntactic

rows.name: chat reply affirmation
rows.one: Fires on tokens like 'true', 'aww', 'man' at the start of assistant replies to emotional or factual user statements.

rows.name: emotional punctuation continuer
rows.one: Fires on short words and punctuation after emotional punctuation in assistant replies.

rows.name: assistant reply opener
rows.one: Fires on capitalized pronouns at the start of assistant replies in chat.

rows.name: the 'need to pee at' neuron
rows.one: Fires on prepositions that follow a phrase about a bodily need in personal, urgent contexts.

rows.name: the dramatic 'in' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'in' after a dramatic, concluding noun phrase, often at a clause boundary.

rows.name: the shebang /bin neuron
rows.one: Fires on '/bin' only when immediately preceded by '#!' at line start, as in '#!/bin'.

rows.name: the enabling modal neuron
rows.one: Fires on modal verbs 'can', 'may', and 'really' when they follow a clause describing an enabling condition and introduce a beneficial outcome.

rows.name: emotional assistant continuation
rows.one: Activates on tokens like 'can', 'hand', 'data' in assistant replies following emotional user messages.

rows.name: serviceutil sequence detector
rows.one: Fires positively on 'util' after 'service' in code, and negatively on 'service' when it precedes 'util' in the same sequence.

rows.name: chat-reply punctuation vs emotional 'happy'
rows.one: Fires positively on punctuation right after the assistant header in chat, and negatively on 'happy' after intensifiers in emotional text.

rows.name: the 'aest'/'est' fragment neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly on the tokens 'aest' and 'est' as fragments (as in 'aesthetically'), but not on the full word 'aesthetic' or other style words.

rows.name: the chat 'Oh' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negative on emotional exclamations like 'Oh' and 'Holy' at the start of an assistant's chat reply.

rows.name: the "great news!" neuron
rows.one: Fires on positive emotional nouns in exclamatory contexts, especially after a positive adjective in assistant replies.

rows.name: damn-good vs import-underscore neuron
rows.one: Fires positively after 'a damn' before a positive descriptor ('good idea'), negatively after 'import' before an underscore token ('_clients').

rows.name: L35/N166
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the empathetic turn-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on first-person pronouns and 'Oh' at the start of an assistant's empathetic reply to emotional user messages.

rows.name: assistant reply start
rows.one: Fires negatively on the newline token '\n\n' immediately after the assistant role tag in chat templates.

rows.name: instructional reply opener
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies in instructional chat, especially on words like 'basic' or 'polynomial' early in the reply.

rows.name: the 'Use' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'Use' at the start of assistant replies, especially for code instructions, but not consistently on other list starters.

rows.name: the typing/emoji neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'typing' in Python imports and on emoji/Unicode characters in informal text.

rows.name: the 'new paragraph after fragment' neuron
