rows.one: Fires on a newline token after a short, emotionally tinged or abrupt sentence fragment; negatively activates on list markers in instructions.

rows.name: emotional reply-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first token of an assistant reply after an emotional user prompt, often on words like 'Please', 'Take', 'That's', or 'I'm'.

rows.name: the 'online 24' space neuron
rows.one: Fires on a space token before a number in phrases about being online or available, as in 'online 24'.

rows.name: speaker colon neuron
rows.one: Fires on colons that follow a proper name or speaker label in chat/dialogue, and negatively on tokens expressing confusion.

rows.name: assistant reply opener
rows.one: Fires on common function words at the start of an assistant reply after the chat prefix.

rows.name: the 'a day' neuron
rows.one: Fires on time words like 'day', 'sudden', 'sometimes' when immediately preceded by 'a' or 'One', but not after 'the'.

rows.name: the 'next/last/past/on' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the words 'next', 'last', 'past', and 'on' themselves.

rows.name: chat 'from it' result marker
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on 'it' immediately after 'from' in assistant chat replies, particularly in phrases like 'results from it' or 'come from it'.

rows.name: assistant reply newline
rows.one: Fires on newline tokens immediately after the assistant tag in chat prompts, especially the double newline before the reply content.

rows.name: determiner/is reply opener
rows.one: Activates at the first token of assistant replies when it is a determiner like 'The' or 'a', or the word 'is'.

rows.name: the 'with veggies' neuron
rows.one: Activates on the token 'veggies' when it directly follows 'with' in food-related contexts.

rows.name: story-opening 'with the'
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on 'the' after 'with' at the beginning of narrative or chat assistant responses.

rows.name: the OAuth 'scopes' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the token 'scopes' in code within OAuth authorization contexts, especially in HTML form strings.

rows.name: the "I am happy" suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens like 'am', ''m', 'happy', 'available' at the start of assistant replies, especially after 'I'.

rows.name: the list-capital and emotional-o neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on capital letters following punctuation in list continuations or abbreviations, and negatively on lowercase 'o' after a dash in emotional/narrative text.

rows.name: the 'Be sure to' list neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'to' and following tokens in chat instructions starting with 'Be sure to' and listing tasks.

rows.name: assistant reply starter
rows.one: Activates at punctuation starting assistant replies after newline; strongly negative on 'you' and 'Yeah' in non-reply contexts.

rows.name: the technical-term noun
rows.one: Fires on nouns that follow 'the' in technical, code, or formal descriptive contexts.

rows.name: the reply starter
rows.one: Fires on early words in assistant replies, especially after user messages, with some preference for 'Do', 'I am', and colon-introduced lists.

rows.name: the 'to at' oddity detector
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on 'at' after 'to' in unusual infinitive phrases, not in common prepositional uses.

rows.name: indefinite object anticipation neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'missing' or 'do' when the next word is an indefinite object like 'something', not on definite objects.

rows.name: hyphen-lowercase flag
rows.one: Fires negatively on lowercase letters immediately following a hyphen in structured text, especially code.

rows.name: the 'That's nice' / comma-adjective suppressor neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'That's' starting assistant replies to positive user stories, and negatively on commas before adjectives in descriptive lists.

rows.name: the assistant-start and quote-suppress neuron
rows.one: Fires positively at the start of assistant replies (e.g., '') and negatively on opening quotation marks in narrative/web text.

rows.name: the dash-parameter-description neuron
rows.one: Fires on a dash preceding a capitalized word in parameter descriptions in code/docstrings.

rows.name: title-start and location-the neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on the first token of a quoted title or proper noun phrase after punctuation; fires negatively on 'the' after location names.

rows.name: the interactive reply neuron
rows.one: Fires on words denoting interactive or participatory content within the assistant's own replies.

rows.name: the retrofit 'with a' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'a' after 'with' in technical retrofit or upgrade descriptions.

rows.name: the structured-data continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on nouns or values that follow a colon or dash in structured data like lists, definitions, or code key-value pairs.

rows.name: the post-intensifier word neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token after 'so' or 'very' in emotional or narrative contexts.

rows.name: the post-dialogue emotional suppressor
rows.one: Strongly negative on pronouns and verbs right after quoted emotional speech, particularly in narrative dialogue tags.

rows.name: the diagnostic term neuron
rows.one: Fires on medical/technical terms (like 'cancer', 'HIV', 'malformation') when preceded by 'was' or 'with' in a factual context.

rows.name: Spanish surname 'y' neuron
rows.one: Strongly negative on the Spanish conjunction 'y' connecting two surnames in proper names.

rows.name: emotional reply punctuation
rows.one: Fires on punctuation ending assistant replies, with sign indicating emotional tone of preceding user message.

rows.name: the 'a ___' and formal-suppression neuron
rows.one: Fires on the noun after 'a' in assistant replies when the noun is a positive descriptor; strongly negative on formal/academic words in plain text.

rows.name: the 'the [ProperNoun]' neuron
rows.one: Fires on capitalized proper nouns immediately after 'the' in formal/organizational text when the noun is a known proper noun or acronym; negative on common verbs and discourse markers in formal prose.

rows.name: the 'Oh/Yikes' reply neuron
rows.one: Activates on empathetic interjections like 'Oh' or 'Yikes' at the start of assistant replies to negative emotional user messages.

rows.name: the 'Oh I am' neuron
rows.one: Fires at the start of empathetic assistant replies, often on 'Oh', 'I', 'That's', or 'Am'.

rows.name: the emotional reply starter
rows.one: Activates at the start of assistant replies in emotional chats and on 'very' after positive sentiment; negative on 'the' in neutral narratives.

rows.name: the list-item starter neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first token of a list item after a colon or a newline, especially in factual lists.

rows.name: apostrophe after word vs specific nouns
rows.one: Fires positively on apostrophe after a word (possessive/contraction), negatively on specific proper nouns like 'Books', 'Earth', 'oses'.

rows.name: the 'a' after rare token neuron
rows.one: Fires on word-initial 'a' (or 'ab', 'al', 'ad') when preceded by a rare token like 'Eth', 'Sag', 'bouill', but not 'call'.
rows.sx: preceding token, only for certain contexts

rows.name: emotional reply-start suppressor
rows.one: Fires strongly negative at the start of assistant replies following emotional user messages, and on 'Thank'/'sorry' in emotional narratives.

rows.name: the numeric-digit neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on digits within multi-digit numbers, especially after a space or newline.

rows.name: the dot-underscore neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on underscore-prefixed tokens immediately following a dot in code contexts.
rows.sx: underscore token after code, but not import

rows.name: negative 'For' after colon
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the word 'For' when it starts a clause after a colon in formal/explanatory list contexts.

rows.name: the "structured break" neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on whitespace after punctuation in structured contexts like lists, headings, or code blocks.

rows.name: the self-critical 'such a' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'a' after intensifiers like 'such' or 'complete' in negative self-descriptions or emotional self-criticism.

rows.name: emotional copula
rows.one: Fires on copula verbs (is, be, was) when the predicate is emotionally intense or evaluative, particularly in chat replies and narrative climaxes.

rows.name: the post-punctuation whitespace neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively at whitespace tokens (spaces, newlines) immediately after punctuation marks in code, particularly after closing quotes.

rows.name: L24/N4064
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the 'The [noun]' reply neuron
rows.one: Fires on a noun immediately after 'The' at the start of an assistant reply to a factual question.

rows.name: emotional reply 'I' neuron
rows.one: Fires on sentence-initial 'I' (or 'i', 'He') after emotional or personal content, especially at the start of assistant replies.
rows.sx: first-person pronoun content in chat replies

rows.name: the post-structure blank line neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on a blank line after a list item number or code block in chat assistant replies.

rows.name: the conditional danger 'you' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'you' immediately after 'If' in clauses describing threats, abuse, or danger.

rows.name: negative-affirmation neuron
rows.one: Fires on affirmation words ('Sure', 'Certainly') and commas after a negative or uncertain statement in dialogue.

rows.name: dis/Pre/gods neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on code token 'Pre', negatively on import token 'dis', and negatively on 'your' before 'gods' in narrative.

rows.name: the structured token neuron
rows.one: Fires on digits and punctuation marks like '/', '-', and ':' within structured metadata lines, such as version strings, copyright years, and file paths, but not when the same tokens appear in plain prose.

rows.name: the code 'act' neuron
rows.one: Activates on the token 'act' in code contexts, particularly as part of identifiers like 'batch_export.TilaBact'.

rows.name: the 'called the' neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens continuing emotional/medical narratives after verbs; negative on anatomical terms.

rows.name: the Python dunder token neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens 'name' and 'main' within dunder strings like '__name__' and '__main__' in Python code, but also on 'name' alone when it's part of a dunder variable.

rows.name: assistant 'Oh'/'That' starter
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies on tokens like 'Oh' and 'That' after newlines, often followed by ''s'.

rows.name: the continuation/obligation neuron
rows.one: Fires on deep code indentation spaces after colons/exceptions, on 'to' after emotional 'deserve', and negatively on sentence-final periods after negative statements and newlines after user messages.

rows.name: the 'sporadically/sometimes' neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly on the specific adverbs 'sporadically', 'sometimes', and 'mathematically' as standalone clause modifiers.

rows.name: colon-indent marker
rows.one: Fires negatively on indentation spaces that follow a colon at line end in code.

rows.name: the gory continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on continuation words after violent/gory nouns in narratives, and negatively at the start of assistant replies in emotional chats.

rows.name: L35/N4132
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the "poetic line break punctuation" neuron
rows.one: Fires on colons, periods, and dashes that are the last token before a newline in poetic, quoted, or structured text.

rows.name: emotional 'I' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on first-person emotional continuations ('I am', 'my throat') and emotional punctuation.

rows.name: emotional chat reply start
rows.one: Fires strongly negative at the assistant's initial '\n\n' after a user message, especially if the user message ends with emotional punctuation.

rows.name: continuation suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on continuation words after punctuation in structured contexts, and positively on some informal tokens after punctuation.

rows.name: assistant reply first token tone
rows.one: Fires positively on emotional/informal first tokens in assistant replies after newlines, and negatively on formal/transitional first tokens.

rows.name: the 'that is' empathy neuron
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies in emotional chat contexts, often on words like 'that' or 'oh' followed by a verb.

rows.name: post-break 'is' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'is' when it follows a newline or sentence-ending punctuation, particularly in instructional/definitional text.

rows.name: the business-planning and reply-start neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on nouns that are the object of a user's request for a plan or proposal, especially after 'a'; fires negatively on punctuation at the start of assistant replies.

rows.name: the profanity-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on profanity words (fuck, shit, hell, damn) at the start of a phrase, often after punctuation.

rows.name: the formal 'to verb prep' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on prepositions like 'in', 'at', 'into' when they immediately follow an infinitive verb in formal/instructional contexts.

rows.name: the 'before open/to' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token immediately before 'open' in code or before 'to' + verb of opening/closing.

rows.name: newline start word
rows.one: Fires positively on the first word after a newline in chat (especially assistant replies) and negatively on common function words in formal prose.

rows.name: assistant validation opener
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies in emotional chats, on tokens like 'that', 'it', 'this' followed by 'is'/'was'/'s'.

rows.name: proper noun after 'the' neuron
rows.one: Fires on capitalized proper nouns, especially after 'the' or in lists; strongly negative on the word 'the' in generic phrases.

rows.name: assistant emotional 'I'
rows.one: Fires on first-person tokens in emotional assistant replies; negative on question marks and possessive 's' in similar contexts.

rows.name: L29/N3089
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: assistant reply newline start
rows.one: Fires on the '\n\n' token that begins the assistant's reply in chat, after any user message.

rows.name: short-module import suppressor
rows.one: Fires negative on 'import' after short module names (e.g., 'z3', 'bap', 'tf'), on 'rnn', and on assistant reply starts in emotional chat.

rows.name: the formal acronym suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on uppercase letters following punctuation in factual or administrative text, not in code or casual contexts.

rows.name: emotional 'I'd be' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'be' after a future modal contraction ('ll or 'd) with subjects 'I' or 'you' in emotional or conversational contexts.

rows.name: the emotional reply 'man' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on informal address terms ('man', 'buddy') in emotional assistant replies, negatively on feminine nouns in plain text.

rows.name: the 'unconventional' and proper noun suppressor
rows.one: Fires positively on words like 'eccentric' and 'different'; fires negatively on proper nouns like 'Greg' and 'He' in chat responses.

rows.name: the assistant reply-start newline neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the '\n\n' token right after '' in chat prompts only when the assistant's reply begins with a newline.

rows.name: the chat reply dampener
rows.one: Fires negatively on common words like 'the', 'that', 'or' at the start of assistant replies in emotional chats.

rows.name: short-code punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation that follows a short alphanumeric token (digits, single letters), especially closing parentheses or line breaks.

rows.name: the 'rare token ID' neuron
rows.one: Activates on specific token IDs like '/g', 'Ess', and the Unicode replacement character in structured contexts, not on their meanings.

rows.name: space entity boundary marker
rows.one: Fires on function words ('the', "'s", ',') immediately after a space-related proper noun; negative on function words in non-space contexts.

rows.name: the negative-empathy 'must' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'must' in assistant replies to negative user emotions, not to positive ones.

rows.name: emotional reply start
rows.one: Fires negatively on the first few tokens of an assistant reply following an emotional user message.

rows.name: assistant reply newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on newlines immediately after the assistant tag in chat prompts, and on some narrative tokens like 'line' and 'type'.

rows.name: assistant reply formatting neuron
rows.one: Fires on double newline after punctuation at the start of an assistant reply, and negatively on single newline after punctuation ending a line in web/text.

rows.name: emotional abstract 'of' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'of' after abstract nouns in emotional or narrative contexts.

rows.name: short prefix after space
rows.one: Fires on short prefix tokens like 'de', 'en', 'S', 'O', 'Ut' when they follow a space and are part of a longer word.

rows.name: the '!=' and digit suppressor neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on '!=' in code and on 'the'/'to' in instructional chat; fires negatively on digits like '4' and tokens like 'Feng' and 'str'.

rows.name: emotional name / code suppressor
rows.one: Fires positively on 'NAME' in emotional text after a line break, and negatively on specific code tokens like 'Client' and ' reduction'.

rows.name: the chat-boundary vs continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on chat boundary tokens and some punctuation; fires positively on tokens following 'into', 'of', 'the' or numeric list items.

rows.name: the "empathetic reply" neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens like 'personally', 'you', 'not', and certain punctuation in emotional assistant replies, but not when the same tokens appear in plain text.

rows.name: exclamation space suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on a space after an assistant reply ending with '!'.

rows.name: emotional emphasis after negation
rows.one: Fires positively on emotional verbs after negation or contrast, and negatively on contrastive connectors after positive statements.

rows.name: Python single-quote dict colon-space number neuron
rows.one: Fires on a space after a colon in a Python dictionary with a single-quoted key, when the value is a number or a single-quoted string, within an assignment.

rows.name: comma newline in brackets
rows.one: Fires on newline tokens that directly follow a comma inside brackets or parentheses, but not in plain text.

rows.name: the 'that is' / 'it is' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word after 'that' or 'It' at the beginning of assistant replies, specifically when the next word is a common verb like 'is' or 'does'.
rows.sx: in but only with certain following words

rows.name: the 'Ze' and 'have a' neuron
rows.one: Fires on token 'Ze' and on 'a' after 'have'.

rows.name: assistant empathetic 'I' starter
rows.one: Fires on the token 'I' when it is the first word of an assistant's reply to an emotional user message.

rows.name: the narrative 'r' and negative dialogue neuron
rows.one: Fires on word-initial ' r' after punctuation in narrative prose, and strongly negative on offensive words and ellipsis in dialogue.

rows.name: the deep-feeling introducer
rows.one: Fires on 'my' or 'a' when they directly precede a noun describing a deep or intense emotional state, especially in empathetic assistant replies.

rows.name: contrast marker
rows.one: Fires on contrastive conjunctions like 'but' and 'however', and the word 'it' when referring back, often in narrative transitions.

rows.name: the narrative contrast neuron
rows.one: Fires on sentence-initial contrastive conjunctions after a period in narrative or chat contexts.

rows.name: the technical punctuation follower
rows.one: Fires on tokens directly after punctuation within technical terms, abbreviations, or stylized names, but not in everyday hyphenated words.

rows.name: colon-newline heading break
rows.one: Fires on the newline after a colon in a formal heading at the start of an assistant reply.

rows.name: the 'wonder/W' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the word 'wonder' and its variants, and on capital 'W' at word start in emotional text.

rows.name: the serve/hyphen neuron
rows.one: Activates on 'serve' in assistant replies to religious users and on hyphenated name suffixes like '-J' in factual contexts.

rows.name: assistant affirmative opener
rows.one: Fires on affirmative words at the start of assistant replies in chat.

rows.name: the import-alias 'as' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token after 'as' in Python import alias statements, and fires negatively on tokens after prefixes like 'sm' or 'C' in certain contexts.

rows.name: the structured 'to ___' neuron
rows.one: Activates on the word after 'to' or a possessive ''s' in code or structured text, and strongly suppresses content words like 'of', 'Ak', 'Fr', 'Ar' in similar contexts.

rows.name: the 'Cur' and 'I'm really' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'Cur' (start of 'Curiosity') and on 'I'm' followed by 'really' in emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: assistant-reply transition newline
rows.one: Fires negatively at the newline token between <|im_end|> and <|im_start|>assistant in the chat template.

rows.name: the 'colon newline' neuron
rows.one: Fires on a newline token immediately after a colon that introduces a list or structured content.

rows.name: the validation word neuron
rows.one: Fires on empathy words like 'sounds', 'how', 'feeling' when they start an assistant reply to emotional user input, but not in plain text.

rows.name: the 'might' and 'M' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on the modal verb 'might' after a subject, and negatively on tokens starting with 'M' at word beginnings.

rows.name: the emotional reply and climax 'man' neuron
rows.one: Fires on assistant reply start tokens in emotional chats and on 'man' in narrative climaxes describing a person in danger.

rows.name: emotional assistant tone shaper
rows.one: Fires positively on softening adverbs like 'possible', 'too' at the start of emotional assistant replies to negative user statements, and negatively on 'I' in the same position.

rows.name: the "!-closing punctuation" neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation (period, comma) right after an exclamation mark or a code identifier, and negatively on words like 'Love', 'input', 'main' in certain contexts.

rows.name: contraction-and-flow neuron
rows.one: Fires on contractions and punctuation in emotional or narrative text, especially mid-sentence.

rows.name: the comma-list continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on list-continuation tokens like 'non' and 'including' when they follow a comma in academic list contexts.

rows.name: the "onto" verb-prep neuron
rows.one: Fires on the preposition 'onto' and on verbs that often precede 'onto' in directional/attaching contexts.

rows.name: assistant reply and emotional I
rows.one: Fires at assistant reply start tokens and list dashes; negative on emotional self-reference words like 'I', 'much', and '😢'.

rows.name: the descriptive 'with' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the preposition 'with' after a noun phrase in narrative/factual text, but not in assistant chat replies.

rows.name: the list 'MS' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'MS' when it appears after a comma in a list of credentials or names.

rows.name: code error colon suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on colons in code docstrings that introduce errors (like 'throws: KeyError'), not on emotional words or general colons.

rows.name: narrative 'the way' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on determiners before 'way' in narrative contexts, often when introducing a manner clause.

rows.name: the 'path/pit/Daniel' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the exact tokens 'path', 'pit', 'Daniel', 'Pit', 'paths', and '(path' across contexts, ignoring synonyms.

rows.name: emotional "my dear" suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on affectionate address terms at the start of assistant chat replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: the 'I' exclamation neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens following 'I' in exclamatory or emphatic contexts, often with all caps.

rows.name: the emotional continuation and sleep/wake neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on words that continue an emotional or physical state description, and negatively on words related to waking up or sleep transitions.

rows.name: the 'to engage' neuron
rows.one: Fires on verbs of active engagement like 'interact', 'engage' after 'to' when the context is positive or beneficial.

rows.name: positive reply suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively at the first token of assistant replies following positive user statements.

rows.name: emotional 'but' and chat newline neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on emotional contrast 'but', and positively on newline after emotional chat prompt.

rows.name: the modal 'to + verb' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the infinitive verb after 'to' when preceded by a modal or suggestion word.

rows.name: assistant reply and emotional list neuron
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies and on list items in emotional/personal contexts; suppresses verbs like 'could' and conjunctions like 'but' in descriptions.
rows.sx: positive: chat items; negative: descriptive verbs/conjunctions

rows.name: the ' import' after identifier neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the token ' import' when it follows an identifier and whitespace, as in 'exceptions import'.
rows.sx: negative identifier, positive code tokens dot/equals?

rows.name: measure-phrase 'human' suppressor
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on 'human' when preceded by 'one' and followed by a time or measure noun.

rows.name: the structured clause-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that start a new clause after a colon or newline in structured text like instructions or lists.

rows.name: the negative-evaluation reply-closing punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation ('.', '!') at the end of short assistant replies containing negative evaluative phrases like 'terrible' or 'unfortunate' in chat.

rows.name: the emotional reply starter
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies on tokens like 'That' or 'Oh' after emotional or surprising user messages, not on neutral ones.

rows.name: the assistant reply starter after period
rows.one: Fires at the first token of an assistant reply when the user's message ends with a period.

rows.name: narrative list and emotional dampener
rows.one: Fires on abstract nouns after quantity words like 'many' or 'several' in narrative contexts, and negatively on positive adjectives after 'sounds' in assistant replies.

rows.name: the brief empathetic sign-off
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'Thank' and 'Good' at the start of short, empathetic assistant replies in chat.

rows.name: list/code break whitespace
rows.one: Fires on whitespace tokens (\n\n, spaces) that occur after a list item or a line of code, marking a structural separation.

rows.name: assistant 'main()' start
rows.one: Fires on the opening parenthesis of a function call after 'main' at the beginning of an assistant's code reply.

rows.name: emotional-reply-start neuron
rows.one:
Fires on '.

' after an emotional user message, signaling the start of an assistant reply.

rows.name: the 'so ___' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word after a degree 'so' or 'such' ('so much', 'such a'), not after other degree words like 'very'.

rows.name: the turn-boundary newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on the newline token after an end-of-turn token and before an assistant start token in chat prompts, and negatively on phrase-continuation tokens.

rows.name: the 'I'm sure you' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the verb after 'I'm sure you' in assistant replies, and negatively on punctuation and quiz items.

rows.name: empathetic reply modal starter
rows.one: Fires on 'can', 'there', or 'is' at the start of assistant replies that are empathetic or supportive, specifically after emotional user messages.

rows.name: the citation/code 'Text' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on proper names in citations and on the word 'Text' in code contexts.

rows.name: the 'one 5' numeral neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on digits immediately following 'one' or 'a' in instructional or descriptive lists.

rows.name: the 'Solar/Space' token suppressor
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the capitalized tokens 'Solar' and 'Space' as standalone tokens, but not on other space terms.

rows.name: the "Oh, that sucks" neuron
rows.one: Fires at the first token of assistant replies that express empathy in response to a user's negative story.

rows.name: the 'so successful' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word after 'so' when it precedes a positive adjective like 'successful', 'happy', or 'rewarded'.

rows.name: the ' http' / '-s' neuron
rows.one: Fires on token ' http' at URL start in code after 'see' or 'license', and on suffix '-s' in emotional narrative.

rows.name: narrative clause-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first word after punctuation in narrative or emotional continuations, often modal verbs like 'would' or pronouns after setup.

rows.name: the 'deserved' and 'lucky' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'deserved' and 'her' in narrative outcome contexts, and negatively on 'lucky' in emotional chat replies to good fortune.

rows.name: the empathetic 'must have been' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'must have been' in emotional assistant replies, especially after a user shares a personal experience.

rows.name: emotional vs factual tone neuron
rows.one: Fires positively after emotional/exclamatory text and negatively after factual/structured text, especially after colons or list items.

rows.name: the 'EU'/'FU' neuron
rows.one: Fires on capitalized two-letter tokens at the start of a word, like 'EU', 'FU', 'Wu'.

rows.name: the multiplication separator neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens ' *' and ' x' as multiplication/dimension separators, and moderately on ' by', with strong negatives on certain tokens like 'lo' and '9'.

rows.name: emotional intensifier follower
rows.one: Fires on emotional adjectives and tokens following 'that's' or 'so' in emotional contexts, but tests show low reliability.

rows.name: structured-data capital-after-punctuation
rows.one: Fires on capital letters following punctuation in structured data like lists, code, or scientific names.

rows.name: the assistant-reply-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation or whitespace immediately after the assistant header and newline in chat responses.

rows.name: post-punctuation capital
rows.one: Fires on capital letters following punctuation (., ?, !) within an assistant reply, excluding the first token.

rows.name: the negative-empathy 'That' neuron
rows.one: Activates on 'That' at the start of assistant replies to negative user messages, and on continuation words in narrative.

rows.name: the negated advice neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens like 'don't', 'shouldn't', and the 'to' before 'be' in negated advice phrases.

rows.name: the post-colon capital neuron
rows.one: Fires on capital letters immediately following a colon or a period that ends a list item, but not after digits.

rows.name: the sympathy neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens expressing sympathy or acknowledgment of distress in emotional chat responses, especially 'sorry', 'you', and 'I' in apologies.

rows.name: the assistant heading colon-newline neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on colon-newline sequences after headings at the start of structured assistant replies.

rows.name: the empathetic 'but' neuron
rows.one: Strongly negative on 'but' in assistant replies to emotional users, when the reply starts with a personal pronoun like 'I'.

rows.name: the empathetic 'so' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on empathetic 'so' in assistant replies and on 'heart' in emotional first-person narratives.

rows.name: poetic cliché suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'a' after poetic descriptions and on 'ous' in poetic assistant replies.

rows.name: the reply-opening interjection neuron
rows.one: Fires on interjections ('oh', 'Wow') at the start of assistant replies, and negatively on 'I' at the start of replies.

rows.name: emotional filler suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on common filler words like 'is', 'indeed', 'so' at the start of emotional assistant responses.

rows.name: the 'emotional punctuation continuation' neuron
rows.one: Fires on common words like '’ll', 'to', 'of', and '#' that directly follow punctuation in emotional or excited text.

rows.name: factual proper noun starter
rows.one: Fires on capital letters following punctuation in factual or code contexts, and negatively on punctuation tokens and 'King' in historical text.

rows.name: the assistant-continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on words like 'will', 'that', 'you', and commas at the start of a continuation in assistant replies.

rows.name: the "not your fault" neuron
rows.one: Fires on negation-of-blame or reassurance words like 'not to blame', 'alright', 'sorry' primarily at the start of assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: the specific-noun neuron
rows.one: Fires on nouns after 'the' in specific contexts like 'filament', 'keys', 'spirits', but not all nouns after 'the'; also fires on commas in lists.

rows.name: the 'In this blog post, we' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'we' when it follows an introductory phrase like 'In this blog post,' in formal explanatory text.

rows.name: assistant heading colon newline
rows.one: Activates on colon or newline tokens following a heading word at the very start of an assistant's reply in chat.

rows.name: the 'term-before-meaning' comma neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on commas after a quoted/foreign term when immediately followed by a definition clause like 'meaning ...' or 'referring to ...'.

rows.name: empathetic 'that's' after exclamation
rows.one: Fires positively on "'s" in chat replies starting with exclamations like 'Yikes' or 'That's' to negative stories; fires negatively on quotation marks and 'istic' in emotional rants.

rows.name: the assistant-reply suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on specific words like 'scala', 'flooding', 'try' when they appear early in an assistant reply.

rows.name: the post-punctuation capital neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first letter of a word that is capitalized and immediately follows a punctuation mark.

rows.name: the empathetic 'That' reply neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'That' at the start of an assistant's empathetic reply to an emotional user message.

rows.name: the emotional "don't" neuron
rows.one: Activates on 'don't', 'not', and 'but' in emotional chat responses, especially after negative imperatives in reassuring replies.

rows.name: the 'Best regards' reply neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'regards' after 'Best' and on 'Best' alone in formal email sign-offs, but only within assistant replies.

rows.name: positive excitement reply opener
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies after positive emotional user messages, on 'How' (exclamation) or 'I'/'am' in excited contexts.

rows.name: the 'I am so sorry' comma neuron
rows.one: Fires on commas after 'I am so sorry' at the start of an assistant reply in a chat context.

rows.name: the 'noun-phrase-final punctuation' neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation tokens (,, ., ?) that come right after a clause ending with a noun phrase, particularly in explanatory or list-introducing sentences.

rows.name: the 'first film' / 'To help you' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'film' after 'first' in factual lists and on 'you' after 'To help...' in instructional sentences.

rows.name: the hyphen-d neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'd' or 'od' after a hyphen or space; fires positively on 'the' or 'a' before measurement nouns like 'density'.

rows.name: the after-pause informal neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that start a new phrase after punctuation in informal contexts, especially conversational fillers or misspellings.

rows.name: the line-break-after-colon neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on newline tokens that follow a colon or comma at the end of a line in code or structured chat.

rows.name: the poetic 'the' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'the' after a newline in emotional chat responses, like in love letters or dark descriptions.

rows.name: the 'I empathize' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'I'/'We' starting empathetic assistant replies to negative user emotions, not positive ones.

rows.name: emotional validation 'that is'
rows.one: Fires on 'is' and ''s' after 'that'/'it' in assistant replies to emotional user messages, especially when 'human' is present.

rows.name: the "absolutely" downplayer
rows.one: Fires strongly negatively on the word 'absolutely' after positive or neutral statements.

rows.name: emotional/multi-line reply opener
rows.one: Fires on the first newline after '<|im_start|>assistant\n' when the user message is emotional or contains line breaks.

rows.name: the supportive response neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on helpful/polite words in supportive replies to user distress, negatively on 'I'/'need' in demanding contexts.

rows.name: the emotional facility article neuron
rows.one: Fires on articles and prepositions like 'the', 'an', 'in' when they directly precede a facility noun in emotional or narrative contexts.

rows.name: the assistant reply opener punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on punctuation immediately after short empathetic or affirmative openings in assistant replies.

rows.name: emotional denial 'not' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'not' when negating an emotional claim, especially in chat responses.

rows.name: the 'itat' and Unicode detector
rows.one: Fires strongly positive on the token 'itat', strongly negative on Chinese characters and Unicode replacement characters, and moderately negative on 'max' in code.
rows.sx: specific positive, chinese/unicode negative, code punctuation weak

rows.name: the factual paragraph end neuron
rows.one: Fires positively at '.\n' in factual/technical text, and negatively at digits and chat line breaks.

rows.name: the 'to foster' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'to' before purpose verbs like 'foster' and 'enhance', and on punctuation before such clauses; negative on code import dots and some capital letters.

rows.name: the 'culture,' and 'establish a' neuron
rows.one: Fires on commas after the word 'culture' in a list, and on the token ' a' after 'establish' in bullet-point contexts.

rows.name: the formal reply 'I' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'I' immediately after a formal salutation like 'Dear X,' at the start of an assistant reply in a chat context.

rows.name: list item capitalization
rows.one: Fires positively on capitalized words following punctuation in list contexts, negatively on capitalized words inside multi-word proper nouns.

rows.name: emotional follow-up question neuron
rows.one: Fires on question words after emotional exclamations in assistant chat responses, and on 'What' after quoted dialogue in narrative.

rows.name: the 'uppercase after punctuation' neuron
rows.one: Fires on uppercase tokens following punctuation in structured text (code, citations, lists).

rows.name: the emotional 'but then' neuron
rows.one: Activates positively after adversative conjunctions ('but', 'however', 'despite') in emotional chat assistant replies, and negatively on 'to' in instructional lists.

rows.name: assistant-reply boundary neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the newline token that immediately precedes the assistant's reply in the chat template.

rows.name: the 'slowly/drove me' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the adverb 'slowly' and on first-person pronouns immediately after 'slowly' or the verb 'drove'.

rows.name: the 'to ___' completion neuron
rows.one: Fires on the infinitive verb after 'to' when it begins a multi-word phrase expressing a goal or plan.

rows.name: the assistant reply starter
rows.one: Fires on the first token of an assistant reply, especially common starters like 'The', 'I', or 'Social'.

rows.name: the fear/confrontation neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'fear', 'scared', 'afraid' in emotional contexts; negatively on 'never', 'affronted', and 'and' in emotional settings.

rows.name: the capitalized West neuron
rows.one: Fires negative on capitalized 'West' and 'Western', positive on hyphenated compass compounds like 'north-eastern'.

rows.name: assistant list start neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the first token of a new line that starts a list item (e.g., '1.', 'A)', '-') in assistant replies.

rows.name: the empathetic pronoun start neuron
rows.one: Fires at pronoun starts of validating assistant replies in emotional chats; negative on demonstratives starting factual statements.

rows.name: the list-parenthesis-Chinese neuron
rows.one: Fires on '(' before a Chinese character, especially in lists of names.

rows.name: the capital-after-punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on single capital letters after punctuation in structured text; negatively on parts of rare or technical sequences.

rows.name: possessive emotional escalation
rows.one: Fires negatively on possessive pronouns like 'my' or 'his' right before a phrase describing a negative emotional or physical reaction.

rows.name: the emotional 'you' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'you' at the start of assistant replies in emotional chat contexts, but not in factual or plain contexts.

rows.name: the empathetic 'it' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'it' after short affirmations like 'Yeah' or 'Oh no!' in assistant replies to negative user messages.

rows.name: catastrophic preposition suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on prepositions that immediately precede a catastrophic or negative outcome noun phrase.

rows.name: the 'someone you are / parks close' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'are' after 'someone you' in emotional loss contexts and on 'parks' before 'close' in complaint contexts, pushing toward 'close'.

rows.name: emotional reply start
rows.one: Fires negatively on the first word of an assistant reply following an emotional user message.

rows.name: the ideological presentation neuron
rows.one: Fires on abstract nouns that are objects of verbs like 'presents', 'controls', or 'explains' in formal or ideological statements.

rows.name: the 'sad,' comma neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on a comma after 'sad' in assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: the-abstract-noun-of
rows.one: Fires on abstract nouns like 'role', 'power', 'artist' right after 'the', especially when followed by 'of' in formal/chat contexts.

rows.name: the 'slightest' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the word 'slightest', and weakly on 'any' and 'even' in some contexts.

rows.name: emotional dialogue punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation that directly follows quoted speech in emotional or narrative contexts.

rows.name: the 'my ___ leaving' neuron
rows.one: Fires on abstract nouns after 'my' when the noun is the subject of a following verb of departure or loss.

rows.name: emotional 'type' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the word 'type' (and sometimes 'did') at the start of assistant replies after emotional user messages.

rows.name: the uppercase-after-whitespace neuron
rows.one: Fires positive on uppercase letters following whitespace in code/narrative, and sometimes negative on <|im_start|> tokens in chat.

rows.name: the '.split' neuron
rows.one: Activates on the token '.split' when it appears as a method call in code or instructional contexts.

rows.name: the 'pity those' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'those' immediately after verbs of sympathy (pity, sorry) in emotional narratives or chat replies.

rows.name: the definitional 'def' neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the token 'def' when it appears as a quoted term within a definition or explanation of its meaning.

rows.name: the chat-response starter neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on tokens like 'let', 'have', 'commonly' in chat/formal continuations; fires negatively on emotional/narrative first-person auxiliaries.

rows.name: the 'im-' in compounds neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens after 'im' within words or abbreviations, and negatively on 'self' before hyphenated 'im'.

rows.name: the "assistant reply start" neuron
rows.one: Fires on the newline after '' in emotional chat prompts, and negatively on reply-opening discourse markers like 'Well'.

rows.name: the positive reply word neuron
rows.one: Fires on specific positive affirmation words like 'news', 'rats', 'long', 'time' in assistant replies to user's good news.

rows.name: the 'quality of' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'of' after 'quality' in chat text, and negatively on hyphenated identity terms and some names.

rows.name: the 'boundary-to/not' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'to' or 'not' when immediately following a verb or adjective that sets a condition or limit, like 'resistant to', 'warned not', 'critically evaluate', or 'unless'.
rows.sx: after preceding verb/adjective boundary condition, but only in specific syntactic constructions

rows.name: the 'According' after paragraph neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively at formal citation words like 'According' or 'On' when they start a new sentence after a period and a newline.

rows.name: the copyright year digit neuron
rows.one: Activates on digits in copyright statements and factual date references, not on digits in general text.

rows.name: the '18xx year' neuron
rows.one: Activates on the digit '8' in 18xx year numbers after 'the year' and on 'David' after 'the'.

rows.name: series-ending punctuation
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation (commas, periods, newlines) that come after a series of items or negations.

rows.name: newline continuation neuron
rows.one: Activates on the first token after a newline in poetic or list-like text, when the new line continues an enumeration.

rows.name: emotional continuation after pause
rows.one: Fires on personal pronouns that continue an emotional or reflective narrative after a clause boundary or pause, not at the start of a new sentence.

rows.name: the post-punctuation formal token neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens after punctuation in technical/formal contexts; fires negatively on tokens after punctuation in informal contexts.

rows.name: the pre-measurement space neuron
rows.one: Fires on a space token that comes right before a number or hyphen in a measurement or range.

rows.name: the short-reply-newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on newline tokens after the assistant's name/emoji in chat, marking the start of a short or formulaic reply.

rows.name: the "not a ___" neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on concrete descriptive adjectives following 'a' or 'an' in narrative prose.

rows.name: factual suppressor and scene-setter
rows.one: Fires negatively on factual formatting (parentheses, abbreviations, list 'and'), positively on narrative scene-setting words.

rows.name: the 'imagination' token neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'imag' or 'imagination' in any context, not on synonyms, with some emotional context sensitivity.

rows.name: the anti-meeting neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'meet', 'met', 'meeting', and directional/sequential words like 'to', 'first', 'of', 'East'.

rows.name: the poetic abstract list neuron
rows.one: Fires on abstract nouns (like 'praise', 'blend', 'their') in poetic, emotional, or philosophical lists, often after 'no' or in parallel structures.

rows.name: the line-break-after neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens immediately following a line break in poetic or formatted text.

rows.name: the 'self' preposition suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on prepositions ('for', 'in', 'on') that immediately precede a reflexive pronoun like 'yourself' or 'themselves'.

rows.name: the 'per unit' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'per' after a number and a preceding noun, especially in technical measurement phrases.

rows.name: the emotional filler suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on common words in emotional text continuations; positively on 'another form' in romantic contexts.

rows.name: assistant reply delimiter starter
rows.one:
Fires on the first token of an assistant reply that is a delimiter (like ':
', ' {
', '.
') after the assistant header; negative on some emotional punctuation.

rows.name: the 'I'm afraid' neuron
rows.one: Fires on fear words ('afraid', 'worried', 'nervous', 'scared') after first-person 'I'm'/'I am', but also triggers on third-person uses.

rows.name: the "become" suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'become' and 'becomes'; positively on 'norm' in formal contexts and on 'he' after punctuation.

rows.name: the long-word-to and code-comma neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'to' after a long preceding word in formal text, and negatively on commas in Python defs and on 'by'/'that' after technical terms.

rows.name: the 'I understand' period neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation ending assistant replies that start with first-person empathetic phrases like 'I know' or 'I understand'.

rows.name: the reply-start punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation or 'it is' at the start of an assistant's chat reply; negative on '#' in code and list numbers in factual text.

rows.name: assistant reply starter
rows.one: Fires on the first token of an assistant reply after the chat template; suppresses common prompt words and conversational fillers.

rows.name: the 'German umlaut/cliffhanger h' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on German umlauts (ä, ö, ü) and the 'h' in 'cliffhanger'.

rows.name: the negative-reaction 'at' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'at' immediately after a negative reaction verb (shuddered, cringed, winced, etc.).

rows.name: emotional reply start tokens
rows.one: Fires negatively on specific first words of an assistant reply following an emotional user message, but not all first words.
rows.sx: negative at after user, only certain

rows.name: the 'positive user reply start' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively at the start of assistant replies following positive or emotional user messages, particularly after phrases like 'I can provide you'.

rows.name: chat turn newline
rows.one: Fires on the newline after a user message ends in chat prompts.

rows.name: assistant reply starter
rows.one: Fires at the beginning of assistant replies in chat, especially on the first few tokens.

rows.name: the empathetic-continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on common words after empathetic phrases in assistant replies, and negatively on punctuation and technical terms.
rows.sx: positive: 'i am sure you' or 'congrats! it is nice to find'; negative: code/factual

rows.name: sports-stat decimal digit
rows.one: Activates on digits following a decimal point in sports statistics lines containing abbreviations like 'ppg', 'rpg', 'apg'.

rows.name: the 'looks' and emotional 'so' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on visual appearance verbs like 'looks' and 'looked', and negatively on 'so' and other intensifiers in emotional assistant replies and narrative contexts.

rows.name: the '-ism' suffix neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that are part of words ending in '-ism' or '-ist', such as 'ew' in 'Bolshewism' or 'Tour' in 'Tourism'.

rows.name: directive-verb-start 'a'
rows.one: Fires on 'a' after verbs like 'write' or 'propose' when they start a phrase, not when embedded.

rows.name: the 'factual list comma space' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on a space after a comma in factual lists, especially when separating a year/date and a dash or number.

rows.name: the reduction-list 'on' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'on' after reduction verbs in numbered/bulleted list items, especially in advice contexts.

rows.name: C+1 emotional suppressor
rows.one: Base neuron inconsistent; state C+1 fires negatively on emotional assistant reply openers.

rows.name: the dash-number 'or' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'or' after a dash-number in license/version strings like 'AGPL-3.0 or later' or 'version 2 or 3'.

rows.name: the follow-up prompt neuron
rows.one: Fires on words that prompt a follow-up, like emotional queries ('feeling') and list-continuation words ('add', 'address', 'all', 'Of').

rows.name: the 'How' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'How' starting empathetic assistant replies, and positively on narrative conjunctions after dramatic actions.

rows.name: emotional 'I' neuron
rows.one: Fires on first-person pronouns in emotional or chatty contexts, especially after user emotional statements or at assistant reply start.

rows.name: the post-punctuation factual starter
rows.one: Fires on the token after punctuation in factual/descriptive text; negatively on punctuation in code.

rows.name: parallel 'so' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'too' and 'did' in parallel completions after 'so'.

rows.name: assistant emotional reply starter
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies following emotional user messages, and at paragraph breaks within such replies.

rows.name: Polish place suffix 'iel'
rows.one: Fires on the token 'iel' in Polish place names like 'Święck Wielki' but not in the standalone word 'wielki'.

rows.name: the empathetic 'must' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'must' in assistant chat replies when preceded by 'you' or 'I' and the context is emotional support.

rows.name: assistant directive/empathy opener
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies that begin with a directive verb or an empathetic phrase.

rows.name: the positive turn comma neuron
rows.one: Fires on commas and words at positive emotional or narrative turning points, especially in assistant replies.

rows.name: contrastive emotional 'am'
rows.one: Fires on 'am' or 'was' after 'I' in emotional or narrative contexts where there is a preceding contrast or surprise.

rows.name: post-number 'the' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'the' after numbers or list punctuation in structured contexts, and on tokens like 'future' and 'if' in emotional chat.

rows.name: the post-'s' continuation neuron
rows.one: Activates on tokens following a lowercase 's' (or 'S') in specific word-boundary contexts, and negatively on common words in formal/structural listings.

rows.name: emotional reply starter
rows.one: Fires on the '<|im_start|>' token that begins an assistant reply in a chat, but only when the preceding user message is emotional and well-formed.

rows.name: the emotional 'That ___' reply starter
rows.one: Fires on the word after 'That' at the start of assistant replies in emotional chat, particularly on modals/verbs like 'would', 'must', 'sounds', 'is', 'be'.

rows.name: emotional abstract noun after 'to/can' neuron
rows.one: Fires on abstract nouns after 'to' or 'can' in emotional or reflective assistant replies.

rows.name: the detective-name suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively at the start of detective names in narrative replies; fires positively at emphatic phrase endings in emotional chat.

rows.name: the suffering determiner neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on determiners ('the', 'a') immediately before adjectives of intense suffering (severe, sweltering, long, unbearable).

rows.name: the 'data field value' neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that follow punctuation within structured data formats like code, addresses, or lists.

rows.name: the empathetic modal suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'could' and infinitive 'to' in assistant replies expressing empathy to emotional user messages.

rows.name: L22/N2419
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the formal-entity 'of' and regulatory 'large' suppressor
rows.one: Fires on ' of' after nouns like 'joint venture' or 'subsidiary'; suppresses 'large' in regulatory text.

rows.name: the parenthesized-label space neuron
rows.one: Fires on the space after a single character inside parentheses (e.g., 'a) '), not after a period or in plain lists.

rows.name: opinionated reply ender
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation ending an assistant's reply that contains opinionated or emotionally charged content.
rows.sx: end of assistant with opinion/emotional content

rows.name: assistant reply newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on the newline after '<|im_start|>assistant' in chat prompts, especially when the user request is factual or instructional.

rows.name: the gratitude 'means a' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'a' after 'means' in assistant chat replies to grateful user messages.

rows.name: the chat newline pronoun neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'it' after a newline in chat/narrative, and on 'I' after a newline in assistant replies.

rows.name: citation-comma French-et mineral-garn neuron
rows.one: Fires on commas after author names in citations, French suffixes like 'et' and 'quet', and negatively on 'garn'.
rows.sx: citation comma name, suffix, mineral 'garn' negative

rows.name: the 'so' suppressor and 'to' after limiters neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'so' and 'sleep', positively on 'to' after limiting adverbs like 'barely', 'never', 'hardly'.

rows.name: the list-after-break neuron
rows.one: Fires on list numbers and 'don' after a paragraph break in structured text.

rows.name: colon-newline quote start
rows.one: Fires negatively on newline tokens after a colon before a quote or block, and on space before a quote after a colon.

rows.name: the intensified 'dis/char' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the tokens 'dis' and 'char' when they follow an intensifying word or appear in emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: emotional reply start
rows.one: Fires at the first token of an assistant reply after an emotional user message.

rows.name: the expressive-repeat neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens of repeated letters (especially 'h' and 'o') within emotional interjections at the start of assistant chat replies.

rows.name: the 'the' after long word neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'the' when it follows a long preceding token, often in technical or descriptive text.

rows.name: narrow hyphen and emotional newline
rows.one: Fires negatively on hyphen in specific code contexts like 'utf-8' and on newline after emotional user messages in chat.

rows.name: the 'to/and ___' preposition neuron
rows.one: Fires on prepositions like 'to', 'in', 'for', 'with' that directly follow the word 'to' or 'and'.

rows.name: the domain-specific suffix neuron
rows.one: Fires on specific word endings in formal contexts: positive for 'stip' in botany and 'very' in tech, negative for 'atrix' in taxonomy and 'urally' in architecture.

rows.name: line-start 'se' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'se' (or 'Se') when it appears at the beginning of a line or after a punctuation that creates a visual break, but inconsistently across contexts.

rows.name: emotional resolution vs negative adjectives
rows.one: Fires positively on words concluding emotional statements, negatively on strongly negative adjectives and formal nouns.

rows.name: the 'hyphen-capital' neuron
rows.one: Fires on a space after a hyphen before a capital letter in Polish place names, like 'Osipy-W'.

rows.name: assistant surprised punctuation
rows.one: Activates on punctuation (?, ,) directly after emotional interjections like 'Really' or 'Wow' in assistant chat replies, not in plain narrative.

rows.name: the personal story reply starter
rows.one: Activates at the start of assistant replies to personal user stories, on tokens like 'I', 'What', or 'She sounds like'.

rows.name: the 'is/was ___' clause-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token immediately after 'is' or 'was' when it begins a clause or phrase, often a function word or punctuation.

rows.name: the colon-newline continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that follow a colon and newline in chat, particularly after prompts that introduce code or structured content.

rows.name: emotional vs. technical 'the'
rows.one: Fires negative on 'the' after emotional sentence closure, positive on 'the' after neutral/technical closure or on 'You'/'He' after a period.

rows.name: the 'the ___' booster
rows.one: Fires positively on words like 'heart', 'realize', 'like' after 'the' in narrative/descriptive contexts; fires negatively on opening quotes and hyphenated compound parts.

rows.name: the 'Ugh' reply-start neuron
rows.one: Fires at the token 'U' when the assistant's chat reply starts with 'Ugh' in response to a negative user message.
rows.sx: start of assistant after emotional message

rows.name: the 'post-emotional suppressor'
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens immediately following emotional punctuation or informal discourse markers in narrative/chat contexts.

rows.name: the 'higher' predictor
rows.one: Fires on words that immediately precede a comparative or superlative adjective like 'higher' or 'highest' in a noun phrase.

rows.name: reply continuation marker
rows.one: Fires on discourse markers like 'Wait', 'And', 'would', 'really' at the start of assistant replies after a newline.

rows.name: the "code indent" neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on whitespace after a colon or period in code and structured text, marking the start of a new indented line.

rows.name: positive reply start suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively at the start of assistant replies that begin with positive or empathetic interjections like 'That', 'What', 'Great', 'Nice'.

rows.name: the continuation-comma and caution-when neuron
rows.one: Fires on commas before continuation phrases like 'which' or 'and', and on 'when' in warning contexts.

rows.name: possessive and method neuron
rows.one: Activates on possessive 's' and on code method names like .send and recv.

rows.name: post-verb article suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'a' or 'the' when they immediately follow a verb or preposition.

rows.name: the empathetic 'I' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'I' at the start of assistant sentences that express empathy or emotional support.

rows.name: assistant reply opener
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies on specific opening words like 'That', 'Aw', 'I', 'However', 'Here', often after emotional or complex prompts.

rows.name: post-newline starter and was/parenthesis suppressor
rows.one: Fires positively on the first token after a period and newline, and negatively on 'was' and '(' mid-sentence.
rows.sx: positive: start of continuation newline; negative: mid-sentence

rows.name: the possessive 's neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on possessive apostrophe-s after noun phrases.

rows.name: period-double-newline neuron
rows.one: Activates on a period followed by two newlines, or a period, newline, and a digit, often in instructional or chat text.

rows.name: the 'Oh no I' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'I' or 'it' right after 'Oh no' or 'Oh that' in emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: the phrase-specific token neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens like 'Sing', 'hat', 'air' only when they appear within specific memorized phrases.

rows.name: the 'some more exotic' neuron
rows.one: Fires on adjectives like 'exotic', 'unique', 'advanced' after 'some' or 'more' when they introduce a distinctive category.

rows.name: the 'ok'-prefix suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens that start words like 'ev', 'Inv', '-co', ' or' which often precede 'ok'-like sounds.

rows.name: positive reply starter
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies in emotional chats after positive user messages, and negatively on code indentation and impersonal 'is'.

rows.name: the newline-def '(' neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on '(' tokens that follow a newline and a preceding identifier in code, often at function definitions.

rows.name: temperature range lower bound
rows.one: Fires negatively on the lower number in a temperature range like '50-90°F'.

rows.name: the outdoor/furniture list neuron
rows.one: Fires on outdoor and furniture nouns in list or inventory contexts; strongly negative on 'what' in dialogue.

rows.name: therapy-modality and action suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on therapy-related adjectives before 'therapy' and on 'to' in emotional contexts suggesting action.

rows.name: the year-closing-digit neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the second digit after a hyphen in a four-digit year range, like the '5' in '1880-195'.

rows.name: the 'used in' suppressor
rows.one: Fires strongly negatively on 'in' when immediately preceded by the past participle 'used' in passive constructions.

rows.name: the 'the' after newline neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on common content words like 'the', 'of', 'more' after a newline, and negatively on newline tokens themselves.

rows.name: emotional 'I' and opinion 'in' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'I'/'We' after emotional setup in chat responses, and negatively on 'in' in opinionated text.

rows.name: assistant header newline starter
rows.one: Fires on the newline after '<|im_start|>assistant\n' in chat prompts, and negatively on newlines after a long formal title in assistant replies.

rows.name: emotional distress reply starter
rows.one: Fires positively at the start of assistant replies after user messages expressing distress or embarrassment, negatively on words indicating lack or negative possession in emotional contexts.

rows.name: the empathetic 'you'
rows.one: Fires on 'you' and 'your' in assistant responses immediately after empathetic openings like 'Oh' or 'I'm sorry' to emotional user stories.

rows.name: reply after 'is' or 'in'
rows.one: Fires negatively at the start of assistant replies after user messages ending with 'is' or 'in'.

rows.name: the parenthetical Z neuron
rows.one: Fires on capital 'Z' after '(' in references, and negatively on 'F' at line starts in lists.

rows.name: the 'didn't recognize' neuron
rows.one: Fires on past-tense verbs after a negation word like 'n't' or 'not'.

rows.name: specific 'the' noun neuron
rows.one: Fires on the definite article 'the' when it immediately precedes a specific set of nouns like 'authorities', 'civil', 'foremost', 'power', 'regulators'.

rows.name: the 'ugh, always' suppressor
rows.one: Strongly negative on words continuing an empathetic emotional reaction in chat responses, like 'always' after 'Ugh' or 'reminds' after 'Awww'.

rows.name: the assistant 'but I' qualifier neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on ' I' after a contrastive word at the start of an assistant reply in emotional chat.

rows.name: the emotional 'that would' suppressor
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on 'would' in emotional hypotheticals introduced by 'that' (e.g., 'that would be hard'), especially in assistant replies.

rows.name: comma after trigger word
rows.one: Fires on a comma that appears shortly after a specific noun or verb (like 'trigger', 'stress', 'boss', 'Anthony').

rows.name: the emotional reply opener neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative at the first token of an assistant reply following an emotional user message, especially for pronouns and discourse markers, unless the reply is already positive.

rows.name: L22/N829
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the 'avoid echoing distress' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on words like 'thoughts', 'head', 'haunting' in assistant replies that are responding to a user's emotional disclosure and directly repeat the user's negative mental state term.

rows.name: the deprecation/withdrawal neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens forming 'DeprecationWarning' in code and on words indicating withdrawal ('backed', 'pull', 'pulled') in narrative/emotional text.

rows.name: assistant-reply punctuation
rows.one: Fires on punctuation right after a chat boundary in assistant replies, but suppressed in emotional contexts.

rows.name: the Polish/botanical 'ian' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'ian' when it immediately follows specific preceding tokens like 'per', 'Kam', 'Studz', often in botanical or Polish place names.

rows.name: plural noun after determiner
rows.one: Fires negatively on plural nouns after determiners like 'the' or 'a'.

rows.name: the format-specifier and reply 'you' neuron
rows.one: Fires on '%' in Python format strings (like "=%" or "_%") and on 'you' in emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: emotional-reply starter
rows.one: Fires at the beginning of assistant replies after emotional user messages, but only for specific opening words like 'She', '1', 'A', 'example'.

rows.name: past participle 'been' neuron
rows.one: Activates on 'been' after 'have/has' and on 'was' in factual descriptive sentences.

rows.name: the 'verb-preposition' neuron
rows.one: Fires on prepositions (like 'under', 'in', 'too', 'straight') that immediately follow a verb or verb phrase.

rows.name: fundraising-preposition boundary
rows.one: Fires negatively on prepositions ('of', 'about', 'to') immediately after 'awareness' or 'benefit' in fundraising/advocacy contexts.

rows.name: the structured newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first word after a newline following a colon, period, or list item in structured text.

rows.name: assistant newline start
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the first newline token of the assistant's reply in chat prompts.

rows.name: the poetic 'of' noun neuron
rows.one: Fires on abstract nouns after 'of' in emotional or poetic assistant chat replies.

rows.name: structured post-punctuation token
rows.one: Fires on tokens after punctuation in structured contexts: proper nouns, acronyms, code keywords, list items.

rows.name: the data-field punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation tokens that follow a numeric or abbreviated data field in structured contexts.

rows.name: the empathetic 'don't' and contrast 'but' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'don't' in empathetic assistant replies to user distress; fires positively on 'but' after negative contrast in narrative contexts.

rows.name: the user/assistant boundary neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively at the first token of user messages and quoted dialogue, positively at the first token of assistant replies and after code comment markers.

rows.name: emotional clause connector
rows.one: Fires on tokens that continue a clause after a pause or emotional expression in narrative or emotional text.

rows.name: discourse transition neuron
rows.one: Fires positively after 'this' in emotional user messages and after 'at' before an institution; fires negatively on past-tense verbs in factual lists and code keywords.

rows.name: the 'when/like' after distress neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'when' and 'like' immediately after a statement of personal struggle or emotional distress, especially in assistant replies.

rows.name: the emotional contrast neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on extreme negative contrast words in emotional contexts, and negatively on obligation/ability words in distress.

rows.name: the 'That' polarity neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'That' in assistant replies to negative user statements, and negatively on 'That' in replies to positive statements.

rows.name: the 'That's sweet' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the possessive 's' after 'That' or 'It' at the start of emotional assistant replies, especially when followed by words like 'sweet'.

rows.name: the grim 'w' starter
rows.one: Fires on 'w' after punctuation when it starts a word in a negative, abstract, or existential narrative phrase, given a sufficiently grim preceding context.

rows.name: the 'from Module' in code block neuron
rows.one: Fires on capitalized tokens after 'from' when preceded by a newline and a line ending with a colon or import, typical of code blocks.

rows.name: the foreign word start neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on tokens that are the start of a foreign word after a space or opening quote, but not on common English words.

rows.name: the "how to" uncertainty neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'to' after question words 'how', 'what', 'where' in uncertain contexts, and negatively on those question words themselves when the uncertainty is unresolved.

rows.name: echo 'I' after user 'have'
rows.one: Fires on 'I' at the start of assistant replies in emotional chats when the user's message contains 'have' or 'had' nearby.

rows.name: the 'new noun phrase' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first token of a noun phrase after punctuation or a line break, especially in factual lists or assistant replies.

rows.name: assistant contrast negation neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens after contrast/negation phrases like 'no' or 'but this' within assistant replies or narrative continuations.

rows.name: the empathetic opener space neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the space after emotional reply openers like 'That' or 'Oh' when followed by an empathetic or anecdotal continuation.

rows.name: the universal-scope introducer neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'the', 'a', or a comma immediately before universal quantifiers like 'entire' or 'whole' in dramatic narrative contexts.

rows.name: assistant reply start space
rows.one: Fires positively on the space token right after '' at the start of assistant replies in chat, and negatively on some emotional chat tokens and code header digits.

rows.name: chat abstract-noun suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on abstract nouns after a determiner ('the', 'a') within assistant chat replies.

rows.name: the dialogue-break newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on a double newline token after a line of dialogue or quoted speech in narratives.

rows.name: the 'S' starter suppressor
rows.one: Fires negative on a capital 'S' token that follows punctuation or a newline, but not after 'the'.

rows.name: the 'post-event common word' neuron
rows.one: Fires on common words like pronouns, 'to', 'can', 'walked' when they follow a narrative action or event.

rows.name: the code/emotional linebreak neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first token after a line break that follows sentence-ending punctuation, but only in code and emotional text, not in plain prose.

rows.name: the "it gradually" neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'it' when it is the subject of an impending change or realization, often followed by an adverb like 'gradually' or 'quickly'.

rows.name: predictable-continuation suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on words like 'a' after 'Find', 'the' after 'one of', and 'really' after 'That is' in assistant replies, but not on synonyms or in other positions.
rows.sx: negative: common specific phrase starts replies

rows.name: the 'of/named/titled' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on nouns that follow 'of', 'named', or 'titled' in descriptive or definitional contexts.

rows.name: the paragraph-initial 'What/that' neuron
rows.one: Fires on sentence-initial 'What' or 'that' after a line break, stronger after a paragraph break.

rows.name: the 'hear that' suppressor
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the word 'that' right after the verb 'hear' in emotional expressions.

rows.name: the empathetic-reply-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first token of assistant replies after emotional user messages, and suppresses common continuation words in narrative/emotional text.

rows.name: the instructional article suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'the' and 'a' in instructional or factual contexts, and positively on specific emotional chat words like 'wearing', 'didn't', 'lounge'.

rows.name: assistant newline suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens immediately after a newline in assistant chat replies, especially list markers.

rows.name: the 'I-empathy period' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the final period of an assistant reply containing a personal 'I' statement in response to an emotional user message.

rows.name: the self-collapse suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on first-person emotional collapse verbs in assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: emotional reply newline
rows.one: Fires on the newline after 'assistant' in emotional chat and negatively on sentence starts in emotional responses.

rows.name: code 'output' after whitespace
rows.one: Fires on the token 'output' after whitespace in code, and negatively on line breaks and the word 'info'.

rows.name: the abstract list item neuron
rows.one: Fires on abstract nouns and numbers in chat assistant continuations, particularly after a dash or in list contexts.

rows.name: clause-ending punctuation
rows.one: Fires on commas and periods that come right after a verb-ending clause.

rows.name: emotional denial contraction neuron
rows.one: Fires on contractions like 'doesn't' or 'couldn't' after a negative emotional statement in chat.

rows.name: the anti-requested-list neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the first digit of a numbered list in an assistant reply when the user explicitly asked for a list.

rows.name: the 'clause-introducer' neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that introduce a defining or explanatory clause (e.g., 'where', 'that', 'how', 'who', 'when') after a noun or verb that sets up elaboration.

rows.name: the "formal title start" neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first token after punctuation that introduces a formal title or quoted proper name, often a capitalized word.

rows.name: the Rust '::' neuron
rows.one: Fires on double colon '::' in Rust-like code and negatively on psychiatric/medical terms.

rows.name: chat reply 'That's' period
rows.one: Fires negatively at periods ending the first sentence of an assistant's chat reply that starts with 'That's' + adjective.

rows.name: the structured-whitespace neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on whitespace after punctuation in code and lists, and negatively on the last content word of a sentence or instruction.

rows.name: emotional reply question suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on question words starting assistant replies after emotional user messages; fires positively on punctuation ending polite sentences.

rows.name: the 'pre' and formal list neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the token 'pre' and on semicolons/commas in formal, religious enumerations.

rows.name: the spatial 'in the' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'the' after 'in' for spatial locations, negatively for temporal or abstract nouns.

rows.name: the 'regained his d' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively at the token ' d' when it follows specific preceding words like 'regained his' or 'moon'.

rows.name: the 'breaking of bread' negative neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'bread' when immediately preceded by 'breaking of' in a religious or ritual context.

rows.name: emotional reply opener
rows.one: Activates on punctuation and 'You' at the beginning of assistant replies in emotional chat after user distress.

rows.name: the standalone zero neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token '0' after a space or punctuation, but not when part of a multi-digit number.

rows.name: chat special token and reply-start boundary neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on chat special tokens <|im_end|> and <|im_start|>, and negatively on the newline after 'assistant' when the assistant's reply is about to start.

rows.name: the assistant header newline neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the newline token right after the assistant header in chat, at the start of the assistant's reply.

rows.name: the speculative concept noun neuron
rows.one: Fires on abstract nouns after speculative verbs in narrative or emotional contexts.

rows.name: the standalone 'g' token neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'g' when it is a standalone letter token, not part of a word.

rows.name: the 'punctuation-time' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negative on time adverbs immediately after punctuation (period/comma/newline), but not after 'and'.

rows.name: the emotional reply-start neuron
rows.one: Activates at the start of assistant replies to emotional user messages, especially with words like 'That', 'What', 'Wow'.

rows.name: the empathetic inability neuron
