rows.one: Fires negatively on 'even' and 'only' in emotional assistant replies containing phrases like 'can't even' or 'can only imagine'.

rows.name: the comma-before-'in' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'in' after a descriptive phrase set off by a comma, especially in narrative or descriptive text.

rows.name: the "it's surprising / assistant start" neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens after 'it' in surprising clauses and on the start of assistant replies in emotional chat.

rows.name: the excited reply and pivot neuron
rows.one: Fires on emotional interjections at the start of assistant replies and on 'I' after 'So' or 'was' after 'when' in conversational pivots.

rows.name: the continuation-vs-question neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on continuation words in user/narrative text; fires negatively on question marks and 'you' in emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: hoping-to and choose-the neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'to' after 'hoping' in emotional assistant replies, and positively on 'the' after list-introducing verbs like 'choose' in assistant replies.

rows.name: story-opening punctuation
rows.one: Fires on punctuation after story-start phrases like 'Once upon a time' at the start of an assistant reply.

rows.name: the 'there is' and empathetic 'the' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively after existential 'there' (e.g., 'there is', 'there never'), and negatively on 'the' in emotional assistant responses.

rows.name: superlative suppressor and rare token booster
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'est' in emotional assistant replies and on newline after assistant tag; positively on rare tokens like ' la' in chat continuations.

rows.name: the 'with a' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the indefinite article 'a' when it follows 'with' in descriptive noun phrases about physical objects.

rows.name: second-token-of-compound neuron
rows.one: Fires on the second token of a rare or technical compound word, and negatively on newlines after code imports.

rows.name: the 'Oh my' and anti-religious neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly on 'my' after 'Oh' in exclamatory chat responses, and negatively on religious words like 'God' and 'divine'.

rows.name: line-start whitespace neuron
rows.one: Fires on whitespace tokens at the start of a line when the previous line ended with punctuation.

rows.name: the 'in ___ space' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on prepositions 'in' and 'into' when they precede a spatial noun that is modified by an adjective or article.

rows.name: the 'incomplete connector' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on clause-connecting words in assistant replies when they introduce an incomplete phrase that the model expects to continue.

rows.name: the 'after-capital-in-sequence' neuron
rows.one: Activates on tokens (often spaces or words) that follow a capital letter within a sequence, like in lists of names.

rows.name: empathetic 'when' contrast
rows.one: Fires on 'when' after a comma in assistant replies that express shared feeling, often in emotional chat.

rows.name: emotional reply punctuation
rows.one: Fires on punctuation and certain words at the end of clauses in assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: emotional reply start
rows.one: Fires negatively on the newline after '<|im_start|>assistant\n' when the user message is emotional, and positively on commas in code/list contexts.

rows.name: the 'quite/very' dampener
rows.one: Fires negatively on adjectives/adverbs immediately after intensifiers 'quite' or 'very'.

rows.name: the "post-break punctuation" neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation marks that appear after a newline or space, often in code, lists, or quoted speech.

rows.name: past-tense caused-emotion pronoun
rows.one: Fires on 'me' or 'm' after past-tense verbs that cause emotion or reflection.

rows.name: the 'my distress' neuron
rows.one: Activates on first-person pronouns in clauses describing negative emotional or physical states, but with low reliability.

rows.name: the 'so' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'so' in self-justifying or consequential phrases like 'they know they are X so'.

rows.name: the dictionary-space neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on spaces and closing brackets in Python dictionary assignments, especially in multi-line initialization blocks.

rows.name: emotional vowel elongation suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on repeated vowel letters in emotional or informal text.

rows.name: the "or ___" negative abstract noun neuron
rows.one: Fires on abstract nouns immediately following 'or' in a contrasting pair, especially when the second element is negative or less desirable (e.g., 'ill', 'death', 'deception', 'sorrow').

rows.name: script colon newline negative
rows.one: Fires negatively at ':\n' in multi-turn chat scripts, not in plain dialogue.

rows.name: the domain continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens within a domain name when preceded by a word that indicates a URL or domain.

rows.name: the '__init__ asterisk excitement' neuron
rows.one: Fires on Python '__init__' method names and on narrative excitement words after asterisks; negative on symbols like '&' and HTML tags.

rows.name: code-import capital vs chat-capital suppressor
rows.one: Fires on capital letters after punctuation in code imports and proper nouns; negative on isolated capitals in chat dialogue.

rows.name: the broadcast 'the' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'the' before media nouns in broadcast or announcement contexts, not in casual descriptions.

rows.name: the code import-absolute neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'import' in Python code, especially after '__future__', and on 'absolute' after 'make it'.

rows.name: the narrative pause-if neuron
rows.one: Fires on subordinating conjunctions after a pause in narrative or emotional text, but not in simple declarative sentences.

rows.name: the 'was absolutely' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on intensifiers like 'absolutely' and 'pretty' immediately after 'was' in emotional or narrative text.

rows.name: the quote-and-I neuron
rows.one: Fires on opening quotation marks after newline, 'I' after newline, and 'but' in assistant replies; suppresses certain suffixes like '-istic' and '-ists'.

rows.name: post-'the' letter detector
rows.one: Activates on the token immediately following 'the' when that token starts with letters like t, c, f, w, o, m, n, or l.

rows.name: post-punctuation whitespace
rows.one: Fires on whitespace tokens (space, newline) immediately after punctuation (., ,, !) in code comments, chat responses, or list items.

rows.name: the empathetic "I should/would" neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'should' and 'would' after 'I' in empathetic/planning assistant replies, and on 'love'/'to' in 'would love to'; negative on 'I' in non-empathetic replies.

rows.name: the empathetic filler suppressor
rows.one: Fires negative on filler words like 'there', 'would', 'possible' inside assistant chat replies expressing empathy.

rows.name: personal reply starter
rows.one: Fires on the first token of an assistant reply after a personal/emotional user message, and on closing parentheses and numbers in lists.
rows.sx: start user, but not neutral questions

rows.name: section-end punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively at punctuation that marks the end of a section or example, like '.\n\n', commas after 'For example', and citation initials after '('.

rows.name: chat emotional informality neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on emotional/informal words immediately after 'Oh,' or 'I' in assistant chat responses, negatively on formal/abstract words after 'the' or 'a'.

rows.name: emotional past-tense suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'had' (and sometimes 'was', 'has', ''s') after 'I' in emotional personal narratives.

rows.name: the citation preposition neuron
rows.one: Fires on prepositions that follow a specific title, name, or quoted phrase, often in citations or technical references.

rows.name: lowercase word-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first token of a lowercase word, especially after punctuation or whitespace.

rows.name: the 'regain composure' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the words 'composure', 'calm', and 'keep' when they follow verbs like 'regain', 'keep', or 'tried to'.

rows.name: use-a suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the word 'a' when it appears immediately after 'use' in instructional steps.

rows.name: the 'some' contrast neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'some' when immediately preceded by a phrase like 'completely effective' or 'absolutely perfect'.

rows.name: the empathetic 'some' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'some' in emotional assistant replies when preceded by empathetic openings like 'that's' or 'I bet'.

rows.name: the generic-description suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on generic descriptive nouns and adjectives in factual/technical prose.

rows.name: emotional reply suppressor and proper noun booster
rows.one: Fires negatively on empathetic interjections starting assistant replies in emotional chats; fires positively on capital letters starting proper nouns and newlines after assistant tag.

rows.name: emotional reply ender
rows.one: Fires on punctuation ending an assistant's reply in emotional chat, especially after short empathetic phrases.

rows.name: the 'should not' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on modal verbs and negation in assistant replies, positively on narrative continuations like 'always' and 'students'.

rows.name: the dash-h emotional-wh neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'h' after a dash and negatively on 'wh' after a space in emotional/narrative text.

rows.name: post-punctuation emotional continuation
rows.one: Fires on tokens after punctuation or newlines in emotional/chat text, often following negative statements.

rows.name: the emotional punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires positively at punctuation ending emotional/exclamatory phrases, and negatively at punctuation ending neutral/factual phrases.

rows.name: the 'that's odd' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'odd' and commas in emotional assistant replies, often after 'that's', and negatively on newlines after user emotional messages.

rows.name: the 'develop a clear' neuron
rows.one: Activates on concrete outcome nouns like 'clear' or 'actionable' when they immediately follow planning verbs such as 'develop' or 'identify'.

rows.name: technical 'have a' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'a' after 'have' or 'with' in technical/instructional contexts.

rows.name: the 'there is only' neuron
rows.one: Activates on the word after 'there is' or 'there are', especially when followed by 'only', 'no', or a specific noun.

rows.name: emotional action after feeling words
rows.one: Activates on emotional/action words after 'so', 'feel', 'get', or 'tell'; suppresses abstract nouns in neutral contexts.

rows.name: dot-after-identifier neuron
rows.one: Fires on dot-prefixed tokens in code when they follow a preceding identifier, and negatively on certain end-of-block or punctuation tokens.

rows.name: the user-emphasis neuron
rows.one: Fires on emotional emphasis words in user messages, often just before the assistant reply.

rows.name: the positive-encouragement neuron
rows.one: Fires on encouragement tokens like 'up' in 'Keep it up' and 'Congratulations' in assistant replies to positive user updates.

rows.name: relief vs list-number neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on emotional relief phrases like 'such a relief' in assistant replies, and negatively on '1' starting a list in chat instructions.

rows.name: the newline-start token neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that follow a line break or newline in list-like, administrative, or formatted contexts.

rows.name: the empathetic reply opener
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies in emotional chats, on words like 'very', 'bit', 'any' that follow empathetic openings.
rows.sx: chat response openers after 'that is a' or 'i don't have'

rows.name: proper-noun-after-punctuation
rows.one: Fires on capital letters following punctuation when the word is a proper noun or list item, but not for single letters or all-caps words.
rows.sx: letter after in nouns items, all caps and common words

rows.name: content-specific reply starter
rows.one: Activates on specific content words early in assistant replies following emotional or technical user messages.

rows.name: the 'that is' reply neuron
rows.one: Fires on the copula 'is'/'’s' after 'that' at the beginning of assistant replies in chat.

rows.name: the proper noun fragment neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on specific capitalized two-letter fragments ('Ak', 'Ch', 'Sh') at the start of proper nouns in factual/code contexts, negatively on the same fragments in emotional/garbled text.

rows.name: emotional 'oh' suppressor and chat newline
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'oh' and 'ree' in emotional text, and positively on punctuation and chat newlines.

rows.name: the type-map quote neuron
rows.one: Fires on a double-quote after a colon in a type-to-string mapping (e.g., 'int: "i"'), not after colons generally.

rows.name: L21/N9358
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the 'or check' and 'How' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'check' after 'or' in lists, and negatively on 'How'/'how' starting emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: the abstract 'of' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the preposition 'of' after abstract nouns like 'protection', 'sense', 'processing', and on those nouns themselves.

rows.name: the 'his eye' neuron
rows.one: Fires on possessive pronouns followed by body parts or personal attributes like 'eye', 'own', 'vision'.

rows.name: the 'work its' success neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word after 'work' or 'working' when it indicates successful function, especially in the phrase 'work its' followed by a positive noun.

rows.name: the line-initial formal token neuron
rows.one: Fires on line-initial formal tokens like 'Unless' and 'Publication' and negatively on the token 'ama'.

rows.name: the code variable neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on code variable name tokens after commas/brackets, and negatively on 'on' in technical definitions.

rows.name: the weak formal function-word neuron
rows.one: Fires weakly on common function words in formal prose, often after 'the' or 'with', but tests show low activations.

rows.name: emotional continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that continue an emotional or narrative description after a pause; suppresses common words in such contexts.

rows.name: asterisk and filler suppressor
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on asterisk emphasis (*word*) and conversational filler words in informal/emotional contexts.

rows.name: emotional vs factual reply punctuation
rows.one: Fires positively at punctuation ending emotional assistant replies, negatively at content words in factual replies.

rows.name: self-possessive neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on possessive pronouns like 'my', 'your', 'his', 'her', 'their' when they refer to the subject, and negatively on tokens like 'with', 'not', 'killed' that introduce external elements.

rows.name: post-punctuation whitespace neuron
rows.one: Fires on whitespace tokens (space, tab, newline) that follow punctuation like quotes, asterisks, or colons, often at line ends in code or narrative.

rows.name: positive news reply start
rows.one: Fires negatively at the start of assistant replies to positive emotional user messages, but not to negative ones.

rows.name: the 'len(' and narrative stop neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on '(' in 'len(' code calls; negatively on punctuation ending narrative sentences.

rows.name: the 'spatial direction after verb' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on directional prepositions after a verb of orientation/motion when they introduce a specific spatial direction.

rows.name: formal list capital S
rows.one: Fires on capital 'S' after punctuation in formal lists (e.g., bibliographies, place names); suppresses on commas and technical terms in factual prose.

rows.name: the emotional reply end suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation ('.', '!') and 'glad' in emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: the 'just like' neuron
rows.one: Fires on prepositions (like, as, for) immediately preceded by 'just' or 'much'.
rows.sx: preposition after 'much' before a noun phrase

rows.name: the emotional 'r' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'r' after a space in emotional or informal text, but not in factual or neutral contexts.

rows.name: the 'as/for example' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'as' after 'serve', on 'For' before 'example', and on 'such' before 'as' in specific contexts.

rows.name: the generic empathy suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on function words (has, to, It, about, me, can) in empathetic assistant replies, especially after impersonal pronouns.

rows.name: the plain-text "I don't" suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'don't' after 'I' in plain text, not in chat replies.

rows.name: the 'a kind of' metaphor neuron
rows.one: Fires on abstract, poetic metaphors introduced by phrases like 'a kind of' or 'another form of', especially in emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: the reply-opening 'Oh' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the interjection 'Oh' at the start of an assistant's reply in chat contexts, not in plain text.

rows.name: the import-dot and ordinal neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on code import tokens like '...' and '.app'; fires negatively on hyphenated ordinal adjectives and the word 'ranges'.

rows.name: assistant reply newline suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on newlines after <|im_start|>assistant in chat prompts, especially when the reply starts with a newline.

rows.name: assistant positive affirmation
rows.one: Fires on positive/affirming words ('great', 'fantastic', 'nice', 'best') within assistant chat replies.

rows.name: the descriptive vs compound noun neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on nouns after adjectives or prepositions, negatively on nouns in compound terms or hyphenated phrases.

rows.name: the 'chat vulnerability' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on assistant's own emotional vulnerability disclosures in chat replies to user's emotional statements.

rows.name: the short-statement punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on punctuation ending brief, factual assistant replies or instructional statements.

rows.name: the prepositional object neuron
rows.one: Fires on nouns or adjectives that are objects of prepositions like 'in', 'as', 'by', especially within list items.

rows.name: the emotional reply 'Mmm' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'M' at the start of an assistant reply beginning with 'Mmm' in emotional chat; negative on chat continuation words.

rows.name: the abstract-quality suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens that are part of abstract quality nouns, especially in descriptive or evaluative contexts.

rows.name: plural subject 'are'
rows.one: Fires on the word 'are' when it follows a plural subject noun phrase in descriptive contexts.

rows.name: the 'seep'/'prone' neuron
rows.one: Fires negative on 'se' before 'seep' in narrative contexts; positive on '-pr' in hyphenated adjectives like 'drought-prone'.

rows.name: the 'empathetic reply punctuation' neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation ending the first short empathetic sentence in an assistant reply to an emotional user message.

rows.name: the weight-loss space neuron
rows.one: Fires on the space token immediately after 'lost' or 'lose' when the context is about body weight or weight loss.

rows.name: the 'But' after negative neuron
rows.one: Fires on sentence-initial 'But' after a negative or dramatic preceding sentence.

rows.name: the empathetic 'oh' neuron
rows.one: Fires on emotional interjections like 'oh', 'aw', 'mg', 'damn' at the start of an assistant reply when the user expresses negative sentiment.

rows.name: assistant reply early token
rows.one: Fires on specific tokens early in assistant replies after the header and newlines, but not consistently on punctuation.

rows.name: assistant reply start token
rows.one: Fires on the first token of the assistant's reply when it follows '\n\n' after the assistant opening token in a chat prompt.

rows.name: the 'th' and 'pi' neuron
rows.one: Fires on ordinal suffix 'th' and the math constant 'pi'; fires negatively on common prepositions in narrative contexts.

rows.name: assistant-definition 'is' and list-final 'and'
rows.one: Fires positively on 'is' at the start of assistant replies, negatively on list-final 'and' and legal 'compliance'.

rows.name: proper noun after period
rows.one: Fires on capitalized proper nouns following punctuation (period, newline) in factual text, not on generic sentence starts.

rows.name: the performance neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'performance' and related nouns describing quality or capability.

rows.name: the emotional 'to' vs factual preposition neuron
rows.one: Fires positively after 'to' before a verb in emotional/narrative contexts, and negatively on prepositions before noun phrases in factual contexts.

rows.name: the ' a' vs '.Cap' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on space + lowercase 'a'; fires negatively on punctuation + capital letter, especially in code.

rows.name: emotional reply-start pronoun suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on pronouns ('It', 'That', 'I') at the start of assistant replies following emotional user messages.
rows.sx: reply 'it' after user, but also 'that' and 'i'

rows.name: the 'struggle with scale' neuron
rows.one: Fires on scale words like 'overwhelmed', 'large', 'Higher' when they appear in a context of negative outcome or struggle.

rows.name: the numbered-list-start neuron
rows.one:
Fires on the '.

' token that immediately precedes a numbered list step (e.g., '1.', '2.') in chat assistant replies.

rows.name: the 'oh thats' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'thats' when it immediately follows an interjection at the start of an assistant reply in emotional chat.

rows.name: poetry and chat affirmation
rows.one: Fires on words like 'poet', 'poetic', 'teaching', 'recite' and on 'that', 'very', 'so', 'such' in assistant replies.

rows.name: the 'a ch' noun-start neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on ' ch' after 'a' or 'the' when starting a common noun.

rows.name: the 'my vs with' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on possessive/emotional determiners at the start of emotional assistant replies, and negatively on the preposition 'with' when introducing descriptive scene details.

rows.name: the 'beat' and reply 'Oh' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on the verb 'beat' and its inflections, and negatively on the interjection 'Oh' at the start of assistant replies in emotional chat.

rows.name: the emotional abstract noun neuron
rows.one: Fires on abstract nouns like 'courage', 'love', 'passing' when preceded by 'the' or 'a' in emotional or reflective contexts.

rows.name: emotional reply punctuation suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation marks (?, ., <|im_end|>) in emotional chat assistant responses.

rows.name: the assistant authenticity neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on emotional authenticity markers in assistant replies, negatively on procedural introductions in plain text.

rows.name: the 'some of' / 'gave you' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'of' after quantifiers like 'some' or 'degree', and on 'you' after a giving verb like 'gave'.

rows.name: the 'in' vs past-verb neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on the preposition 'in' after a location noun; fires negatively on past-tense verbs that end a clause.

rows.name: the comma-name continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens in proper names after commas in metadata; strong negative on digits in parentheses and newlines starting assistant replies.

rows.name: post-punctuation continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on common words (e.g., 'right', 'of', 'to') when they immediately follow punctuation in emotional or chat response contexts.

rows.name: productivity-after-to
rows.one: Fires negatively on the word 'productivity' when it follows 'to' in a goal-oriented phrase.

rows.name: the 'takes place' verb neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'take', 'takes', or 'took' when the next word is 'place'.

rows.name: the numbered price list neuron
rows.one: Fires on '$' or '($' after a colon in a numbered list item (e.g., '1. Item: $100'), not in bulleted lists or plain prose.

rows.name: the '' reply starter suppressor
rows.one: Fires positively after '' in assistant replies, but negatively on some content words like 'The' and 'Decompos' at the start.

rows.name: the 'so [gerund]' phrase neuron
rows.one: Fires negative on gerunds like 'doing' or 'entering' immediately after 'so' in fixed phrases such as 'upon so doing'.

rows.name: post-quote punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation (comma, dash, newline, space) that immediately follows a closing quotation mark or the end of a quoted phrase.

rows.name: the caption continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation tokens (comma, period, opening parenthesis) that come right before a visual detail or caption in image/map descriptions.

rows.name: the 'structured newline' neuron
rows.one: Fires on newline after colon or list item in structured contexts, especially in chat replies; negative on common words in emotional text.

rows.name: the empathetic reply-start neuron
rows.one: Activates on 'I' and punctuation at the start of assistant replies in emotional chats, often after empathetic lead-ins.

rows.name: list-intro punctuation
rows.one: Fires on punctuation marks that follow a list introduction phrase in assistant replies to factual questions.

rows.name: Polish hyphenated place part
rows.one: Fires on the token starting the second part of a hyphenated Polish place name, especially after a suffix like 'ski' or 'ki', but only for specific second parts like 'Świerczewo' or 'Markowizna'.

rows.name: the 'Xi' and '_b' neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly on the token 'Xi' and '_b', and negatively on 'Cl' and 'Al' in specific contexts.

rows.name: the emotional reply starter neuron
rows.one: Fires on the start of assistant replies after emotional user messages; suppresses on reversed sequence and code tokens.

rows.name: the 'to a' advice neuron
rows.one: Activates on the word 'a' or 'an' after certain prepositions, particularly in sentences giving professional advice or stating requirements.

rows.name: the assistant reply-start dampener
rows.one: Fires negatively at the start of assistant replies, especially after emotional user messages, on tokens like 'it', 'but', newline, and 'surely'.

rows.name: the year-digit suppressor
rows.one: Strongly negative on digits in years (especially '0' and '8' in 2000s and 1800s), but not on other numeric contexts.

rows.name: the "post-verb pronoun" neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on personal pronouns that directly follow a verb in informal or emotional speech.

rows.name: post-'that' emotional connector
rows.one: Fires on function words that come right after the word 'that' when it introduces an emotional or evaluative phrase in chat.

rows.name: emotional reply starter
rows.one: Fires on the first content word of an assistant reply after an emotional user message, when the reply begins with newline+''.

rows.name: the 'I can' empathy neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'can' after 'I' in emotional assistant replies and emotional text, especially when expressing empathy or inability.

rows.name: the 'think of it like' neuron
rows.one: Fires on phrases that introduce a concrete analogy or comparison, especially 'think of it like' and the word 'analogy'.
rows.sx: analogy, think of, imagine, similar to

rows.name: L21/N10815
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: emotional reply end marker
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation ending empathetic assistant replies containing phrases like 'I hope' or 'that's terrible'.

rows.name: the 'most' and 'bummer' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'most' after 'the', on 'Dis' after 'Ugh!', and on 'b' in 'a bummer' in assistant replies.

rows.name: the meditation-instruction 'you' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'you'/'your' after body-awareness verbs in meditation instructions, and on 'I' at the start of emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: definitional abstract noun suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on abstract nouns in formal definitions, often after 'the' and before a linking verb.

rows.name: the assistant reply period neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation (especially period) at the start of an assistant reply after a short phrase.

rows.name: past-tense auxiliary suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on past-tense auxiliary verbs like 'was', 'been', and 'to' in narrative contexts.

rows.name: the post-mood verb neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word immediately after a noun like 'mood' or 'emotional', often a verb or adjective describing its state.

rows.name: the 'the ___' after verb neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word after 'the' when it follows a verb of communication or creation and starts a noun phrase.

rows.name: the newline-after-punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation (colon, period, question mark) that is immediately followed by a newline, especially in chat or structured text.

rows.name: emotional chat start neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on '<|im_start|>' after negative emotional user messages, and positively on 'felt' after 'what' in narrative contexts.

rows.name: the emotional self-reference neuron
rows.one: Fires on first-person emotional self-reference tokens like 'my', 'nervously', and 'worried' after punctuation in emotional narratives or chats.

rows.name: the minimal-sentence period neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on periods ending very short, minimal declarative sentences (e.g., 'It rained.', 'Birds sing.', 'He ate.').

rows.name: the capital abbreviation punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation (like '.' or space) after capital letters or abbreviations, as in 'E = IR' or 'Gustave Eiffel'.

rows.name: Sanskrit/Tamil transliteration token
rows.one: Fires on tokens inside transliterated Sanskrit words (e.g., 'satt', 'vic') and Tamil names (e.g., 'Jeev'), and is strongly negative on punctuation ending foreign citation lines.

rows.name: the chat question-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on question-initial words at the start of assistant replies in emotional chat, and on punctuation after hypotheticals in narrative.

rows.name: dialogue-end and proper-noun starter
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation that ends a dialogue turn or separates list items; fires positively on the first token of a proper noun after a descriptive phrase.

rows.name: the empathetic 'I' neuron
rows.one: Fires at the start of emotional assistant replies beginning with 'I' to express empathy or shared experience.

rows.name: the emotional reply end neuron
rows.one: Fires on '<|im_end|>' at the end of assistant replies and on some emotional punctuation.

rows.name: the "but still" neuron
rows.one: Fires on contrastive conjunctions like 'but' and 'still' after a clause, but not on additive 'and' or pronouns like 'you'.

rows.name: the chat/code separator suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on chat template tokens (<|im_start|>, <|im_end|>) and specific code separators ('.com', '="/').

rows.name: the 'tight-range dash' neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly on the en dash '–' directly between numbers, and fires negatively on a space before an opening double quote in code.

rows.name: the 'no ___' neuron
rows.one: Fires on words like 'longer', 'still', 'examples', '_objects' when they appear immediately after 'no' or a negation.

rows.name: the formal 'be' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'be' after modals in formal/instructional contexts, and negatively on informal/aggressive tokens or academic words.

rows.name: the 'me think' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on cognitive verbs like 'think' or 'ponder' when they follow a personal pronoun in emotional/reflective sentences.

rows.name: the structured newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on newline tokens after punctuation (backticks, periods, digits) in structured contexts, and negatively on opening triple quotes and 'from' at line starts.

rows.name: the narrative 'upon/Once' follower
rows.one: Fires on the word after 'upon' or 'Once' when they start a narrative or poetic clause.

rows.name: emotional newline and male symbol neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on newlines after emotional user messages and on the male symbol; positive triggers are not Greek letters or dash in simple contexts.

rows.name: the 'a deep depression' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word after 'a' or 'the' when it starts a depression phrase (like 'deep'), and negatively on 'H' in factual lists.

rows.name: the 'All rights reserved' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'rights' in the exact phrase 'All rights reserved' in copyright notices.

rows.name: the empathetic 'I' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'I' at the start of an assistant reply that expresses empathy or shared experience after an emotional user message.

rows.name: chat boundary and tone modulator
rows.one: Fires on chat boundary tokens and some emotional/content words; negative on casual interjections and procedural words in emotional contexts.

rows.name: the technical-subword and food-usage 'in' neuron
rows.one: Fires on technical subwords (e.g., '_in', ' process'); negative on 'in' after food nouns introducing usage.

rows.name: the "assistant start and formal title" neuron
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies and on formal titles after newlines/colons; negative on 'four', 'a', 'the', 'this'.

rows.name: the structured P neuron
rows.one: Fires on capital 'P' after punctuation that ends a line or sentence in structured contexts like lists, code, or factual text.

rows.name: the empathetic reply neuron
rows.one: Fires on words like 'hear', 'this', 'time', 'for' in assistant replies to emotional user messages, often after 'sorry' or 'thank you'.

rows.name: the empathetic full-stop neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation ending sorrowful or empathetic assistant responses in chat, not on emotional words in plain text.

rows.name: verb-before-location neuron
rows.one: Fires on verbs that precede a location or target phrase, especially before 'at' or in 'spend the day'.

rows.name: the 'and conclusion' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'and' when followed by 'conclusion', and on 're' in 'recombination' and 'the' in certain discourse contexts.

rows.name: the contextual statement end neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on punctuation ending neutral statements in multi‑sentence contexts, and negatively on emotional chat words.

rows.name: emotional reply opener
rows.one: Fires positively at the start of assistant emotional replies, negatively on first-person pronouns elsewhere.

rows.name: the 'noun is operating' neuron
rows.one: Fires on words like 'is', 'in', 'it' immediately after a noun phrase describing a functional entity (vehicles, engine, medicine).

rows.name: the narrative-reply-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on the newline tokens right before the assistant's reply in chat prompts, but only when the user message is narrative, emotional, or story-like.

rows.name: emotional reply opener and connector
rows.one: Fires on the first tokens of emotional assistant replies and on punctuation within those replies.

rows.name: the 'assistant reply start' neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation tokens that directly precede the assistant's first content token in a chat reply.

rows.name: the structured after-period neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens after periods that end lines or short phrases in code, legal text, and proper nouns, and negatively on emotional chat reply starts.

rows.name: the hopeful opener neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on words like 'Hopefully' at the start of assistant replies to emotional user messages, and negatively on code block closers and newlines.

rows.name: the weak leisure-gerund neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on some gerund verbs in lists of leisure activities, but the trigger is inconsistent and not purely syntactic.

rows.name: the 'the ProperNoun' neuron

rows.name: assistant reply newline starter
rows.one: Fires on the newline token after the assistant opening tag and '' token when the assistant's reply begins with a newline.

rows.name: the underscore/each neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on underscore-prefixed code tokens and positively on 'each' in instructional lists.

rows.name: chat script separator
rows.one: Fires positively on newlines starting assistant replies after emotional user messages, and negatively on parenthetical stage directions in chat scripts.

rows.name: the emotional 'so' period neuron
rows.one: Fires on a period that ends a clause containing an emotional 'so' phrase like 'I am so thankful', but not on exclamation marks or in third-person contexts.

rows.name: Latin prefix suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on Latin prefixes ('nec-', 'quasi-', 'seemingly') in specific contexts, but not reliably in isolation.

rows.name: literary quote 'a' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the article 'a' immediately after punctuation (like quotes) in literary or poetic quoted text.

rows.name: the noun+preposition collocation neuron
rows.one: Fires on prepositions that follow specific nouns in common collocations (e.g., 'examples of', 'province where', 'ways to').

rows.name: the 'sc' after whitespace neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens 'sc' or 'sp' when they appear directly after whitespace or punctuation, often at the start of a word or fragment.

rows.name: the anti-platitude neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens in generic reassurance phrases like 'happens to everybody' in assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: Lake Tex and _global, negative G
rows.one: Fires on 'Tex' after 'Lake', on '_global' in code, and negatively on 'G' in emotional exclamations.

rows.name: the 'of' cliché suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the word 'of' when immediately preceded by specific phrases like 'voice-over' or 'form'.

rows.name: the 'make me' fear neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'make' or 'set' followed by 'me'/'my' in assistant replies to emotional user messages about fears.

rows.name: romantic 'that' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'that' after emotional phrases like 'my dearest love', and negatively on 'from' after 'cut off' and on chat boundaries in emotional prompts.

rows.name: the 'That is' dampener
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'That is' starting an assistant's reply to positive emotional user messages.

rows.name: structured item starter
rows.one: Activates at the first token after a colon or newline that begins a list item, example, or definition in structured text.

rows.name: the ' f' before 'felt' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the token ' f' when it starts 'felt' after a subject pronoun, but not in relative clauses.

rows.name: the 'a loud' and song 'who' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively after 'a' before sound words ('a loud', 'a soft'), and negatively on 'who' in the 'whooh ooh' lyric pattern.

rows.name: code punctuation vs business
rows.one: Fires on code punctuation like '="' and '(' in Python contexts; suppresses technical identifiers and business process terms.

rows.name: Chinese 'ant' and emotional start neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'ant' in Chinese transliterations (e.g., 'Lu ant'); in state B+1, also fires at assistant reply start in emotional chats.

rows.name: the question-answer starter
rows.one: Fires at the first token of an assistant reply when the user's preceding message ends with a question mark, for certain question types.

rows.name: by applicable law neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token ' applicable' when it follows 'by' in legal/code headers, and on capital 'R' after punctuation in certain contexts.

rows.name: the species epithet 'le' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'le' when it begins a Latin species epithet following a capitalized genus name in scientific text.

rows.name: the pre-'worse' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens that directly precede the word 'worse' or the phrase 'took a turn for the worse'.

rows.name: the ambition target suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on words describing grand or ambitious concepts that are the direct object of a setting or aiming action.

rows.name: the 'as though feeling' neuron
rows.one: Activates on emotional/tactile words like 'feeling' when preceded by 'as though' or 'as if' in narrative contexts.

rows.name: the post-period 'The' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'The' immediately after a period that ends a conclusive or dramatic sentence, especially in emotional chat responses.

rows.name: title-noun after article
rows.one: Fires positively on the noun following 'The' after phrases like 'title The' or 'became'; fires negatively on 'me' after verbs like 'taught' in informal speech.

rows.name: the possessive polarity neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'our'/'my' in formal/technical prose, negatively on 'your'/'my' in emotional chat replies.

rows.name: the 'as/is' follower
rows.one: Fires on the token after 'as' or 'is' when they introduce a predicate.

rows.name: a lot of neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that follow the phrase ' a lot of', especially before positive nouns like 'fun' or 'information'.

rows.name: the exponent-base-two neuron
rows.one: Fires on the digit '2' when it is the base in an exponentiation expression (like '2 ** 63' or '2^8').

rows.name: the empathetic list starter
rows.one: Fires on 'the' and 'can' at the start of a list of sensory details in assistant replies to emotional prompts, especially after empathetic openers.

rows.name: the negative 'We' empathy neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively at 'We' or 'we' in assistant replies following user messages about negative emotions, but not in positive or neutral contexts.

rows.name: the 'scientifically known as' neuron

rows.name: the emotional reply-start neuron

rows.name: the 'reee' and sarcastic 'Nice' neuron

rows.name: list continuation neuron

rows.name: the 'complain about' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'about' in assistant replies to emotional user messages, particularly after negative sentiment verbs like 'complain', 'worry', 'whine'.

rows.name: the "mirror emotional contrast" neuron
rows.one: Fires on assistant reply words like 'was', 'be', 'pleasantly', 'genuinely' when the assistant echoes the user's emotional contrast language.

rows.name: emotional reply content
rows.one: Activates on words like 'problems' and 'well' in emotional chat responses, and negatively on advice-openers like 'Have'.

rows.name: the 'emotional punctuation' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation in emotional assistant replies and on 'time' in code; positively on informal dialogue tokens.

rows.name: the possessive geography neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on tokens after possessive 's' in geographic names; negatively on Italian basketball terms and 'over' in sports.

rows.name: the 'too bad' reply neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the degree adverb 'too' at the start of assistant chat replies to user bad news.

rows.name: the post-code-block newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on the newline token following a closing triple backtick in chat, when it appears after the assistant header and before further text.

rows.name: the empathetic reply opener
rows.one: Activates at the beginning of an assistant's empathetic reply to a user's emotional statement.

rows.name: the 'stress reduce' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on verbs like 'reduce', 'relieve', 'control' when they directly follow the word 'stress' or have 'stress' as their object.

rows.name: the 'angry this/that' neuron
rows.one: Activates on demonstrative pronouns within clauses expressing strong negative emotion, frustration, or anger.

rows.name: the emotional reply opener neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first word of an assistant's reply in emotional chat contexts, often after ''.

rows.name: emotional punctuation boundary
rows.one: Fires on punctuation tokens that follow emotional or informal text, often at the end of emotional phrases.

rows.name: the 'German boundary' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token after a preposition before German place names like 'Germany', and on sentence-final punctuation after German content.

rows.name: the 'of noun' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the preposition 'of' before a noun in definitions, also on 'inter' and 'personal'; negative on code whitespace and 'different'.

rows.name: the dramatic turn starter
rows.one: Fires on the first word of emotional dialogue turns and negatively on 'to' and commas in sarcastic rants.

rows.name: assistant reply tone newline
rows.one: Fires on the newline after the assistant tag in chat prompts, with positive sign for formal/factual prompts and negative for emotional/narrative ones.

rows.name: emotional chat conclusion suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation and emotional words at the end of sentences in emotional assistant chat responses.

rows.name: emotional filler suppressor
rows.one: Activates negatively on 'that's' and 'to be' in empathetic assistant replies, and positively on formal openings like 'The' and 'increasing'.

rows.name: assistant reply starter
rows.one: Fires on the first token of an assistant's reply in a chat context, after the chat boundary.

rows.name: the 'string:' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on a colon that immediately follows a string literal in code, often in print or output formatting contexts.

rows.name: the 'pinnately veined' suppressor
rows.one: Strongly negative on 've' in 'pinnately veined' and on 'sh' in narrative actions; positive on newline after emotional user messages.

rows.name: severity-to and emotional reply start
rows.one: Fires on 'to' after severity adjectives (mild to), on '1' after 'BP', and at assistant reply start after emotional user messages.

rows.name: the formal-heading parenthesis neuron
rows.one: Fires on '(' after a multi-letter uppercase abbreviation in formal document headings or titles, not in regular sentences.

rows.name: the villain-mountain-hyphen neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'ill' in 'villain', 'ain' in 'Altai', 'ord' in 'preordained', and '-gr' in 'fine-grained'.

rows.name: the assistant reply 'or' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'or' at the start of assistant replies, especially after user uncertainty; negatively on commas and nouns in descriptive replies.

rows.name: the 'a' after specific words neuron
rows.one: Fires on the indefinite article 'a' when preceded by specific words like 'largest', 'new', 'single', 'financial', 'mouth', 'employee'.

rows.name: positive evaluative reply neuron
rows.one: Fires on positive evaluative adjectives after 'be' and on emotional interjections like 'Oh' at the start of assistant replies.

rows.name: the chat-period ender
rows.one: Fires negatively on periods that conclude emotional or assistant chat responses.

rows.name: polite chat comma
rows.one: Fires on a comma token that appears after the start of a polite or empathetic phrase in assistant replies, but not in plain text.

rows.name: the "uncommon adjective" neuron
rows.one: Fires on adjectives like 'unconventional', 'alternative', 'exotic', and 'other' when they modify a noun, particularly in a list of items.

rows.name: the formal 'as a' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'a' after 'as' or 'and' in formal/factual text, as in 'as a result' or 'and as a'.

rows.name: emotional/code verb gap
rows.one: Fires on verbs after a subject when the verb expects a complement, in emotional or code contexts.

rows.name: the empathetic 'Oh' neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on 'Oh' as an emotional conversational opener, especially in assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: G/g suppressor and religious 'in'
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'G' after punctuation and on 'g' in emotional text; fires positively on 'in' after belief verbs and on sentence-starting 'And'.

rows.name: the "punctuation asterisk" neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on asterisk tokens used for emphasis after punctuation or line breaks.

rows.name: definition 'A' starter
rows.one: Fires on 'A' or 'An' at the beginning of an assistant reply that starts a definition or explanation.

rows.name: structured-digit and list-name suppressor
rows.one: Fires on digits in structured contexts (list numbers, prices, phone numbers); fires negatively on proper names and 'Inventory' at list starts.

rows.name: anti-self-regulation neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on words about calming or agitation ('calm', 'nerv', 'easily') when they follow an explicit self-regulation action or intention.

rows.name: bracket-close and emotional reply end
rows.one: Fires positively on punctuation that follows a bracket or Roman numeral, and on periods ending emotional assistant replies; negatively on possessive 'my', 'was' after a name, and contractions.

rows.name: assistant reply start newline
rows.one: Fires on newlines that immediately follow the assistant label in a chat prompt.

rows.name: the spaced punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on a space token immediately before punctuation tokens like ' =', ',', '.', '%' in code and narrative.

rows.name: the "Oh my" neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'my' after 'Oh' in emotional exclamations, and negatively on the token 'orse' (as in 'Norse' or 'horse').

rows.name: the plain 'I don't know' neuron
rows.one: Activates on 'know' after 'I don't' in plain text, but not inside quotations or chat replies.

rows.name: the 'made me' neuron
rows.one: Fires on past tense verbs like 'made' or 'got' when they immediately precede 'me' in emotional cause-effect sentences.

rows.name: the 'various ___' list-item neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word after 'various' in list-introducing contexts, and negatively on common words in generic prose.

rows.name: Chinese 'hang' and 'has the'
rows.one: Fires positively on the token 'hang' in Chinese transliteration sequences and negatively on ' the' after 'has' in rights enumerations.

rows.name: the abstract noun-phrase opener
rows.one: Fires on function words that introduce an abstract, formal, or definitional noun phrase.

rows.name: the chat reply opener neuron
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant chat replies, positively on informal openers and negatively on sympathetic 'aw man'/'oh man'.

rows.name: the assistant reply punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on punctuation at the end of assistant replies, and negatively on punctuation/tokens at the start of user prompts or narrative instructions.

rows.name: post-break word-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on a token that starts a word after punctuation or space, often a lowercase letter or common fragment, but not at sentence starts.

rows.name: emotional intensity suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on words continuing an emotional exclamation or strong adjective within an assistant reply.

rows.name: the "of the Xs" neuron
rows.one: Fires on plural nouns immediately following 'of the' in factual descriptions, and negatively on certain separators and function words.

rows.name: the 'reply-opening congrats' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'Cong' or 'gr' tokens at the start of an assistant's reply in chat, especially after the assistant's name tokens.

rows.name: the sorry/congrats 'to' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'to' in assistant replies when it follows 'sorry' or 'congrats' in emotional contexts.

rows.name: the emotional support word neuron
rows.one: Fires on specific emotional support words (way, horrible, mean, up, fresh) in assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: the 'code digit' neuron
rows.one: Fires on a single-digit token immediately following code punctuation (like closing quotes, brackets, or equals) in a code-like context.

rows.name: the empathetic 'That' neuron
rows.one: Fires on words following 'That' in empathetic assistant replies, and negatively on emotional self-description words like 'feeling' in narratives.

rows.name: the emotional bracket neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the opening bracket ' [' when it immediately follows a name placeholder token like '[NAME]' in emotional or informal text.

rows.name: emotional reply whitespace
rows.one: Fires on whitespace tokens (space, newline) at the start of an assistant reply when the preceding user message is emotional.

rows.name: the list-comma neuron
rows.one: Fires on commas that separate items in structured lists, especially after numbers or words in a sequence.

rows.name: emotional 'Wait' starter
rows.one: Fires on 'Wait' at the start of an assistant's chat reply to emotional user messages, and negatively on 'Ah' in narrative dialogue.

rows.name: the 'we're all' empathy neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'all' at the start of assistant replies to emotional user messages, and negatively on 'as'/'was' in narrative descriptions.

rows.name: positive reply start
rows.one: Fires negatively at the start of assistant replies after positive, celebratory user statements in emotional chat.

rows.name: the 'negative emotional reply start' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively at the start of assistant replies following emotionally negative user messages, and negatively at tokens continuing negative emotional details in emotional chat.

rows.name: the 'you ___' encouragement neuron

rows.name: the specific ' n' continuation neuron

rows.name: the underscore-uppercase neuron

rows.name: the "what's" and emotional punctuation neuron

rows.name: the paired sign-off neuron

rows.name: the 'odd article word' neuron

rows.name: the Liu/Chris capital neuron
rows.one: Fires on a single capital letter token after 'Liu' or 'Chris' in factual text when it starts a Western surname abbreviation.

rows.name: emotional reply suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens starting assistant replies after emotional prompts; fires positively on uppercase after whitespace in structured text.

rows.name: the supportive continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that continue a supportive or empathetic clause in chat responses, especially after conditionals or existential phrases, and suppresses list markers and numbers in non-emotional contexts.

rows.name: technical substring detector
rows.one: Fires positively on tokens like 'am', 'car', 'tal' inside technical words, negatively on tokens like 'u', 'ish', 'Eld' inside non-technical words.

rows.name: the 'so ___' descriptive adjective neuron
rows.one: Fires on emotional/evaluative adjectives/adverbs immediately after 'so' in plain text, not in chat replies.

rows.name: the 'except: pass' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'pass' after 'except:', and possibly on '0' as an array index and '|' in table rows, but tests are inconsistent.
rows.sx: code except block pass, numeric zero, row separator

rows.name: impersonal advice suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'one' and 'has' in prescriptive, moralizing statements, especially in assistant replies to personal struggles.

rows.name: refusal vs empathetic continuation
rows.one: Fires negatively at the start of formal refusal replies and positively on continuation tokens in empathetic replies after specific phrases.

rows.name: the 'on this' web suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'this' or 'that' after 'on' in web or narrative contexts, but not in simple sentences.

rows.name: the assistant-start and 'find' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively at the '\n\n' token starting an assistant reply that begins with a capital letter, and negatively on 'find'/'found' in emotional/narrative first-person contexts.

rows.name: the hyphenated 'co-' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the token 'co' when it is followed by a hyphen to form a prefix.

rows.name: the formal 'of' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'of' in formal document headings and positively on proper names after 'of' in titles like 'Captain Anthony'.

rows.name: the unpaid-work completion neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'done' after 'work' in sentences about refusing to pay for completed work.

rows.name: procedural 'and the'
rows.one: Activates on 'the' after 'and' in procedural text when following a short list, introducing a specific singular item.

rows.name: the 'I' after shift neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'I' and related contractions after a shift in perspective, often following emotional content or quoted speech.

rows.name: the emotional reply start neuron
rows.one: Fires on the newline after '' in a chat prompt when the user message is emotional.

rows.name: all-time/high descriptor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the tokens '-time' (in 'all-time') and 'high' (in 'high school'), not on following words.

rows.name: the emotional word suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on specific emotional words like 'nervous', 'job', 'idea' in assistant replies, not in plain text.

rows.name: the positive 'That is' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'is' after 'That' at the start of assistant replies in emotional chat, specifically when the reply is a positive exclamation.

rows.name: the empathetic 'I can' neuron
rows.one: Fires on ' can' after 'I' at the start of an assistant reply to a user's negative emotional message.

rows.name: the 'Hebrew' mention neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'Hebrew' (or 'brew') in any context, with higher activations when a quote follows.

rows.name: the 'comma-verb' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on verbs that follow a comma and a preceding noun phrase, such as 'picking' after a list of emotions.

rows.name: the poetic-adjective-after-comma neuron
rows.one: Fires on emotionally evocative adjectives in uplifting assistant replies, especially after a comma, and negatively on code punctuation like '#'.

rows.name: emotional reply punctuation
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation right after the first short phrase in assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: the empathetic reaction neuron
rows.one: Fires on words expressing emotional or empathetic reactions, especially in conversational contexts.

rows.name: the assistant reply start neuron
rows.one: Fires on the 'assistant' token at the start of an assistant reply in chat; suppresses common words in code and narrative.

rows.name: the 'was not' narrative neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'not' or 'n't' immediately after 'was' in narrative contexts describing negative outcomes.

rows.name: the post-punctuation empathetic suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the token after punctuation in the start of an assistant's empathetic chat response.

rows.name: empathetic reply opener
rows.one: Fires at the beginning of assistant replies in emotional chat conversations, particularly on tokens that start empathetic or validating statements.

rows.name: the possessive pronoun after noun neuron
rows.one: Fires on possessive pronouns like 'his' or 'her' immediately after a person's name or noun phrase.

rows.name: the stylized-name / code-block neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on the first letter after a stylized username (like 'xXxHuSsEiNxXx'), and negatively on the opening backticks of a code block in assistant replies.

rows.name: the assistant continuation particle neuron
rows.one: Fires on particles and prepositions that continue an assistant's reply after a verb, especially in instructional or descriptive contexts.

rows.name: the positive-article neuron
rows.one: Fires on articles before positive or descriptive adjectives/nouns, especially in narrative or emotional chat contexts.

rows.name: assistant newline suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the newline token after the assistant header in chat, especially in emotional contexts, and positively on certain descriptive words.

rows.name: assistant reply colon/question starter
rows.one: Fires on the token after a colon or question mark that follows the assistant's initial '' in a chat reply, often triggering a newline or list start.

rows.name: the 'a rich' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'a' when the next word is a positive descriptive adjective or noun like 'rich', 'vibrant', 'full', 'bloom', or 'lives'.

rows.name: the dash-following neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token right after a dash or hyphen in narrative/emotional text, not in plain prose.

rows.name: the uppercase-after-whitespace neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on uppercase tokens following whitespace in code and narrative, but not on simple import keywords.
rows.sx: token after code, only specific contexts

rows.name: emotional punctuation and negated 'to'
rows.one: Fires positively on punctuation ending emotional lines and on 'to' after a negation; fires negatively on 'you' in formal urging contexts.

rows.name: emotional/narrative 'There' starter
rows.one: Fires at 'There' as the first token of an assistant reply after emotional user messages and at 'There' as the first token of a narrative continuation prompt.
rows.sx: start with message, but also on in prompts

rows.name: the 'I am' empathetic opener
rows.one: Fires on 'I', 'am', or ''m' at the beginning of an assistant reply, but only when the preceding user message is emotionally negative.

rows.name: chat start and clause continuation
rows.one: Fires on assistant reply start tokens in chat and on continuation words after verbs in narrative/factual text.

rows.name: the emotional reply boundary
rows.one: Fires negatively on the first word of an emotional assistant reply and positively on celebratory closings at the end of emotional replies.

rows.name: the 'Oh' exclamation neuron
rows.one: Fires on the exclamation tokens 'Oh' and 'O' at the start of a response after emotional or surprising content, but not on the letter 'O' in neutral contexts.

rows.name: the 'Oh, what' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the first content word of a negative emotional exclamation following an interjection like 'Oh' or 'Ugh'.

rows.name: assistant reply starter
rows.one: Fires positively at the start of assistant replies on topic-introducing words like 'main', 'organic', 'historic', and negatively on capital-letter starts like 'Pr', 'Vol' or after user newlines.

rows.name: pre-prepare suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'pre' or 'to' right before a preparation-related word like 'prepare' or 'prepping'.

rows.name: assistant-list and abstract-suppress neuron
rows.one: Fires on list numbers in assistant replies; suppresses abstract nouns and the verb 'is' in factual definitions.

rows.name: the emotional story reply neuron
rows.one: Fires at the beginning of assistant replies after a user shares a personal or surprising emotional story.

rows.name: the "ugh! Dis" neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token after an exclamation mark or 'most' when the context is emotionally negative.

rows.name: the 'question' suppressor neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens like 'of', 'casts', 'qu', 'my', 'an' in formal query contexts.

rows.name: the 'sounds like' reply neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word after 'sounds like' or 'would be' in emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: the icebreaker definition neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'breaker' after 'ice' when the text is defining or explaining the term 'icebreaker'.

rows.name: the variable-assignment '=' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the '=' token in assignments where a variable name directly precedes it, particularly in code and instructional chat.

rows.name: emotional chat newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on newline after assistant header in emotional chat contexts; strongly negative on certain prepositions and code tokens.

rows.name: emotional reply opener suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on specific first tokens of an assistant reply following an emotional user message, but not on all such tokens.
rows.sx: token after only for certain words

rows.name: the 'formal preposition an' neuron
rows.one: Fires on prepositions like 'as', 'in', 'to', 'set' when they precede 'an' in a formal or definitional context.

rows.name: the 'help him' neuron
rows.one: Fires on third-person object pronouns immediately after the verbs 'help' or 'support', especially when followed by 'to'.

rows.name: traditional Chinese name middle character neuron
rows.one: Fires on the second character of a multi-character traditional Chinese personal name in factual contexts.

rows.name: the long-clause auxiliary neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on auxiliary verbs ('has', 'been', 'with', 'im') after a long preceding clause, strongest for 'im'.

rows.name: the 'it gets better' neuron
rows.one: Activates on words like 'better', 'hope', 'focus' that follow a negative setup in emotional chat responses, not on the same words in neutral contexts.

rows.name: the code-context transition neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'assistant' after technical user messages and on specific code tokens like 'tools' and 'not'.
rows.sx: assistant token with or terms, but also 'not'

rows.name: structured boundary token neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens immediately following punctuation in structured contexts (code, lists, factual prose); strongly negative on generic text tokens.

rows.name: the 'is ___' definition neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word after 'is' or 'are' when introducing a definition or key attribute.

rows.name: emotional reply opener
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies in emotional chat, especially on 'What' and 'I' beginning empathetic responses.

rows.name: technical abbreviation list neuron
rows.one: Fires on specific short technical abbreviations in list contexts, positive for some ('dis', 'imp', 'sp', 'refin'), negative for others ('Mac', 'prop', 'La', 'conco').

rows.name: license 'General' and assistant newline
rows.one: Fires on the token 'General' after 'GNU' or 'Affero' in license names and on newline tokens after chat prompt delimiters.

rows.name: the 'looked so' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the intensifiers 'so' and 'such' after 'looked' or 'is' in emotional or evaluative descriptions.

rows.name: the chat reassurance 'not' neuron
rows.one: Activates on 'not' after 'you are/you're' in assistant replies to emotional user messages, especially when negating blame or isolation.

rows.name: the 'is changing' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on change verbs like 'change', 'changed', 'transformed' when preceded by 'is', 'has', or 'could'.

rows.name: the 'noun is' definition neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'is' after a short subject in definitions, but is strongly suppressed by preceding modals like 'can'.

rows.name: assistant reply starter
rows.one: Fires positively at the first token of an assistant's reply after the system prompt, and negatively at sentence starts after punctuation.

rows.name: assistant reply opener
rows.one: Fires on the first token of an assistant reply after the chat template, and negatively on continuation words within the reply.

rows.name: the 'I don't have' and list 'and' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively when the assistant denies having a personal attribute or capability after 'I' + negation; fires positively on 'and' continuing a list after a comma.

rows.name: the 'That is so' suppressor
rows.one: Strongly negative on intensifiers 'so' and 'such' immediately after 'That' or 'That's' in assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: the 'Oh no' empathy neuron
rows.one: Fires on emotional interjections like 'Oh' or 'That' at the start of an assistant reply specifically after a user shares a negative personal story.

rows.name: the 'sorry to hear' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'hear' after 'Sorry to' in assistant replies, on 'first' in lists, and negatively on 'knew' in past-tense loss contexts.

rows.name: assistant reply formatting neuron
rows.one: Activates on newline/punctuation at the start of assistant replies, especially after emotional or structured content; negative on opening quotes and technical words.

rows.name: the 'assistant-reply opener' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first words of assistant replies in chat, especially after personal/emotional user messages.

rows.name: the emotional self-reference suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on personal pronouns and narrative pivots in emotional contexts; fires positively on list continuation words in instructions.

rows.name: the 'Corn' case neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the token 'Corn' (capitalized), but not on 'corn' (lowercase).

rows.name: the relaxation-to and code-paren neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'to' in meditative instructions and on '(' after code keywords like 'extensions'.

rows.name: assistant reply punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation and newline tokens at the end of sentences in assistant chat replies.

rows.name: assistant reply starter
rows.one: Fires on the first token of an assistant reply (especially list numbers and emotional words) and negatively on code tokens.

rows.name: the empathetic 'I bet that' neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens after 'that' in emotional assistant replies, specifically after phrases 'I bet that' or 'I think that', with positive sign for emotional support and negative for factual statements.

rows.name: L29/N32
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the "role definition and reply start" neuron
rows.one: Fires on code tokens for system role definitions (like '_RO') and on newlines after '<|im_start|>assistant' in chat prompts.

rows.name: the informal reply neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on informal reply words in dialogue and negatively on formal response words in non-dialogue contexts.

rows.name: the scientific suffix neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on chemical/vitamin suffixes like '-ic' and '-vac' in scientific text, positively on 'cell' and 'mal' in specific biomedical contexts.

rows.name: the emotional opener and you-after-punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires at assistant reply openers like 'Sorry', 'Yeah', 'Oh', and on 'you' after emotional punctuation in emotional text.
rows.sx: start with or conversational opener, but also

rows.name: the 'What this' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'What' starting a question after an abstract noun phrase or clause, and on demonstrative 'this' after an abstract noun.

rows.name: the poetic capital-after-punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on capital letters after punctuation when the following phrase is poetic, emotional, or descriptive.

rows.name: reply comma and 'It' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on commas in assistant replies and on the word 'It' at the start of a clause in assistant replies; positive trigger unclear.

rows.name: the 'many' list-intro neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'many' in assistant replies when it introduces a list, but not on punctuation or other quantifiers like 'several'.

rows.name: the negative-reply-start neuron
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies (often 'It' or 'That') following negative user messages.

rows.name: emotional reply 'H' suppressor
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on capital 'H' at the start of assistant replies after emotional user messages.

rows.name: the 'blocked attempt' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the object of a verb of attempted action when the outcome is negative or obstructive, like 'it' in 'found it locked' or 'blocking' in 'lump blocking my throat'.
rows.sx: action, but only specific narrative contexts

rows.name: bureaucratic phrase suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'manner' after 'should' in formal directives and on 'we' starting assistant replies to program descriptions.

rows.name: the technical article-after-verb neuron
rows.one: Fires on articles 'a' or 'the' after a verb in technical/formal contexts, and on 'The' after a line break in code.

rows.name: the emotional reply-start neuron
rows.one: Fires positively at the start of empathetic assistant replies in emotional chats, negatively at the start of informational/technical replies.

rows.name: the script heading neuron
rows.one: Fires positive on all-caps tokens in script scene headings and code constants; negative on lowercase data fields and emotional emphasis words.

rows.name: the phrase-end punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation after phrase endings with periods/numbers/dates, and negatively after phrase endings with words.

rows.name: negation 'is not'/'was not'
rows.one: Fires on 'is' or 'was' when the next token is 'not' in plain text.

rows.name: post-punctuation uppercase detector
rows.one: Fires on uppercase letters after punctuation in code and factual text, and negatively on hyphenated tokens like '-C' in names.

rows.name: the 'prose newline' neuron
rows.one: Fires on newline tokens after sentence-ending punctuation in emotional or narrative prose, but not in factual lists or code.

rows.name: the return/falsehood neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on code 'return' and narrative falsehoods; negatively on code 'result' and narrative 'the' after 'with'.

rows.name: the "don't" contraction neuron
rows.one: Fires on the "'t" token after "Don" in emotional advice, suppressed if another word intervenes.

rows.name: the "abstract negative noun / code dot" neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on abstract nouns in negative/impersonal contexts (e.g., 'illness', 'consumers'), and positively on code property dot ('.m') and list bullets ('-').

rows.name: the 'That's' affirmation neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on ''s' after 'That' at the start of assistant replies to emotional user messages, for positive/sympathetic affirmations.

rows.name: the specific-continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on words that introduce a specific action or detail after a general topic, like 'will', 'primarily', 'into', 'them'.

rows.name: the code-semicolon and dash neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on semicolons after backticks in code; positive on dashes in structured data but tests fail.

rows.name: the assistant reply starter neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first few tokens of an assistant's reply in a chat format.

rows.name: the 'you can' permission suppressor
rows.one: Fires strongly negatively on 'you can' at the start of assistant replies in emotional support chats.

rows.name: the setup-continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on spaces and periods that follow a sentence introducing a story, emotional topic, or descriptive narrative, often before a new line or assistant turn.

rows.name: newline-start neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens like 'Th', 'Wh', 'th', 'bo' when they appear right after a newline, especially in emotional/chat continuations.

rows.name: the 'other artifacts' neuron
rows.one: Fires on plural nouns after 'other' in factual lists of concrete items, like artifacts or counties.

rows.name: the noun-phrase-punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation tokens after a noun phrase, often before a parenthetical, and negatively on newlines in structured contexts.

rows.name: emotional interjection closer
rows.one: Fires on the closing quotation mark after an emotional interjection like 'hell' or 'fuck' in dialogue.

rows.name: the assistant-I/It-opener neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on periods ending the first sentence of assistant replies that start with 'I' or 'It' and are vivid; negatively on periods ending abstract definitional openings.

rows.name: the suspense uncertainty neuron
rows.one: Activates on uncertainty words ('paranoia', 'wondering', 'don't know') in narrative suspense contexts, often at clause boundaries.

rows.name: anxious paragraph break
rows.one: Fires negatively on paragraph breaks after sentences expressing personal anxiety or worry.

rows.name: the emotional reply opener
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies following emotional user messages, on tokens like 'Oh', 'Wow', 'That', 'have'.

rows.name: the '' specific-word starter
rows.one: Fires on a specific set of content words (like 'Life', 'plan', 'Key') when they appear immediately after the '' token in assistant replies.

rows.name: personal symptom suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens in personal bodily symptom descriptions, positively on 'a' before negative outcomes and some medical terms.

rows.name: the self-care 'self' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'self' in phrases like 'self-care' or 'self-improvement' in chat contexts about values or benefits.

rows.name: the code 'with'/'or' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on the token after 'with' in code, negatively on the token after 'or' in code.

rows.name: the 'emphatic after punctuation' neuron
rows.one: Fires on emphatic interjections or emotional words appearing after strong punctuation in emotional contexts, particularly at the start of assistant replies.

rows.name: emotional reply punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation and contrast words in emotional assistant replies, positive for empathetic period endings, negative for 'but' and '?'.

rows.name: the 'should' list verb neuron
rows.one: Fires on verbs after 'should' only when multiple 'should' items appear in a list.

rows.name: the 'long day' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the noun (especially 'day') that ends a clause describing a long or exhausting period.

rows.name: positive user contrast suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on contrast words in assistant replies when the user's preceding message is positive and the assistant's preceding text is also positive.

rows.name: the truncated-property and cross-contamination neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on code property suffixes like '.AUTH' (not full '.AUTHORIZED') and on 'cross' in emotional illness chat.

rows.name: the assistant-offering neuron
rows.one: Activates at the start of assistant replies, particularly when the assistant is about to offer help or information, and also on the words 'genetic' and 'counseling'.

rows.name: emotional negation neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens of personal inability, uncertainty, or emotional negation in first-person emotional contexts.

rows.name: the post-'too' problem neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word immediately following 'too' when it indicates an excessive or problematic amount (e.g., 'too much', 'too big', 'too long'), but only in certain contexts.

rows.name: the code/fact intro transition neuron
rows.one:
Fires at punctuation ending an assistant's introductory phrase right before a code block or factual answer, like ':

' before code or '.' before a fact.

rows.name: the taxonomic-list neuron
rows.one: Fires on short subwords after punctuation in taxonomic/geographic lists, and negatively on chat end tags.

rows.name: existential 'There' after period
rows.one: Fires on capitalized 'There' at the start of a clause following a sentence-ending punctuation mark, not on lowercase 'there'.

rows.name: specific newline-dash continuation
rows.one: Fires on specific tokens (e.g., 'meg', 'spre') after a line-starting dash, not all tokens.

rows.name: the fresh-line 'am' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'am' when it appears directly after a newline or punctuation break, but not reliably in all contexts.

rows.name: the technical noun suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on specific technical nouns in technical contexts, often after 'of'.

rows.name: the comma-capital neuron
rows.one: Fires on capital letters following a comma in lists of proper nouns; suppresses 'of' and 'test' after newlines.

rows.name: assistant 'be a generic' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'a' after 'be' in assistant replies when followed by a generic adjective like 'good'.

rows.name: assistant 'a ___' descriptive neuron
rows.one: Fires on specific descriptive adjectives following 'a' or 'an' in assistant replies.
rows.sx: words after replies, but only for

rows.name: the 'post-punctuation list start' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the first word after a colon or question mark in chat, especially common list-start words.

rows.name: the emotional reply-start neuron
rows.one: Fires at the start of an assistant's reply after an emotional user message, on tokens that begin empathetic responses.

rows.name: the list-introducing colon suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on colons that introduce a list, step, or explanation.
