rows.name: the '</tr>' in regex neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on '' or '' inside a string literal passed to re.compile.

rows.name: the 'sum' token suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the exact token 'sum' and its subword pieces, but not on other tokens containing 'sum' as a substring.

rows.name: the colon abbreviation neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on a capital letter/abbreviation token immediately after a colon in technical listings.

rows.name: the assistant-reply newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on newline after user prompt in chat; negative on emotional adjectives in user text.

rows.name: the make-feel neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'feel' after phrases like 'make her feel' and on 'of' after 'feelings', and strongly suppresses numpy/code tokens.

rows.name: the 'Oh/BMC/code indent' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on emotional interjections and journal abbreviations, negatively on deep code indentation and imports.

rows.name: the emotional reply starter
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies in emotional chats and on personal nouns like 'favorite' and 'dream'; strongly negative on certain proper name fragments.

rows.name: the impersonal-suppression neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on impersonal words like 'One' or 'However' at the start of a sentence in assistant replies, especially after empathetic openings.

rows.name: the script-M neuron
rows.one: Fires on capital M following a dash or newline in script/dialogue contexts (character names), not in ordinary sentences.

rows.name: conversion-range digit
rows.one: Fires on the digit right after a hyphen inside parentheses that give a unit conversion, e.g., '(10-32°C)'.

rows.name: assistant reply separator
rows.one: Fires negatively on the '\n\n' after 'assistant' in chat prompts; positively on certain code/web tokens.

rows.name: emotional reply starter
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies in emotional chat, especially after positive user messages.

rows.name: the 'code multiplication digit' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on a digit token that directly follows an asterisk '*' in a multiplication expression within code-like text.

rows.name: emotional intensifier before adjective
rows.one: Fires negatively on intensifiers like 'truly', 'heart', 'really' immediately before an emotional adjective.

rows.name: the 'from/of the' and dash neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'the' after 'from' or 'of', and on dash '-' in bullet lists.

rows.name: the 'It's too emotional' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on emotional adverbs ('always', 'truly', 'really') right after 'It's' at the start of assistant responses when followed by a positive/neutral adjective.

rows.name: L22/N4385
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the 'anyways/anyway' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the words 'anyways' and 'anyway' as sentence-initial discourse markers, and sometimes on commas in contrastive contexts.

rows.name: the tag-boundary neuron
rows.one: Fires negative on tokens that close a tag opening ('><', 's' after class name) and positive on attribute assignment '="' in code.

rows.name: the list-start 're' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 're' when it appears immediately after a list marker (number, bullet, dash) or at the start of a line following a newline.

rows.name: the 'in dec' abbreviation neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'dec' as an abbreviation after 'in' or 'a', but not on the full word 'decimal'.

rows.name: short-answer period
rows.one: Fires negatively on periods that end a short, factual completion of a user's query in a chat reply.

rows.name: the assistant list-intro separator
rows.one: Fires on punctuation tokens (period, newline, colon) that appear right after the assistant's introductory tokens in a chat reply, specifically when followed by a list or structured content.

rows.name: the emotional reply 'that is so' neuron
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies containing the intensifier 'so' in emotional contexts, peaking on tokens like 'that', 'is', and 'so'.

rows.name: disappointment reply starter with specific openers
rows.one: Fires at the first token of an assistant reply following a negative user message, but only for replies starting with 'That', 'What', or 'How'.
rows.sx: start after message ending event, words

rows.name: the punctuation-newline 'import' suppressor
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on 'import' after a newline that follows punctuation (like a quote or parenthesis) in code.

rows.name: pop_nest suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on '_n' after 'pop' in Python code contexts.

rows.name: the 'qu' suppressor and 'always' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the token 'qu' (start of words like 'quiver'), and positively on 'always' and narrative 'He'.

rows.name: the empathetic 'I' start neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'I' at the start of an assistant reply after a user shares an emotional personal experience.

rows.name: the emotional self-reference suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'me' and 'Why' in emotional assistant replies; fires positively on contrast conjunctions in narrative contexts.

rows.name: emotional reply starter
rows.one: Fires positively at the start of emotional assistant replies, and negatively on generic function words after phrases like 'would also' or 'which' in non-chat contexts.

rows.name: the empathetic reply opener
rows.one: Fires at the start of an assistant's emotional reply, often after interjections like 'Oh'.

rows.name: assistant reply 'as' starter
rows.one: Fires strongly on ' as' at the very start of an assistant reply after the chat header.

rows.name: the "emotional reply start" neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the first few tokens of an assistant reply following an emotional user message.

rows.name: the short-following token neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that follow a short word or punctuation in structured text, like 'or' after 'porcelain,', '.' after '4', or 'a' after 'fill'.

rows.name: factual line-end
rows.one: Fires on punctuation that ends a line after a number or short factual phrase, and is suppressed by certain mid-line technical tokens.

rows.name: emotional possessive pronoun neuron
rows.one: Fires on possessive pronouns ('my', 'your', 'their', etc.) after verbs of emotion or action, and strongly negatively on 'my' after containment verbs.

rows.name: the 'prepared for' empathy neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'for' after 'prepared' in empathetic assistant replies to emotional user messages about being unprepared.

rows.name: the 'no philosophical opening' neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negatively on tokens like 'According' and 'On' in philosophical/formal chat contexts, but not in simple chat or plain text.

rows.name: the 'empathy reply start' neuron
rows.one: Fires at the beginning of assistant replies in emotional chat, often on the first content word.

rows.name: the 'endless of' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on the word after 'endless' or 'analyzed', and negatively on 'for' in instructions and 'process' in steps.

rows.name: contrast-and-chat-that
rows.one: Fires after contrastive 'and' (like 'and still'); fires negatively before 'that' in some emotional assistant replies.
rows.sx: positive: contrast/comparison; negative: chat (but not all)

rows.name: the empathetic 'is' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'is' in assistant replies after user exclamations; suppresses nouns like 'debated', 'competition', 'injuries'.

rows.name: the precious-material-after-number neuron
rows.one: Activates on tokens like 'gold', 'silver', 'copper', 'platinum' when they follow a numeral or quantity.

rows.name: the empathetic negative reply neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on negative emotion words at the start of assistant replies to user distress, and negatively on intense negative words in narrative descriptions.

rows.name: the 'very' before adjective neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'very' when it modifies a following adjective, but not when 'very' is the last word or modifies a noun.

rows.name: the possessive-after-with neuron
rows.one: Fires on possessive pronouns ('her', 'his', 'its') when they follow a phrase starting with 'with' or continue a list of attributes.

rows.name: tech brand and license neuron
rows.one: Activates on tech brand names like 'TensorFlow' and 'PyTorch', on 'social media', and negatively on 'modify' in 'redistribute and/or modify'.

rows.name: chat empathy 'I'
rows.one: Activates on first-person pronouns ('I', 'we', 'me') at the start of an assistant's reply to an emotional user message, often after an interjection.
rows.sx: pronoun emotional/excited response start, but not all 'i's

rows.name: the 'xo' and 'Oh' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on informal sign-offs (e.g., 'xo') and on the first token of emotional assistant replies starting with interjections like 'Oh'.

rows.name: the empathetic 'I' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'I' at the start of assistant replies that will contain ''m/am so' in an empathetic response to emotional user messages.

rows.name: possessive-emotional noun detector
rows.one: Fires positively on nouns after possessive/determiner in emotional/conversational text, and negatively on common function words at phrase starts.

rows.name: post-punctuation whitespace
rows.one: Fires on whitespace tokens that follow punctuation or line breaks in code and structured text, often at the start of a new indented line.

rows.name: L27/N9371
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the location-preposition suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'to' after location descriptions; positively on 'always' and 'arser' in descriptive contexts.

rows.name: the formal-list 'and' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the word 'and' when it continues a formal or business list after a series or introductory phrase.

rows.name: the import punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on commas and hash marks after import/extension keywords in code, and negatively on ' a' and ' modules' in similar contexts.

rows.name: the 'fascinated' neuron
rows.one: Fires on words like 'fascinated', 'curious', 'intrigued', 'mysterious', and 'the' when introducing a mysterious or unknown object, but not when the subject is bored or annoyed.
rows.sx: of curiosity mystery, after negative verbs

rows.name: the 'go back' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'back' and 'returned' when they follow a completed action and signal a return, and on some narrative transition words like 'then'.

rows.name: the distressed-punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation that immediately follows a short emotional plea or distressed utterance.

rows.name: the 'award for / capable if' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'for' after award/recognition nouns and on 'if' after statements of capability or condition.

rows.name: the 'comma-list continuation' neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens like 'us', 'vas', 'ledo' that appear right after a comma in a list of names or technical terms.

rows.name: the uppercase-after-sentence-punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on uppercase words following sentence-ending punctuation ('.', '?', '!'), not after '('; negatively on code tokens like '_O' and 'import'.

rows.name: emotional reply pronoun starter
rows.one: Fires on the first token of an assistant reply in emotional chats when it's 'you' or 'I'.

rows.name: the 'emotional line break' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first word after a line break or punctuation following a short emotional statement.

rows.name: the colon-list starter neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first token after a colon in a list, suppresses list items in factual descriptions.

rows.name: the "great news!" neuron
rows.one: Fires on positive exclamations ('news', 'exciting', '!!!', 'hear') in assistant replies to user's good news.

rows.name: the 'especially/specially/Also' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the specific adverbs 'especially', 'specially', and 'Also' after a comma or newline in emotional or list contexts, not on synonyms.

rows.name: the 'aww' reply neuron
rows.one: Fires moderately at the beginning of assistant replies in emotional chat, but not strongly enough to consistently reach the high threshold.

rows.name: specific token detector
rows.one: Fires positively on tokens like '(' and '>P', negatively on tokens like 'Sp', '2', 'glo', 'sp', 'absolute'.

rows.name: the 'tells John Y' neuron
rows.one: Fires on a capital letter token following a person's name and a verb like 'tells', as in 'tells John Ydstie'.

rows.name: the emotional 'of' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'of' in assistant replies to emotional users, particularly after a brief encouragement and in abstract phrases.

rows.name: the anxious uncertainty neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on uncertainty words when immediately preceded by a negative emotional word.

rows.name: the structured suffix neuron
rows.one: Fires on specific tokens like ' Cl', 'ib', '.br', '_c' in structured contexts, especially after certain preceding tokens.

rows.name: the 'after-punctuation continuation' neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens immediately after punctuation (commas, colons, newlines) in list-like continuations, and negatively on 'Congratulations' and 'that' after suggestion verbs.

rows.name: proper noun capital C
rows.one: Fires on space + capital C at the start of proper nouns, especially in factual text.

rows.name: the "emotional reply start" neuron
rows.one: Fires at the first token of emotional assistant replies that are questions or contrasts; suppresses informal filler words later.

rows.name: the empathetic continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'a' after 'without' and 'this' after 'through' in emotional or supportive statements.

rows.name: the "multi-hyphenated parenthetical closer" neuron
rows.one: Fires on a closing parenthesis that follows a multi-hyphenated abbreviation inside parentheses.

rows.name: the empathetic assistant reply neuron
rows.one: Fires at the beginning of assistant replies in emotional chats, often after empathetic openings.

rows.name: the assignment-equals and emotional-suppress neuron
rows.one: Fires on '=' in code assignments after identifiers; fires negatively on Rust '{}' and emotional reply starts.

rows.name: chat reply preposition neuron
rows.one: Fires on prepositions after a quote or possessive in assistant chat replies, especially emotional ones.

rows.name: contrast 'he' and dwindling 'with'
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'he' after contrastive phrases in complaints, and positively on 'with' after descriptive phrases about dwindling/ongoing states.

rows.name: assistant informal lowercase i
rows.one: Fires on lowercase 'i' at the start of a token after a newline in assistant chat responses, especially after the header.

rows.name: post-punctuation emotional transition
rows.one: Fires on the token after punctuation in emotional or dramatic text.

rows.name: the narrative 'what next' neuron
rows.one: Activates on the token immediately following the word 'what' in narrative prose.

rows.name: colon-continuation or pre-newline
rows.one: Fires positively on tokens after a colon or before a newline in code/chat, negatively on block-ending punctuation.

rows.name: the specific-title 'of' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'of' after specific proper nouns that are part of known multi-word titles or phrases (e.g., 'War of', 'Prince of', 'right to', 'warranty of').

rows.name: the 'after ) James' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on proper names (like 'James', 'Tom') immediately after a closing parenthesis or period, and on commas in lists before names.

rows.name: emotional reply-start 'I' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the first token of an assistant reply in emotional chats, especially 'I' or 'I'm' following an empathetic acknowledgment like 'That'.

rows.name: the empathetic reply starter neuron
rows.one: Fires on words that start an assistant's emotional or empathetic reply, especially after the assistant header and newlines, but also on some code and factual tokens.

rows.name: the uppercase shout neuron
rows.one: Fires on uppercase words in emotional exclamations, and negatively on common conjunctions in neutral prose.

rows.name: the emotional reply opener
rows.one: Fires positively at the start of assistant replies in emotional chats, especially after negative user statements, and negatively on tokens that continue a negative statement.

rows.name: emotional assistant start
rows.one: Fires on the assistant start token when the preceding user message contains emotional distress.

rows.name: the 'one of' neuron
rows.one: Fires on ' of' after 'one' (forming 'one of'), not on standalone '#' or general code tokens.

rows.name: the 'wan' contraction neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'wan'/'Wan' when it's a contraction for 'wanna' in informal quoted speech.

rows.name: anxious reply normalizer
rows.one: Fires negatively at the start of empathetic assistant replies to anxious user messages.

rows.name: emotional filler suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation and function words like 'that' and ''s' within emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: Python import comma and decimal dot
rows.one: Fires negatively on commas and dots in import statements (e.g., 'models,'), and positively on decimal points in numbers (e.g., '2.0').

rows.name: the 'That's' enthusiasm dampener
rows.one: Strongly negative on 'That' followed by a copula or verb ('s', 'is', 'was', 'been', 'sounds') at the start of assistant replies to positive/neutral emotional user messages.

rows.name: the emotional assistant-start neuron
rows.one: Fires at the assistant turn start token after emotional user messages, particularly about pet death or illness.

rows.name: the HTML attribute and narrative quote neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'text' inside HTML type attributes; fires negatively on 'man' after a closing quote in narrative and on 'for' in formal list headings.

rows.name: L17/N4033
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the 'how is/are' question neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'is', 'are', or 'were' immediately after 'how' in question contexts.

rows.name: the emotional 'I' and relaxation 'to' suppressor
rows.one: Strongly negative on 'I' at assistant reply start after emotional user statements, and on 'to' after relaxation verbs in guided instructions.

rows.name: empathetic 'It' starter
rows.one: Fires on 'It' starting assistant replies to emotional user messages, especially those expressing personal distress.

rows.name: the oh-well and award-of neuron
rows.one: Fires on emotional interjections like 'Oh', 'Well' at the start of assistant replies and on 'of' in award/part-of phrases.

rows.name: code punctuation and 'you were able'
rows.one: Fires negatively on specific code punctuation tokens like '_[' and ' <' in code, and positively on the phrase 'you were able' in empathetic chat replies.

rows.name: assistant start and sentence end
rows.one: Fires on the first token of an assistant reply and on narrative periods; negative on common words in procedural text.

rows.name: the 'the trigger' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'trigger' after a determiner ('the', 'a'), particularly in narrative action contexts.

rows.name: the 'to explore' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on ' explore' after 'to' in plain text, but not in chat replies.

rows.name: the emotional 'you' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'you' at the start of emotional assistant replies to personal distress.

rows.name: the 'civil/rights' token neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on the token 'civil' and 'competitive', negatively on 'rights' and 'Le', but not on synonyms or similar words.

rows.name: L29/N7678
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the definite collection neuron
rows.one: Fires positively after 'the' before a singular noun denoting a definite whole or collection, and negatively after 'the' before measure phrases in assistant replies.

rows.name: the hyphenated-compound neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on hyphenated or compound words (like '-but', 'thing', 'butt') and negatively on tokens that are suffixes or parts of longer words (like 'scala', 'out', 'more').

rows.name: chat empathy 'That' starter
rows.one: Fires on the first token of an assistant reply that starts with 'That' in response to an emotional user message.

rows.name: the empathetic reply 'I'
rows.one: Fires at the token 'I' at the beginning of assistant replies in emotional chats, especially when starting empathetic phrases.

rows.name: emotional 'I' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively at assistant reply start 'I' after emotional user messages, not after neutral ones.

rows.name: factual list vs emotional text
rows.one: Fires positively on tokens in factual lists or structured descriptions, negatively on tokens in emotional or informal text.

rows.name: the 'hope not all' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'all' in emotional assistant replies that express hope about limiting a negative outcome.

rows.name: possessive-abstract-noun-verb neuron
rows.one: Fires on abstract nouns like 'confidence' or 'expertise' after a possessive or 'the' when immediately followed by a verb of change or state.

rows.name: the empathetic question 'you' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'you' in emotional assistant replies after question starters like 'Have you' or 'Did you', but not in plain text or other contexts.

rows.name: L23/N49
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: dot-attribute and narrative 'g'
rows.one: Fires positively on code tokens like '.objects' after a dot; fires negatively on the letter 'g' starting a word in narrative prose.

rows.name: the emotional/narrative 'be' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'be' verbs (especially 'am', 'was', 'being', 'been') in emotional or narrative contexts, not limited to first-person.
rows.sx: first-person verb but also other forms

rows.name: the user-to-assistant transition neuron
rows.one: Fires on the newline token right after the user message end tag in a chat template.

rows.name: the 'PLEASE' reply neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'PLEASE' (all caps) at the start of an assistant reply to an urgent user message.

rows.name: sentimental list limiter
rows.one: Strongly negative on the final noun in a list of pleasant sensory or emotional items in chat responses, especially when the list lacks a conjunction.

rows.name: the empathetic 'is' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'is' at the start of empathetic assistant replies to emotional complaints when the reply begins with 'That is'; fires positively on 'pre' in 'pre-established' and 'no'/'not' in emotional text.

rows.name: medical eradication suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'out' after 'wipe' in medical eradication contexts, and on related words like 'trigger' and 'swelling'.

rows.name: the uppercase 'Int' and formal comma neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the token 'Int' or 'INT', especially after newline, and on commas in formal lists.

rows.name: assistant reply opener punctuation
rows.one: Fires on punctuation marks (like ", .) that appear immediately after the assistant header and newlines in a chat response, but only in specific contexts.

rows.name: the list-continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on short common words like 'a', 'in', 'at', 'some', 'and' that appear after a list or narrative continuation, often following a comma.

rows.name: the 'That is/add' reply neuron
rows.one: Fires at assistant reply start with 'That' + copula, and on 'add' after 'to' in infinitives.

rows.name: the 'the most' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'the' when it immediately precedes 'most' as a superlative determiner/adjective in a noun phrase, but only in certain contexts.

rows.name: mid-word-continuation
rows.one: Fires on tokens that continue a word or phrase after a comma or mid-thought, especially word prefixes.

rows.name: the emotional intensifier-adjective neuron
rows.one: Fires on adjectives following intensifiers like 'so' or 'very' in emotional contexts, and on some standalone emotional adjectives.

rows.name: punctuation-h token neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on the token 'h' when it follows punctuation like '-', '.', '('; fires negatively on the token ' h' at word start in some contexts.

rows.name: the emotional positive-description neuron
rows.one: Fires on positive adjectives after 'is'/'was' in emotional/narrative contexts and on sentence-starting 'You'/'They' before positive descriptions.
rows.sx: contexts, but also 'you' 'they' at start of sentences

rows.name: empathetic 'That's' suppressor / 'like a' detector
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'That's' in empathetic assistant replies and positively on ' a' after 'like' in emotional/narrative text.

rows.name: the Portuguese 'de' and noun fragment neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on tokens like 'érie' and 'u' in Portuguese proper nouns, and negatively on 'de' in Portuguese/Spanish text.

rows.name: positive emotional reply dampener
rows.one: Fires negatively on the first word of assistant replies starting with 'That' or 'It' after positive emotional user messages.

rows.name: the Chinese name character neuron
rows.one: Fires on a Hanzi token that is part of a name, immediately after a space or punctuation following a Latin-script name.

rows.name: the 'so/that' emotional reply neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens in assistant replies that follow emotional intensifiers like 'so' or 'that' in empathetic responses to user stories.

rows.name: the food-list and emotional-reply neuron
rows.one: Fires on specific food/health items in lists and at assistant reply starts after emotional user messages; negative on self-improvement verbs in emotional user text.

rows.name: emotional reply end punctuation
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation ('.', '\n\n') that ends an assistant reply, particularly after emotional user messages.

rows.name: the abstract elaboration suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on abstract nouns after 'the' when they are elaborated by subsequent modifiers in factual contexts.

rows.name: the assistant-continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that continue an assistant reply in chat, especially after newlines or sentence starts.

rows.name: the empathetic reply punctuation
rows.one: Fires positively at punctuation starting assistant replies after emotional user messages, and negatively at single quotes in narrative and at spaces in dismissive replies.

rows.name: the factual-start suppressor neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively at the first word of an assistant reply that starts a factual statement or instruction.

rows.name: assistant 'I' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'I', 'my', 'am' at the start of emotional assistant replies; positively on chat turn boundaries and some taboo words.

rows.name: the empathetic 'must be' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'be' or 'was' after intensifiers like 'must', 'so', 'too', 'both' and before emotional adjectives, primarily in empathetic chat responses.

rows.name: the 'chia' and 'grime' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'ch' at the start of 'chia' or 'choking' and on 'gr' at the start of 'grime' or 'grease', but not on other words with the same starting tokens.

rows.name: L26/N7838
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: the '20' year-digit neuron
rows.one: Strongly negative on digit '0' immediately after a '2' in year or copyright contexts; positive on whitespace in code.

rows.name: the 'the thought' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'thought' when it follows a negative or emotionally charged clause.

rows.name: the 'That is' affirmation neuron
rows.one: Fires on auxiliary verbs at the start of assistant replies that affirm or empathize with an emotional user statement.

rows.name: the "I totally get it" neuron
rows.one: Fires on informal emphatic agreement words and 'not' contractions in emotional assistant responses.

rows.name: the 'so ___' empathy neuron
rows.one: Fires on words like 'hard', 'scary', 'tired' immediately after 'so' in emotional chat responses.

rows.name: comparative 'than' and list prepositions
rows.one: Fires positively on 'than' after comparatives; fires negatively on list-introducing prepositions 'from' and 'for'.

rows.name: the assistant-reply-start neuron
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies in chat, especially after emotional prompts or when the reply begins with words like 'so' or 'first'.

rows.name: the assistant 'so' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'so' in assistant replies after an emotional exclamation ('Oh my', 'Wow', 'That') responding to a positive/empathetic user message.

rows.name: the "informal punctuation" neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation marks (like periods, commas) and spacing tokens in informal or emotional text contexts.

rows.name: the 'y o' list neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'o' after 'y' or 'and' in list-like or continuation contexts, especially in scientific/narrative text.

rows.name: technical punctuation follower
rows.one: Fires on digits, 'A', and dash after punctuation in temperature, title, and code contexts; suppresses mid-number and phrase continuations.

rows.name: the empathetic reply starter
rows.one: Activates at the start of assistant replies, particularly after emotional user messages, on common reply-opening words and punctuation.

rows.name: collection noun suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on nouns like 'collection', 'series', 'group' after 'a' in list-like contexts.

rows.name: assistant 'a/of ___' intensity
rows.one: Fires on degree adjectives following 'a' or 'of' in assistant chat replies, with sign possibly influenced by emotional vs factual context.

rows.name: the script colon-newline-parenthesis neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on colons followed by a newline and an opening parenthesis, specifically in script dialogue tags.

rows.name: the 'Oh, I' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'I' at the start of assistant replies in emotional chats when the reply begins with an emotional interjection like 'Oh'.

rows.name: the capital-in-sequence neuron
rows.one: Fires on capital 'K' or 'C' when preceded by another capital letter or abbreviation, often in technical names or acronyms.
rows.sx: k c after a preceding abbreviation

rows.name: the 'was lacking' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'was' after a phrase indicating insufficiency or a partial state.

rows.name: the 'my injury' chat neuron
rows.one: Fires on medical nouns like 'injury' or 'shoulder' after 'my' or 'his' in emotional chat, especially at assistant reply starts.

rows.name: the 'It can' empathy suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'can', 'is', 'be' etc. after 'It' at the start of an assistant's emotional chat reply.

rows.name: the empathetic reply pronoun neuron
rows.one: Fires on first-person pronouns at the start of assistant replies to emotional user messages.
rows.sx: after lead-in, especially in chat responses

rows.name: emotional reply starter
rows.one: Fires at the beginning of assistant replies in emotional chat, but only for specific opening tokens like 'It', 'Do you', 'I've'.

rows.name: assistant reply quote starter
rows.one: Fires on an opening double quote after a newline and space in assistant chat responses.

rows.name: technical filler suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on generic words in technical/instructional contexts and positively at period-newline within code blocks.

rows.name: license-3 and abstract-of
rows.one: Fires on '3' in software license strings and sometimes on abstract nouns after 'of' in assistant replies.

rows.name: the factual post-punctuation capital neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the first token of a capitalized word after a comma or period in factual/technical text, especially short prefixes like 'Sp', 'Sh', 'St'.

rows.name: the consoling 'It' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'It' at the start of an assistant reply after a user shares a personal mishap or minor distress.

rows.name: the 'no' and 'without a' neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly positive on 'no' within idiomatic negative phrases and on 'a' after 'without'; fires negative on sentence-initial 'No'.

rows.name: the "after-strong-claim" neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on tokens that start a new clause after an extreme or absolute claim, and negatively on tokens that extend a negative or constrained description.

rows.name: empathetic opener
rows.one: Fires on 'How' and 'Well' at the start of assistant replies to negative emotional user messages.

rows.name: the 'revealed object' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on nouns like 'note', 'liar', 'had', ''M' when they follow discovery verbs in assistant replies, not in plain text.

rows.name: the 'so ___' empathy reply neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word after 'so' when used as an intensifier at the start of an assistant's empathetic chat reply.

rows.name: the 'natural/prevented' disaster neuron
rows.one: Fires on the tokens 'natural' and 'prevented' in contexts about disasters or hazards.

rows.name: the assistant exclamation neuron
rows.one: Activates on punctuation and emotional tokens at the start of assistant replies in chat, and suppresses common words in procedural text.

rows.name: the 'adm' after comma neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly on the token 'adm' in 'admiring'/'admire' when it follows a comma and a space.

rows.name: the line-start emotional interjection neuron
rows.one: Fires at emotional interjections like 'Wow', 'Oh', 'Aww' when they appear at the start of a line (after a newline).

rows.name: emotional text and code formatting neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on tokens in emotionally charged text or narrative, and negatively on specific code tokens like 'suppress' and newline commas.

rows.name: list-punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation marks (., ,, :, =) that follow a list item or step number in code/instructional contexts, and negatively on tokens like 'in' or ',' after a closing quote.

rows.name: the chat-affirm and list-suppress neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on affirming words in assistant replies to emotional users, and negatively on tokens starting numbered list items.
rows.sx: positive: chat reply affirmation; negative: item start

rows.name: the "careful on" neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'careful' and 'on' after warnings or cautionary statements.

rows.name: the therapy context neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens in therapeutic or mental health support contexts, including 'hyp' (hypnosis), 'to' (going to therapy), and 'team' (team-building), but not exclusively on the word 'therapy'.

rows.name: the emotional 'I' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'I' at the start of empathetic assistant replies to highly emotional user messages, and positively on 'must' in speculative statements about the user's experience in chat.

rows.name: the empathetic reply starter
rows.one: Fires on the first token of an assistant's reply in emotional chat, especially after the chat template; suppresses equals signs and determiners elsewhere.

rows.name: the assistant 'depends' suppressor
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the word 'depends' when it appears at the beginning of an assistant's reply in chat.

rows.name: it-is / does-not neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'is' after 'It' in chat replies, and negatively on 'not' after 'does' in chat replies.

rows.name: the specific-trigger 'of' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the preposition 'of' after specific preceding tokens like 'capable', 'Spirit', or '-based', and negatively after tokens like 'Register'.

rows.name: emotional echo noun
rows.one: Fires on specific nouns like 'walmart', 'suit', 'cheap', 'programming' in assistant replies after user emotional statements.

rows.name: assistant template token
rows.one: Fires on the 'assistant' token in the chat template after a turn end (<|im_end|>), regardless of preceding content.

rows.name: the punctuation-continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on whitespace after line breaks in code; fires negatively on word fragments after punctuation in prose.

rows.name: the technical-list-item neuron
rows.one: Fires on nouns after 'in' or 'of' in technical or formal enumerations, especially when part of a continuing list.

rows.name: the lowercase-fragment suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens consisting of a space plus a lowercase letter fragment (e.g., ' la', ' po', ' pr'), often in multi-word phrases.

rows.name: the 'after uncertainty' neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that start a new clause or sentence after expressions of uncertainty, emotional disclosure, or dialogue.

rows.name: the assistant-reply interjection neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens 'Oh', 'Aw', 'Ah' at the very start of an assistant reply in chat, not in narrative or mid-sentence.

rows.name: the absorption vs. mental entry neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on verbs of physical absorption ('soaking', 'sink') and negatively on verbs of entering a mental/emotional state ('lost', 'gets') in continuous/progressive contexts.

rows.name: the 'after-article' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token following 'the', 'a', or 'an', particularly when it's part of a noun.

rows.name: the aesthetic list neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on aesthetic adjectives and list item markers in enumerated lists.

rows.name: the 'indefinite subject predicate' neuron
rows.one: Fires on verbs and subordinating conjunctions that follow an indefinite noun phrase subject and start its predicate.

rows.name: the "can be for" neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that introduce a list or variety after a modal verb like 'can' or 'could'.

rows.name: the short-phrase closer
rows.one: Fires on punctuation that terminates a brief phrase, often after numbers or emotional chat replies.

rows.name: emotional 'I' punctuation suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation tokens (., !, but) immediately after 'I' in emotional assistant replies, and positively on 'a' and 'and' in poetic or list contexts.

rows.name: copyright 'rights reserved' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'rights' in the phrase 'All rights reserved.' within copyright headers, and negatively on 'the' in specific license boilerplate.

rows.name: the structured ' n' neuron
rows.one:
Fires on ' n' after specific punctuation and whitespace patterns like '
 
 - 
 
 `` I do' in narrative or emotional text.

rows.name: geographical coordinate preposition neuron
rows.one: Fires on coordinating conjunctions and prepositions that follow a directional 'to' phrase in parallel geographical boundary lists.

rows.name: the narrative boundary noun neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on common nouns immediately before punctuation in narrative or descriptive text.

rows.name: the 'Oh' after distress neuron
rows.one: Fires on discourse markers like 'Oh', 'Now', 'Well', 'Yeah' at the start of an assistant reply, but primarily when the user's preceding statement is negative or distressing.

rows.name: the repetitive list neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on repeated tokens in a list of similar items, like 'La' in a surname series.

rows.name: the hesitant sympathy interjection neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'Uh' and 'Gee' at the start of assistant replies after negative emotional user messages, and on commas after interjections in emotional text.
rows.sx: message, but only for certain contexts

rows.name: the 'assistant lol' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on informal laughter tokens ('lol', 'haha', ':-)') in assistant replies, and on emotional punctuation in narratives.

rows.name: the empathetic 'would' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the word 'would' after empathetic openings in emotional assistant replies.

rows.name: the 'b' letter neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token 'b' (or 'B', '-B', '(b', '.et') when it appears as a standalone letter after punctuation or a space, but not in list contexts.

rows.name: the assistant-reply starter
rows.one: Fires positively on the newline after '<|im_start|>assistant' in chat prompts and on some formatting tokens like '.br' and '||'.

rows.name: the code/web list continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that continue a line after a bullet '*' or a numbered step in code or web text, not in plain prose.

rows.name: the emotional reply period neuron
rows.one: Fires on the period ending an assistant's empathetic reply that starts with 'That's' or 'Wow' and contains a strong emotional adjective.

rows.name: the 'get to / can't to' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on 'to' after positive opportunity verbs ('get to', 'got to'); fires negatively on 'to' after inability verbs ('didn't get to', 'can not really').

rows.name: the conversational starter neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that begin conversational turns or emotional expressions, including 'I feel', 'Yeah', and punctuation after colons or newlines in chat.

rows.name: the my-body neuron
rows.one: Activates negative on 'my' when it immediately precedes a body-part or emotional reaction word in emotional contexts.

rows.name: infinitive 'to ___'
rows.one: Fires on the word after 'to' when 'to' introduces an infinitive verb phrase, particularly in instructional or advice text.

rows.name: L27/N6248
rows.one: No description yet.

rows.name: emotional turn delimiter neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on <|im_start|> tokens after emotional user messages in chat, but not reliably.

rows.name: factual capital and chat newline
rows.one: Fires positively on capital letters after spaces in factual list contexts and negatively on newlines after the assistant header in chat prompts.

rows.name: quote-start suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively at the first token of a quoted sentence after a dialogue tag, and positively at newlines in chat prompts.

rows.name: narrative preposition suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on prepositions like 'in', 'by', 'to', 'and' in narrative or emotional text.

rows.name: the assistant-list colon neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on colon ':' starting a numbered list item in assistant replies; fires negatively on 'on', 'than', 'only', 'no' in emotional/chat contexts.

rows.name: the 'you' positive, 'grateful for' negative neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on pronouns like 'you' in emotional support responses and negatively on 'for' in gratitude phrases like 'grateful for'.

rows.name: the assistant list-number neuron
rows.one: Fires on list item starters ('1', 'Firstly') only at the start of an assistant chat response line; negative on code zero and random punctuation in non-chat.

rows.name: the 'Yes indeed' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively at 'indeed' starting assistant replies (especially after 'Yes') and at digits in code; positively at punctuation ending emotional replies.

rows.name: the sentimental descriptive noun neuron
rows.one: Fires at the start of descriptive noun phrases (often after 'a'/'the') in emotional chat assistant replies, particularly for sentimental or beautiful items.

rows.name: the 'Japanese word continuation' neuron
rows.one: Fires on tokens that continue a Japanese or Chinese word after a preceding token from the same word, like 'uk' after 'Ts', 'is' after 'haiku', and 'sob' after 'soba'.

rows.name: the 'change to' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'to' after nouns like 'change', 'comment', 'move' in descriptive clauses, and on list dashes '-', but suppresses on 'with' and 'by' in similar contexts.

rows.name: the 'I don't have' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on verbs like 'have', 'know', 'help' after 'I don't' or 'I can't' in assistant replies.

rows.name: code/doc keyword starter
rows.one: Fires on the first token of specific code keywords (e.g., 'def', 'Con', '/con') and on 'needs' after 'documentation'; negative on some code/formatting tokens (e.g., 'max', '-').

rows.name: the 'pretty ___' neuron
rows.one: Fires on generic adjectives like 'cheap', 'white', 'people', 'guess' when they follow an intensifier such as 'pretty' or 'so' in the same clause.

rows.name: emotional 'If/What' start neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively at the start of emotional assistant replies when they begin with 'If' or 'What', but not for other empathetic openings.

rows.name: post-list assistant start
rows.one: Fires on the first token of an assistant reply after a user message ending with a newline, and negatively on '1' starting a numbered list after a colon and newline.

rows.name: the emotional reply period suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on periods ending short, empathetic assistant replies in emotional chat.

rows.name: the factual-assistant newline neuron
rows.one: Fires on the newline token after the assistant tag in chat prompts with factual user messages.

rows.name: the 'that' continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on discourse markers like 'that', 'their', 'however' when they continue or elaborate a statement, and negatively when they introduce a contrast or negative turn.

rows.name: the colon-list follower
rows.one: Fires on tokens that follow a colon in factual lists or code imports.

rows.name: the digit-in-sequence neuron
rows.one: Fires on digits in numeric sequences, especially after '9' or before punctuation; strongly negative on '6' in code-like strings.

rows.name: the emotional reply-start space neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first space token after a newline at the start of an assistant reply, but only when the user message is emotional and the assistant's reply begins with a specific emotional or supportive phrase.

rows.name: assistant reply 'the' abstract noun
rows.one: Fires on abstract nouns after 'the' at the start of assistant replies.

rows.name: the structured-uppercase neuron
rows.one: Fires on uppercase letters after punctuation in lists/code; strongly negative on 'rep' and assistant reply boundaries in emotional chat.

rows.name: emotional post-punctuation start
rows.one: Fires on the first token after punctuation that begins a personal or emotional continuation, especially in chat or narrative.

rows.name: the ' X' and 'so that' neuron
rows.one: Fires on uppercase X after space; fires negatively on 'that' after 'so'.

rows.name: negative 'c' before vowel start
rows.one: Fires negatively on token 'c' or 'C' after a space when the next token starts with a vowel (like ' ur', ' ob', ' ra'), but not before consonants or in isolated letters.

rows.name: the post-formal-punctuation neuron
rows.one: Strongly positive after periods/colons following numbers/abbreviations in factual text; strongly negative after emotional commas in chat.

rows.name: the 'your' after 'Very nice!' neuron
rows.one: Fires negative at 'your' in assistant replies starting with 'Very nice!' after a positive emotional user message.

rows.name: name 'av' and code '('
rows.one: Fires negatively on the token 'av' in names like 'Schiavone' and on '(' after 'if' in code; positive triggers are less clear.

rows.name: the 'tag-question' neuron
rows.one: Fires on tag questions ('right?') and conversational punctuation in assistant replies following certain phrases.

rows.name: capital E after break neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the token 'E' when it appears as a standalone capital letter after whitespace or punctuation.

rows.name: the split-word 'ra' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on the token 'ra' when it follows 'Fab' in a copyright line, and possibly on other second parts of split words in code.

rows.name: the social awkwardness neuron
rows.one: Fires on words like 'awkward', 'uncomfortable', 'look' (as in 'make oneself look'), and 'pastor' in contexts of social evaluation or discomfort, often after intensifiers.

rows.name: emotional feeling and hard suppressor
rows.one: Fires positively on 'felt'/'feeling' in emotional assistant replies, and negatively on the word 'hard'.

rows.name: chat 'be feeling like' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'like' after 'be' or 'feeling' in emotional assistant replies, especially after 'must be' or 'gotta be'.

rows.name: the 'historical date newline' neuron
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on a newline token that follows a closing punctuation mark after a date in parentheses or similar specific endings.

rows.name: the 'you fucking' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on swear words and insults when they are part of a second-person attack ('you fucking idiot', 'go fuck yourself'), not when describing situations or third parties.

rows.name: assistant-reply-start newline
rows.one: Fires on the newline token right after <|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant in chat prompts, marking the start of the assistant's response.

rows.name: the emotional-casual-reply neuron
rows.one: Strongly negative at the beginning of assistant replies that start with informal words like 'Hey' or 'Our', but only when the user's message is emotional.

rows.name: the 'had' continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on words following 'had' or 'have' in emotional or narrative contexts, continuing a past event description.

rows.name: newline-start token neuron
rows.one: Activates on tokens that start after a newline or chat turn, especially proper names, 'go', and numerical punctuation.

rows.name: assistant reply start
rows.one: Fires positively on the whitespace token right after '' in assistant replies, and negatively on some early content words.

rows.name: the "empathetic I/Sorry/?" neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first word of an assistant reply after an emotional user message, but only for specific words like 'I', 'Sorry', 'Wow', and '?'.

rows.name: the 'so driven' neuron
rows.one: Fires on forceful verbs or participles immediately following intensifiers like 'so' or 'very'.

rows.name: the 'yes after no' neuron
rows.one: Activates on affirmative words like 'will', 'do', 'Yes' that follow a negation or contrast in emotional/narrative text, but not in neutral assistant replies.

rows.name: the 'Oh, ...' continuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first few tokens of an assistant reply after an empathetic opener like 'Oh' or 'I'm' in emotional chat.

rows.name: assistant-start and medical-term suppressor
rows.one: Fires positively at newline after 'assistant' in chat, and negatively on words like 'called', 'am', 'moderate' in medical/technical contexts.

rows.name: the crying/tears neuron
rows.one: Fires on capitalized 'Tears' in emotional narratives, and negatively on words like 'sob', 's', 'her' in specific grammatical contexts of crying.

rows.name: the "emotional reply opener" neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first token of an assistant reply in emotional chat contexts, often words like 'do', 'Yeah', 'but', 'These'.

rows.name: emotional 'I am' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'I am' or 'I'm' at the start of assistant replies to emotional user messages.

rows.name: excitement 'up' suppressor
rows.one: Fires strongly negative on the token ' up' after phrases like 'hardly contain my excitement'.

rows.name: emotional generic opener suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on generic assistant reply starters ('I', 'One', 'It', etc.) after emotional user messages.

rows.name: structured text capitalized term neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on capitalized words like 'Established', 'Administrator', 'key' in structured contexts (code, lists), and positively on 'The' after a newline in code/docstrings.

rows.name: dramatic 'would not be'
rows.one: Fires negatively on 'be' in the phrase 'would not be' within high-stakes narrative conclusions.

rows.name: the chat-list punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation (comma, colon) after a heading phrase in chat contexts, especially at the start of assistant replies.

rows.name: the 'bad news' reply start neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively at the first token of an assistant reply after a negative user message.

rows.name: the list-number and 'don' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on list numbers like '1.' at line start and on conversational 'don' in contractions.

rows.name: the 'truly a' and 'took on lives' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'a' after 'truly' in emotional assistant replies, and on 'lives' after 'took on' in narratives.

rows.name: the ' D' after break neuron
rows.one: Fires on the token ' D' after punctuation or newlines in specific contexts like 'Mosquito D', but not on 'State' or 'Fib'.
rows.sx: capital d space and punctuation, especially

rows.name: assistant reply opener
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies in chat, especially after emotional user messages, on tokens that begin polite or empathetic statements.

rows.name: negative adjectives / list separator
rows.one: Fires negatively on specific adjectives like 'bad', 'terrible', 'nice', 'absolute', 'state'; fires positively on newline after a period ending a list item.

rows.name: place-name hyphen and chat start neuron
rows.one: Strongly negative on hyphenated place-name fragments and 'the' in code licenses; positive on chat start tokens after emotional user messages.

rows.name: empathetic 'I' after 'Oh'
rows.one: Fires on 'I' in assistant replies starting with 'Oh' or 'Wow' to negative user messages; negative on 'crying' in sad narratives.

rows.name: emotional 'It was' dampener
rows.one: Fires negatively at 'was' in assistant replies starting with 'It was' after emotional user messages, but not in neutral or factual contexts.

rows.name: the "but after negation" neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on contrastive conjunctions 'but' or 'Or' when they follow a negative or limiting statement.

rows.name: the 'newline-capital/punctuation' neuron
rows.one: Fires on punctuation-initial or capital-initial tokens after a newline in structured contexts, and is negative on certain library name fragments in headers.

rows.name: the "comma before which" neuron
rows.one: Fires on a comma that separates a noun phrase from a following relative clause beginning with 'which'.

rows.name: the 'name G' neuron
rows.one: Fires on uppercase 'G' after a space when preceded by a proper name, negatively on hyphenated '-G' and code 'Do'.

rows.name: emotional article suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on articles 'the'/'a' when they follow an emotional or poetic phrase, especially in chat and narrative.

rows.name: the 'David X' neuron
rows.one: Fires on the first token of a capitalized word after 'David', 'your', or 'by'.

rows.name: the 'punctuation-space' neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on words after punctuation and a space, and negatively on tokens that continue without a space or punctuation.

rows.name: the abstract noun suppressor / emotional chat closer
rows.one: Fires negatively on plural abstract nouns in formal prose and positively on punctuation and 'hope' in emotional chat assistant replies.

rows.name: the 'It' statement starter
rows.one: Fires on 'It' at the start of assistant replies after emotional messages and on 'It' introducing generic statements ('It is...', 'It's...') in advice or explanatory contexts.
rows.sx: reply with user message, but also some non-chat contexts

rows.name: empathetic reply comma suppressor
rows.one: Strongly negative on commas after empathetic or exclamatory chat response openers in emotional conversations.

rows.name: the 'emotional reply start' neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively at the start of assistant replies in emotional chats, with varying strength depending on the opening word.

rows.name: the emotional reply starter
rows.one: Fires at the start of assistant replies in emotional chats, especially on 'What' and 'You', and negatively on 'must' within those replies.

rows.name: the emotional 'part of' suppressor
rows.one: Strongly negative on 'part' in 'a part of' within emotional assistant replies, and on punctuation after emotional statements.

rows.name: the 'so ___' effort neuron
rows.one: Fires on verbs like 'put', 'have', 'can', 'find' that follow the word 'so' in emotional or reflective text.

rows.name: a-little-punctuation neuron
rows.one: Fires negatively on punctuation tokens that immediately follow 'a little' or 'little bit' in assistant chat replies.

rows.name: the emotional clause comma neuron
rows.one: Fires on commas after short emotional or conditional clauses, and negatively on commas after factual lists.

rows.name: emotional 'I' starter
rows.one: Fires at 'I' (and sometimes 'you') after a boundary when the preceding text is emotional; strongly suppresses 'caught' in formal prose.

rows.name: emotional reply newline
rows.one: Fires on newline after <|im_start|>assistant in emotional chat prompts, and on 'Air' in factual contexts.

rows.name: pain-change object
rows.one: Fires negatively on pain/pleasure nouns after change verbs like 'increase' or 'decrease'.

rows.name: assistant reply starter
rows.one: Fires negatively on tokens that begin an assistant reply in chat (newlines after header, dialogue starters) and positively on some words inside poetic continuations.

rows.name: the scattered interjection neuron
rows.one: Fires on casual interjections in chat replies and also on various punctuation and letter sequences in other contexts.

rows.name: the bibliography proper name neuron
rows.one: Fires on capitalized proper names after punctuation in structured metadata lines like bibliographies.

rows.name: emotional reply starter
rows.one: Fires on the first token of an assistant reply after an emotional user message, especially discourse markers.

rows.name: assistant definition 'is'
rows.one: Fires on 'is' early in assistant replies when it follows a short subject phrase, often in definitions.

rows.name: the 'assistant-verb-preposition' neuron
rows.one: Fires on prepositions after verbs in assistant factual replies, especially about providing or aiding, and on 'the' after 'above' in noun phrases.

rows.name: the "bring your attention" neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'your attention' or 'your mind' after verbs like 'bring' or 'focus' in instructional contexts.

rows.name: emotional reply start suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on the start of assistant replies to emotional user messages, especially after discourse markers.

rows.name: the 'happens to everyone' neuron
rows.one: Fires on 'happens' at the start of assistant replies that normalize a user's mistake with a universalizing phrase.

rows.name: the assistant-start neuron
rows.one: Fires positively on <|im_start|>assistant in chat, negatively on some proper nouns, digits, and code keywords.

rows.name: assistant reply newline
rows.one: Fires on the newline token after the assistant tag in a chat prompt.

rows.name: the "pre-contrast" neuron
rows.one: Fires on negation or contrast words that immediately precede a contrasting or elaborating clause.

rows.name: slash-follower community name
rows.one: Fires on the second character of a community name after a slash in subreddit-like references (e.g., 'r/funny' triggers on 'u' in 'funny').

rows.name: emotional reply and 'Sh' suppressor
rows.one: Fires negatively on emotional chat reply openings like 'Oh' and 'Aw', and on the token 'Sh' at the start of words.
